documents.title: Bee Movie
documents.tagline: Born to bee wild.
documents.overview: Barry B. Benson, a bee who has just graduated from college, is disillusioned at his lone career choice: making honey. On a special trip outside the hive, Barry's life is saved by Vanessa, a florist in New York City. As their relationship blossoms, he discovers humans actually eat honey, and subsequently decides to sue us.
documents.plot:
Barry B. Benson, an idealistic honey bee graduate who can talk to humans, is about to enter the hive's honey-making workforce, Honex Industries, with his best friend, Adam Flayman. Barry is initially excited, but his ambitious, insubordinate attitude emerges upon discovering that his choice of job will never change once picked. Later, the two bees run into a group of Pollen Jocks, bees who collect pollen from flowers outside the hive, and they offer to take Barry with them if he is "bee enough". While on his first pollen-gathering expedition in Manhattan, Barry gets lost in the rain, and ends up in the apartment of a human florist named Vanessa Bloome. Upon noticing Barry, Vanessa's boyfriend Ken attempts to kill him, but Vanessa gently catches and releases Barry outside, saving his life.
Barry later returns to express his gratitude to Vanessa, breaking the sacred law that bees are not to communicate with humans. Barry and Vanessa develop a close friendship, bordering on attraction, and spend time together. When he and Vanessa are in a grocery store, Barry discovers that the humans have been stealing and eating the bees' honey for centuries. He decides to journey to Honey Farms, which supplies the grocery store with its honey. Incredulous at the poor treatment of the bees in the hives, including the use of bee smokers to incapacitate colonies, Barry decides to sue the human race to put an end to exploitation of the bees, with Vanessa agreeing to help.
Barry's mission attracts wide attention from bees and humans alike, with countless spectators attending the trial. Although Barry is up against tough defense attorney Layton T. Montgomery, the trial's first day goes well. That evening, Barry is having dinner with Vanessa when Ken shows up. Vanessa leaves the room, and Ken expresses to Barry that he hates the pair spending time together. When Barry leaves to use the restroom, Ken ambushes and attempts to murder him, only for Vanessa to intervene and break up with Ken. The second day at the trial, Montgomery unleashes an unrepentant character assassination against the bees, leading a deeply offended Adam to sting him. Montgomery immediately exaggerates the stinging to make himself seem the victim of an assault while simultaneously tarnishing Adam. Adam's actions jeopardize the bees' credibility and his life, though he recovers in a hospital with a small, plastic sword as a replacement stinger. The third day, Barry wins the trial by exposing the jury to the torturous treatment of bees, preventing humans from stealing honey from bees ever again. Having lost the trial, Montgomery cryptically warns Barry that a negative shift of nature is imminent.
Human-obtained honey being returned in overload to the hives leads to Honex stopping honey production and all bees, including the vitally important Pollen Jocks, put out of a job, and all the world's flowers begin to die out without any pollination.

documents.title: Luther
documents.tagline: Rebel. Genius. Liberator.
documents.overview: During the early 16th Century idealistic German monk Martin Luther, disgusted by the materialism in the church, begins the dialogue that will lead to the Protestant Reformation.
documents.plot: During the early 16th century, idealistic German monk Martin Luther, disgusted by the materialism in the church, begins the dialogue that will lead to the Protestant Reformation.

documents.title: Control
documents.tagline: He had the spirit, but lost the feeling.
documents.overview: The story of Joy Division’s lead singer Ian Curtis, from his schoolboy days in 1973 to his suicide on the eve of the band's first American tour in 1980.
documents.plot:
Control is a 2007 British biographical film about Ian Curtis, the singer of the late-1970s rock band Joy Division. It was the first feature directed by Anton Corbijn, who had photographed the band during their career, and it was shot in black and white. Matt Greenhalgh wrote the screenplay based on Touching from a Distance, the biography written by Curtis's widow Deborah, who co-produced the film. Sam Riley stars as Ian Curtis, with Samantha Morton as Deborah, Alexandra Maria Lara as Annik Honoré, and Joe Anderson and James Anthony Pearson as bandmates.

The film opens in 1975 in Macclesfield, south of Manchester, where the teenage Ian marries his girlfriend Debbie Woodruff. Introverted and drawn to poetry, he finds an outlet when he attends a Sex Pistols concert in 1976 with a group of young men who are forming a band, and he offers to become their singer. The group, first named Warsaw and later Joy Division, slowly gains a following, financing its first EP and catching the attention of television presenter Tony Wilson and manager Rob Gretton. Signed to Wilson's Factory Records, the band records Unknown Pleasures and begins to tour.

While working at an employment office, Ian witnesses a client suffering an epileptic seizure, and soon he is diagnosed with epilepsy himself. The medication he takes affects his moods, and the seizures become increasingly frequent, sometimes striking on stage. At the same time, he becomes a father and begins an affair with Annik Honoré, a Belgian journalist, which leaves him torn between her and Debbie. Exhausted by touring, guilt and illness, and on the eve of the band's first American tour, Curtis takes his own life in May 1980 at the age of 23.

Corbijn's restrained direction and the actors' performances, including the cast playing Joy Division's songs themselves, presented Curtis as a fragile young man rather than a rock icon, while focusing heavily on his marriage.

Control premiered at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival in the Directors' Fortnight, where it won several prizes. Critics were enthusiastic: Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian named it the best film of the year, and Roger Ebert gave it three and a half stars out of four. The film also won multiple British Independent Film Awards, including Best Film.

documents.title: Once
documents.tagline: How often do you find the right person?
documents.overview: A vacuum repairman moonlights as a street musician and hopes for his big break. One day a Czech immigrant, who earns a living selling flowers, approaches him with the news that she is also an aspiring singer-songwriter. The pair decide to collaborate, and the songs that they compose reflect the story of their blossoming love.
documents.plot:
A thirty-something busker (Guy) performs with his guitar on Grafton Street, Dublin, but his performance is interrupted when he chases a man who steals his money. Lured by his music, a 19-year-old Czech magazine and flower seller (Girl) talks to him about his songs. Delighted to learn that he repairs hoovers, Girl asks Guy to fix hers. The next day Girl returns with her broken vacuum and tells him she is also a musician.
At a music store where Girl usually plays piano, Guy teaches her one of his songs ("Falling Slowly"); they sing and play together. He invites her to his father's shop, and on the bus home musically answers Girl's question about what his songs are about: a long-time girlfriend who cheated on him, then left ("Broken Hearted Hoover Fixer Sucker Guy").
At the shop, Guy introduces Girl to his father and takes her to his room, but when he asks her to stay the night, she gets upset and leaves. The next day, they reconcile and spend the week writing, rehearsing and recording songs. Girl writes the lyrics for one of Guy's songs ("If You Want Me"), singing to herself while walking down the street; at a party, people perform impromptu (including "Gold").
Guy works on "Lies", a song about his ex-girlfriend, who moved to London. Girl encourages him to win her back. Invited to her home, he discovers she has a toddler and lives with her mother. Guy decides to move to London, but he wants to record a demo of his songs to take with him and asks Girl to record it with him. They secure a bank loan and reserve time at a recording studio.
Guy learns Girl has a husband in the Czech Republic. When he asks if she still loves her husband, Girl answers in Czech, "Miluju tebe" ("It's you, who I love"), but coyly declines to translate. After recruiting a band with other buskers, they go into the studio to record. They impress Eamon, the jaded studio engineer, with their first song ("When Your Mind's Made Up"). On a break in the early morning, Girl finds a piano in an empty studio and plays Guy one of her own compositions ("The Hill").
After the all-night session wraps up, they walk home. Before they part ways, Girl reveals that she spoke to her husband and he is coming to live with her in Dublin. Guy persuades her to spend his last night in Dublin with him, but she stands him up and he cannot find her to say goodbye before his flight. He plays the demo for his father, who gives him money to help him get settled in London. Before leaving for the airport, Guy buys Girl a piano and makes arrangements for its delivery, then calls his ex-girlfriend, who is happy about his imminent arrival. Girl reunites with her husband in Dublin and plays the piano in their home.

documents.title: Princess of Thieves
documents.tagline: If you thought Robin Hood broke all the rules, wait until you meet his daughter!
documents.overview: Sherwood forest has a courageous new hero - Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood. Possessing the cunning skills of her legendary father and the beauty and intelligence of her mother Maid Marian, Gwyn is anxious to follow in her father's footsteps. King Richard nears death and Robin Hood and his Merry Men are summoned to help bring Richard's son Philip to his rightful place on the throne before the evil Prince John can assume power. Robin Hood's life and that of the future King of England soon lies in Gwyn's hands when Robin is captured and sentenced to death.
documents.plot:
Princess of Thieves is a 2001 romantic adventure television film directed by Peter Hewitt and starring Keira Knightley as Gwyn, the daughter of Robin Hood and Maid Marian. Produced by Granada Entertainment USA and filmed in Romania, it co-stars Stuart Wilson as Robin Hood, Stephen Moyer as Prince Philip, Jonathan Hyde as Prince John, Malcolm McDowell as the Sheriff of Nottingham and Del Synnott as Froderick. The story imagines a new chapter in the Robin Hood legend, centered on the outlaw's spirited daughter.

Years after the famous adventures of Robin Hood, Maid Marian has died and Robin spends most of his time away fighting in the Crusades alongside King Richard the Lionheart. His daughter Gwyn has grown up largely without him, becoming an independent and strong-willed young woman with a remarkable talent for archery. Her only close companion is Froderick, a gentle young man studying for the church, who is quietly in love with her. When King Richard dies, Robin returns to England to ensure that the rightful heir takes the throne, but he is captured by his old enemies, the Sheriff of Nottingham and the scheming Prince John, who intends to seize the crown for himself.

Gwyn takes up her father's mission. She must find and protect Prince Philip, King Richard's illegitimate son, who has returned from exile in France to claim the throne but is traveling incognito under the name of his servant, who died protecting him. Gwyn crosses paths with the young man without knowing his true identity, and a romance begins to grow between them. Together they seek out the Merry Men and lead a daring attempt to rescue Robin from imprisonment in the Tower of London and stop Prince John's coronation before England falls into tyranny.

The film presents a family-friendly adventure with a heroine who proves herself the equal of her legendary father, and it was one of Knightley's first leading roles, made shortly before her international breakthrough.

Princess of Thieves premiered on ABC's The Wonderful World of Disney in 2001. Reviews were mixed: Scott Weinberg of eFilmCritic called it an entertaining little movie that bucks the odds, while BeyondHollywood found it aimed squarely at young girls and likely to bore other viewers.

documents.title: Casper's Haunted Christmas
documents.overview: Kibosh, supreme ruler of all ghosts, decrees that casper must scare at least one person before Christmas Day so Casper visits Kriss, Massachusetts where he meets the Jollimore family and sets out to complete his mission. As usual, kindhearted Casper has a ghastky time trying to scare anyone; so The Ghostly Trio, fed up with his goody-boo-shoes behavior, secretly hires Casper's look-alike cousin Spooky to do the job-with hilarious results.
documents.plot: Kibosh, supreme ruler of all ghosts, decrees that casper must scare at least one person before Christmas Day so Casper visits Kriss, Massachusetts where he meets the Jollimore family and sets out to complete his mission. As usual, kindhearted Casper has a ghastky time trying to scare anyone; so The Ghostly Trio, fed up with his goody-boo-shoes behavior, secretly hires Casper's look-alike cousin Spooky to do the job-with hilarious results.

documents.title: Showtime
documents.tagline: Lights. Camera. Aggravation.
documents.overview: A spoof of buddy cop movies where two very different cops are forced to team up on a new reality based T.V. cop show.
documents.plot:
Showtime is a 2002 American buddy cop action comedy film directed by Tom Dey and released by Warner Bros. Pictures. It stars Robert De Niro as a gruff detective and Eddie Murphy as an aspiring actor in uniform, alongside Rene Russo, William Shatner, Pedro Damián and De Niro's daughter Drena De Niro.

Detective Mitch Preston of the Los Angeles Police Department's Central Division shoots a news camera after a botched confrontation with drug dealer Lazy Boy, who escapes using a custom-built armor-piercing gun. The cameraman's network, Maxxis Television, sues the department for $10 million but offers to drop the suit if Mitch stars in its new police reality show, and the captain, eager for good publicity, agrees. His partner on the show is Officer Trey Sellars, a patrolman who keeps failing the detective exam and dreams of acting; Trey even stages a purse snatching to impress producer Chase Renzi, who signs him despite the embarrassing ruse. The producers care little for real police work: they build a set inside the station, give Mitch a Humvee and Trey a Corvette, and hire William Shatner, the former star of T. J. Hooker, to coach them. Trey loves it; Mitch is merely irritated, especially after the show redecorates his home and gives him a retired police dog named Powder.

Mitch keeps investigating the supergun, which arms dealer Caesar Vargas uses to kill Lazy Boy. A ruse by Trey yields Vargas's name, leading to a brawl at his nightclub. Vargas's crew then attacks an armored car, and the ensuing chase ends in a destructive crash, after which the chief cancels the show, suspends Mitch and demotes Trey. Reconciling, the two learn that Vargas plans to sell the weapons at a gun show at the Bonaventure Hotel. Vargas takes Chase hostage, but the partners rescue her; a shot ceiling floods the room from the pool above, washing Vargas out of a window to his death, while Mitch and Trey survive handcuffed together. Trey passes his exam and becomes Mitch's partner as a detective, and the show is revived with two new officers.

Released on March 15, 2002, Showtime received generally negative reviews for its flat humor and failed satire of the buddy cop genre; Rotten Tomatoes reported 25% approval. It grossed about $77.7 million against an $85 million budget, and earned Golden Raspberry nominations for Murphy and for the Murphy-De Niro pairing.

documents.title: Angel Eyes
documents.tagline: The deeper you look, the more you will find.
documents.overview: A story about a seemingly unlikely couple who cross paths under life-threatening circumstances as though they are destined not only to meet but to save each other's lives. Not once, but twice.
documents.plot:
Angel Eyes is a 2001 American romantic drama directed by Luis Mandoki and written by Gerald Di Pego. It stars Jennifer Lopez as Chicago police officer Sharon Pogue and Jim Caviezel as Catch, a mysterious, withdrawn stranger, with Sônia Braga, Terrence Howard and Jeremy Sisto in supporting roles. Marco Beltrami composed the score. The story follows two wounded people whose relationship forces each of them to confront the trauma of the past.

One night, Sharon arrives at the scene of a violent traffic accident and holds the hand of a badly injured man, pleading with him not to give up. A year later, she is estranged from her family because she had her father arrested for beating her mother, something neither he nor her brother has forgiven. Meanwhile, a quiet man known only as Catch wanders the city in a trance-like state, performing small acts of kindness for strangers and neighbors, and seems to be watching Sharon from a distance.

When gunmen open fire on a diner and Sharon gives chase, one of the suspects grabs her gun and is about to shoot her when Catch tackles him and saves her life. The two begin a cautious, intense relationship, but Catch refuses to talk about himself, saying only that he is starting from scratch, and he lives in a nearly empty apartment. One night at a blues club he picks up a trumpet and plays a soulful version of "Nature Boy", and the owner recognizes him as Steve Lambert. Investigating, Sharon discovers that Catch is the man whose hand she held at the accident, a jazz musician whose wife and son were killed in the crash. As she tries to help him face the loss he has blocked from his memory, she must also confront her own painful family history.

The film blends romance with a psychological drama about grief, denial and domestic violence, and about the healing that comes from finally facing pain.

Angel Eyes opened at number four in North America but was a box office bomb, grossing about 29.7 million dollars worldwide against a 38 million dollar budget. Critics were largely unimpressed, giving it 32 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it ultimately a schmaltzy romance, and a Metacritic score of 39, though it earned ALMA Award nominations for Lopez and Mandoki.

documents.title: The Mist
documents.tagline: Belief divides them, mystery surrounds them, but fear changes everything.
documents.overview: After a violent storm, a dense cloud of mist envelops a small Maine town, trapping artist David Drayton and his five-year-old son in a local grocery store with other people. They soon discover that the mist conceals deadly horrors that threaten their lives, and worse, their sanity.
documents.plot:
The Mist is a 2007 American horror film directed by Frank Darabont, based on the novella of the same name by Stephen King. The movie takes place in 1994 and follows a group of people who take refuge in a grocery store after a mysterious mist filled with monstrous creatures envelops their small town.

The story begins with David Drayton (played by Thomas Jane), a divorced father, who is struggling to connect with his son, Billy (played by Nathalie Kelley). As the day progresses, strange occurrences start happening outside, and people begin to disappear. The townspeople soon realize that the mist is filled with monstrous creatures, including giant spiders, snakes, and other terrifying beasts.

As the situation spirals out of control, David finds himself trapped in a grocery store with a small group of survivors, including his son Billy, who has been hiding in the store's basement. The group consists of Kevin (played by Marc Menchaca), a young boy who is initially hesitant to trust anyone; Mrs. Carmody (played by Laurie Holden), a devout Christian woman who believes that God is punishing them for their sins; and Brent Norton (played by Toby Jones), a cynical and world-weary man.

As the group tries to survive, tensions rise as they disagree on how to handle the situation. Mrs. Carmody becomes increasingly fanatical, believing that they must sacrifice some of the survivors in order to appease God. David and Kevin try to reason with her, but she refuses to listen.

Meanwhile, strange events begin to occur within the store itself. The group discovers that the creatures are not just outside, but also inside the store, and that they seem to be attracted to certain individuals. As the days pass, the group's dynamics become increasingly strained, and it becomes clear that some of them may not survive.

As the story unfolds, David and Kevin form a bond as they try to protect each other from the monsters and Mrs. Carmody's fanatical behavior. However, when Brent is killed by one of the creatures, the group's unity begins to break down.

In the end, David makes a desperate decision to escape the store with Billy, but not before realizing that he has lost his son in the chaos. The movie ends with David and Billy walking out into the mist, unsure if they will survive or be consumed by the monsters.

The Mist is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and the breakdown of human relationships under extreme circumstances. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among Stephen King fans and horror enthusiasts.

documents.title: Azumi
documents.tagline: From The Ravages of War Raises An Assassin.
documents.overview: In war-torn Japan, the Tokugawa Shogun, desperate to restore peace to his people, orders the assassination of the hostile warlords. A beautiful young woman is raised from birth with nine other orphans, to become an assassin. Her name is Azumi, the ultimate assassin.
documents.plot: In war-torn Japan, the Tokugawa Shogun, desperate to restore peace to his people, orders the assassination of the hostile warlords. A beautiful young woman is raised from birth with nine other orphans, to become an assassin. Her name is Azumi, the ultimate assassin.

documents.title: Azumi 2: Death or Love
documents.tagline: Love Or Duty... An Assassin Must Choose
documents.overview: Young assassins Azumi and Nagara continue their mission to prevent a civil war. In their hunt for Masayuki Sanada, who is protected by both an army and a dangerous clan, they meet Ginkaku, a person who shows a remarking resemblance with former friend Nachi.
documents.plot:
Azumi 2: Death or Love is a 2005 Japanese jidaigeki action film directed by Shusuke Kaneko and the only sequel to the film Azumi, which was based on the manga series by Yū Koyama. Aya Ueto stars as the young assassin Azumi, with Yuma Ishigaki as her comrade Nagara, Chiaki Kuriyama as the government ninja Kozue, Shun Oguri as the bandit Ginkaku, Kenichi Endō as his brother Kinkaku, Reiko Takashima as Kunio, Kazuki Kitamura as Kanbei Inoue, Tak Sakaguchi as Tsuchigumo and Mikijirō Hira as Sanada Masayuki.

Having carried out a string of assassinations, including the killing of Kiyomasa Kato, Azumi and Nagara are the last survivors of their group and are hunted by ninjas hired by Kanbei Inoue, who seeks to avenge his dead master. While Nagara recovers from his wounds in a temple, Azumi encounters a band of outlaws led by Ginkaku, a young man who strikingly resembles Nachi, the friend she loved and lost. Allied ninjas serving the priest Tenkai, who first ordered the assassins' mission, find the pair, and Azumi and Nagara set out to kill their final target, the warlord Sanada Masayuki, accompanied by a young ninja woman named Kozue. Meanwhile Kanbei raises a large force of mercenaries, ninjas and bandits, among them Ginkaku and Kinkaku. Torn by her feelings for Ginkaku, Azumi parts ways with him, and soon afterwards Nagara announces that he wants to leave the mission and start a new life with Kozue. Continuing alone, Azumi learns that Masayuki's army has left to kill Gessai and races to intervene, facing the giant Roppa of the deadly Uenokagashu ninja clan in a battle that costs the lives of many of Ginkaku's men. Kozue is revealed to be a spy for the Uenokagashu and murders Nagara before turning on Azumi, who kills her. Azumi then defeats Tsuchigumo, whose weapons are poisoned razor wires, but is left paralyzed by his poison and at the mercy of Kunio, Sanada's concubine and the clan's true leader, until Ginkaku sacrifices himself to save her. Weakened but determined, Azumi fights her way through Sanada's troops for a final duel with the warlord.

The film was distributed in Japan by Toho and released on March 12, 2005. In the United Kingdom it was released directly to home video later that year.

documents.title: A Bridge Too Far
documents.tagline: Out of the sky comes the screen's most incredible spectacle of men and war!
documents.overview: Operation Market Garden, September 1944. The Allies attempt to capture several strategically important bridges in the Netherlands in the hope of breaking the German lines.
documents.plot:
In September 1944, Allied forces have won the Battle of Normandy. General Browning, with the approval of Field Marshal Montgomery, drafts a plan known as Operation Market Garden which will land 35,000 paratroopers and glider men 300 miles (480 km) from their airfields in England, behind enemy lines in the Netherlands over a 64-mile corridor with the ultimate goal of crossing the Rhine River at Arnhem. The single road linking a succession of bridges is narrow and exposed. Two American divisions land near Eindhoven, Grave and Nijmegen. A British division under Major-General Roy Urquhart, is to land near Arnhem, supported by a brigade of Polish paratroopers under General Stanisław Sosabowski. The land forces from XXX Armoured Corps are to pierce the front line in Belgium, cross the captured bridges and relieve the forces at Arnhem within two days.
Major-General Urquhart's officers are surprised their landing zones are so far from their objectives. While consensus is that resistance will consist of inexperienced old men and Hitler Youth, reconnaissance photos show German tanks at Arnhem. General Browning dismisses the photos and ignores reports from the Dutch underground.
Although the airborne drops surprise the enemy and meet little resistance, the Son bridge is demolished by the Germans just before it can be secured. At Arnhem, heavily armed jeeps either do not arrive or are destroyed in an ambush. The British division's radios do not function leaving Urquhart out of contact with Browning's headquarters. The progress of XXX Corps is slowed by German resistance, the narrowness of the road, and the need to construct a Bailey bridge to replace the bridge at Son. They are halted by fierce resistance at Nijmegen and soldiers of the 82nd Airborne Division perform a daylight river crossing in rubber boats to capture the Nijmegen bridge but XXX Corps remains delayed while infantry secure the city.
The Germans close in on the isolated British paratroopers occupying Arnhem near the bridge, and although Sosabowski's troops finally arrive after being delayed in England, they are too late to reinforce the British. After days of intense fighting against SS infantry and panzers the outgunned troops are either captured or forced to withdraw to Oosterbeek. Urquhart receives orders to retreat, while the other Allied commanders blame the various difficulties encountered for their failure to provide support. Urquhart escapes with less than a fifth of his original 10,000 troops while those who are too badly injured to flee stay behind to cover the withdrawal. At British headquarters, Urquhart confronts Browning about his personal sentiments regarding the operation and the latter contradicts his earlier optimism.
Back in Oosterbeek Kate ter Horst, whose home has been converted into a makeshift hospital by the British, abandons its ruins.

documents.title: Into the Wild
documents.tagline: Into the heart. Into the soul.
documents.overview: After graduating from Emory University in 1992, top student and athlete Christopher McCandless abandons his possessions, gives his entire $24,000 savings account to charity, and hitchhikes to Alaska to live in the wilderness.
documents.plot:
Into the Wild is a biographical drama film directed by Sean Penn, released in 2007. The movie is based on the life of Christopher McCandless, an American young man who abandoned his material possessions and hitchhiked to Alaska with the intention of living off the land.

The film begins with Chris McCandless (played by Emile Hirsch), a recent college graduate from a wealthy family in Carthage, Missouri. Chris's parents, Walt (Vince Vaughn) and Billie (Catherine Keener), are portrayed as loving but also somewhat neglectful, having given their son the freedom to explore his own path in life.

Chris becomes increasingly disillusioned with the materialism and superficiality of modern society, feeling suffocated by the expectations placed upon him. He decides to leave behind his comfortable life and embark on a journey of self-discovery, inspired by the writings of Henry David Thoreau's Walden.

The film follows Chris as he travels across the country, hitchhiking and working odd jobs to save money for his trip to Alaska. Along the way, he meets various characters who influence his worldview, including Wayne Westerberg (Hal Holbrook), a grizzled old truck driver who teaches him about the importance of living in the moment.

In 1992, Chris arrives in Anchorage, Alaska, and begins his journey into the wilderness. He adopts the alias "Alexander Supertramp" and sets out to live off the land, foraging for food and building a shelter. The film depicts Chris's struggles with the harsh environment, including encounters with bears, mosquitoes, and extreme weather conditions.

As the seasons change, Chris becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, struggling to adapt to the unforgiving wilderness. He begins to question his decision to leave behind civilization, feeling overwhelmed by the vastness of nature.

The film takes a tragic turn when Chris's bus breaks down on the side of the road, and he is forced to abandon his vehicle. In an attempt to survive, Chris sets fire to his bus, but the flames spread out of control, consuming everything in their path.

In the end, Chris's body is discovered by two hunters, who report him missing to the authorities. The film ends with a sense of melancholy and regret, as Chris's parents receive news of his death, realizing too late that they had failed to connect with their son on a deeper level.

Throughout the film, Sean Penn's direction weaves together themes of identity, community, and the human relationship with nature. Emile Hirsch delivers a powerful performance as Chris McCandless, capturing the complexity and vulnerability of this enigmatic young man. The cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the stunning beauty of Alaska's wilderness.

Overall, Into the Wild is a thought-provoking film that raises questions about the human condition and our place in the world. It is a poignant reminder of the importance of connection, community, and living life on one's own terms.

documents.title: The Jane Austen Book Club
documents.tagline: You don't have to know the books to be in the club
documents.overview: Six Californians start a club to discuss the works of Jane Austen. As they delve into Austen's literature, the club members find themselves dealing with life experiences that parallel the themes of the books they are reading.
documents.plot:
The Jane Austen Book Club is the brainchild of fiftysomething six-time divorcée Bernadette, who develops the idea when she meets Prudie, a prim, married high school French teacher in her mid-20s, at a Jane Austen film festival. The plan is to have six members discuss all six of Austen's novels (Pride and Prejudice, Sense and Sensibility, Emma, Persuasion, Mansfield Park, and Northanger Abbey), with each member hosting the group once a month.
Also inducted into the club are Sylvia, a librarian recently separated from her philandering lawyer husband Daniel after over two decades of marriage; her twentysomething lesbian daughter Allegra; Jocelyn, a happily unmarried control freak and breeder of Rhodesian Ridgebacks, and Sylvia's friend since childhood; and Grigg, a science fiction fan invited into the group by Jocelyn with the hope to match him with Sylvia.
As the months pass, each of the members develops characteristics similar to those of Austen's characters. So, they react to events in their lives similarly to their fictional counterparts.
Bernadette is the matriarchal figure who longs to see everyone find happiness. Sylvia clings to her belief in steadfast love and devotion (eventually reconciling with Daniel). Jocelyn denies her own feelings for Grigg while playing matchmaker for him and Sylvia. Prudie is encumbered with her inattentive husband Dean, and free-spirited, marijuana-smoking, aging hippie mother Mama Sky, who dies in a car accident.
Prudie also finds herself desperately trying to resist her feelings for seductive student Trey, meanwhile accusing Dean of coming on to her high-school acquaintance at Mama Sky's funeral. Allegra, who tends to meet her lovers while engaging in death-defying activities, feels betrayed because her partner, aspiring writer Corinne, uses Allegra's life as the basis for her short stories.
Grigg is attracted to Jocelyn and mystified by her seeming lack of interest in him, marked by her failure to read the Ursula Le Guin novels he hoped would interest her. He also serves as the comedic foil to Jocelyn's and Prudie's very serious takes on the books.
The last book club meeting is held on the beach. Daniel wants to join the book club after reading Persuasion with Allegra at the hospital after she has suffered a concussion from an indoor climbing accident. So, Sylvia lets Daniel into the book club.
Grigg brings his elder sister Cat Harris, who persuades Jocelyn to take a chance on him because he loves her. As a date, Allegra brings Dr. Yep, who treated her concussion. Prudie, the scheduled host, does not attend. Instead, she goes to meet Trey, but reconsiders after considering what Jane Austen would do. Prudie goes home to Dean and reads Persuasion with him, helping them rediscover their love. Daniel leaves a letter for Sylvia at her doorstep. Upon reading it, she accepts Daniel back.

documents.title: The Pledge
documents.tagline: Detective Jerry Black has made a promise he can't break, to catch a killer he can't find.
documents.overview: A police chief about to retire pledges to help a woman find her daughter's killer.
documents.plot:
The Pledge is a 2001 American neo-noir psychological thriller film directed and co-produced by Sean Penn, based on the 1958 novella by the Swiss writer Friedrich Dürrenmatt. Jack Nicholson stars as a newly retired detective, supported by an ensemble cast including Aaron Eckhart, Helen Mirren, Robin Wright Penn, Vanessa Redgrave and Benicio del Toro. Released on January 19, 2001, it competed for the Palme d'Or at that year's Cannes Film Festival.

On the night of his retirement party, Reno, Nevada, police detective Jerry Black learns that a young girl, Ginny Larsen, has been found murdered. He breaks the news to the girl's parents, and her grief-stricken mother makes him swear on a cross her daughter made that he will find the killer. A suspect, Toby Jay Wadenah, a Native American man with an intellectual disability, is quickly arrested, and under pressure from Jerry's colleague Stan he confesses, then kills himself with a deputy's gun. The case is closed, but Jerry remains unconvinced.

Abandoning his retirement fishing trip, Jerry continues to investigate on his own. A friend of Ginny's reveals that Ginny had befriended a man she called "the Giant," who gave her small porcupine-shaped treats. A drawing by Ginny shows the man with a black station wagon, not Toby's red pickup, and Jerry uncovers similar unsolved killings of young girls in the region that Toby could not have committed.

Determined to keep his promise, Jerry buys a gas station at the center of the area where the murders took place and settles there. He befriends Lori, a waitress fleeing an abusive former partner, and her young daughter, Chrissy. They move in with him,, and Jerry becomes Chrissy's father figure and Lori's lover. When Chrissy tells him that a man she calls "the wizard" has given her porcupine candies and arranged to meet her again, Jerry persuades the police to set a trap, using Chrissy as bait. But the man never arrives: unknown to anyone, he has been killed in a car crash on his way to the meeting. The police leave, Lori furiously rejects Jerry for endangering her daughter, and in the final scene Jerry, drunk and broken, sits alone outside his abandoned gas station, muttering that the killer is still out there.

The Pledge received mainly positive reviews, with praise for Nicholson's subtle performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 78% approval and Metacritic a score of 71. It was a commercial disappointment, grossing $29.4 million against a budget of over $35 million.

documents.title: Along Came Polly
documents.tagline: For the most cautious man on Earth, life is about to get interesting.
documents.overview: Reuben Feffer is a guy who's spent his entire life playing it safe. Polly Prince is irresistible as a free-spirit who lives for the thrill of the moment. When these two comically mismatched souls collide, Reuben's world is turned upside down, as he makes an uproarious attempt to change his life from middle-of-the-road to totally-out-there.
documents.plot:
Along Came Polly is a 2004 American romantic comedy film directed by John Hamburg and written by Hamburg and Larry Levin. The movie stars Ben Stiller, Jennifer Aniston, Philip Baker Hall, and Debra Messing.

The story begins with Reuben Feffer (Ben Stiller), a risk-averse and uptight insurance salesman who has been in a long-term relationship with his girlfriend, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston). However, their relationship is stagnant, and Reuben feels suffocated by the predictability of it all. He meets a free-spirited woman named Sandy (Debra Messing) at a singles bar, but she's not interested in him.

Reuben's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Polly's cousin, Polly Prince (Jennifer Aniston), who is also his coworker and friend. Reuben has had feelings for Polly since high school, but she never reciprocated them. When Polly gets engaged to a man named Ray (Philip Baker Hall), Reuben sees this as an opportunity to finally be with her.

However, things take a turn when Reuben's life insurance policy is canceled due to his lack of risk-taking behavior. He then decides to go skydiving for the first time, which becomes a pivotal moment in his life. This experience makes him realize that he needs to take more risks and live life on his own terms.

As Reuben navigates his newfound sense of freedom, he starts to reevaluate his relationship with Polly. He realizes that he's been playing it safe all these years, and it's time for him to be more spontaneous and open-minded. Meanwhile, Polly is struggling with her engagement and feeling suffocated by the idea of settling down.

The plot thickens when Reuben and Polly start to reconnect, but their relationship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. Along the way, Reuben learns valuable lessons about love, risk-taking, and being true to oneself.

In the end, Reuben must decide whether he's willing to take a chance on Polly and their relationship. The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous climax that showcases the growth and development of both characters.

Throughout the film, Ben Stiller delivers a standout performance as the lovable but awkward Reuben Feffer. Jennifer Aniston shines as the charming and free-spirited Polly Prince, bringing depth and nuance to her character. The supporting cast adds to the humor and charm of the movie, making Along Came Polly a delightful and entertaining romantic comedy that explores themes of love, risk-taking, and self-discovery.

documents.title: The Family Man
documents.tagline: What if you made different choices? What if you said yes, instead of no? What if you got a second chance?
documents.overview: Jack's lavish, fast-paced lifestyle changes one Christmas night when he stumbles into a grocery store holdup and disarms the gunman. The next morning he wakes up in bed lying next to Kate, his college sweetheart he left in order to pursue his career, and to the horrifying discovery that his former life no longer exists. As he stumbles through this alternate suburban universe, Jack finds himself at a crossroad where he must choose between his high-power career and the woman he loves.
documents.plot: Jack's lavish, fast-paced lifestyle changes one Christmas night when he stumbles into a grocery store holdup and disarms the gunman. The next morning he wakes up in bed lying next to Kate, his college sweetheart he left in order to pursue his career, and to the horrifying discovery that his former life no longer exists. As he stumbles through this alternate suburban universe, Jack finds himself at a crossroad where he must choose between his high-power career and the woman he loves.

documents.title: Evening
documents.tagline: Her greatest secret was her greatest gift.
documents.overview: As Constance (Natasha Richardson) and Nina (Toni Collette) gather at the deathbed of their mother, Ann (Vanessa Redgrave), they learn for the first time that their mother lived an entire other lifetime during one evening 50 years ago. In vivid flashbacks, the young Ann (Claire Daines) spends one night with a man named Harris (Patrick Wilson), who was the love of her life.
documents.plot:
Evening is a 2007 American drama film directed by Lajos Koltai, with a screenplay by Susan Minot and Michael Cunningham based on Minot's 1998 novel of the same name. The ensemble cast includes Claire Danes as the young Ann, Toni Collette, Vanessa Redgrave, Patrick Wilson, Hugh Dancy and Mamie Gummer. The novel and original screenplay were set in Maine, but Koltai was so taken with a Newport house found by his location scouts that he moved the story to Rhode Island; filming began in September 2006, with locations in Tiverton, Bristol, Providence and Manhattan.

The film moves between the 1950s and the present, as Ann Grant Lord lies dying and reflects on her past, mentioning people her daughters Constance and Nina have never heard of and leaving them wondering whether she is delusional. In the 1950s, Ann, a young cabaret singer, arrives at the grand Newport home of her best friend Lila Wittenborn for Lila's wedding to Karl Ross. Lila's brother Buddy, Ann's college friend and a heavy drinker, introduces her to Harris Arden, a young doctor and the son of a former family servant, and confides that Lila has always adored Harris and may be marrying out of duty rather than love. Ann and Harris feel an instant connection. On the wedding day Lila admits that Harris rebuffed her, and she goes through with the marriage. At the reception Ann sings, joined by Harris, while the drunken Buddy confronts them and then unexpectedly kisses Harris. Later Buddy confesses that he has loved Ann for years. When he plays a frightening prank after diving from a clifftop into the sea, Ann angrily rejects him and slips away with Harris to his hideaway, where they make love. That night, searching for Ann, Buddy is struck by a car and killed, a tragedy that Ann and Harris learn of only the next morning. In the present, Lila visits Ann's bedside to reminisce, and the memories of that weekend help Ann offer her daughters, especially the uncertain Nina, guidance about love and the choices they face.

Evening grossed about $20 million worldwide. It received largely negative reviews, holding a 28% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it beautifully filmed but dull and a waste of a talented cast, though some critics praised the performances, particularly those of Danes and Gummer.

documents.title: P.S. I Love You
documents.tagline: His life ended. Now, a new one will begin.
documents.overview: A young widow discovers that her late husband has left her 10 messages intended to help ease her pain and start a new life.
documents.plot: A young widow discovers that her late husband has left her 10 messages intended to help ease her pain and start a new life.

documents.title: The Mexican
documents.tagline: Love with the safety off.
documents.overview: Jerry Welbach, a reluctant bagman, has been given two ultimatums: The first is from his mob boss to travel to Mexico and retrieve a priceless antique pistol, known as "the Mexican"... or suffer the consequences. The second is from his girlfriend Samantha to end his association with the mob. Jerry figures alive and in trouble with Samantha is better than the more permanent alternative, so he heads south of the border.
documents.plot:
In Los Angeles, a traffic light changes to red, and off-screen sounds of an automobile collision are heard.
Five years later, Jerry Welbach has been working off a debt to imprisoned mob boss Arnold Margolese. After Jerry fouls up what was supposed to be his final errand, Margolese's second-in-command, Bernie Nayman, sends Jerry on a new, final errand: retrieving an antique pistol in Mexico for Margolese from a man named Beck. This additional job proves to be the last straw for Jerry's girlfriend, Sam, who leaves him to move to Las Vegas.
In Mexico, Jerry finds the pistol with Beck, who explains the history of the legendary gun, known as "the Mexican". When Beck is killed by a stray bullet from celebratory gunfire, Jerry calls his colleague Ted and learns that Beck was Margolese's grandson. Just then, Jerry's car is stolen, with Beck's body and the pistol inside. Jerry recovers the car and the gun, shooting one of the thieves in the foot and burying the body, but cuts off, and keep, a toe as a keepsake.
While Sam is traveling to Las Vegas, a well-dressed hitman attempts to abduct her but is shot by another hitman who captures her instead. The second hitman introduces himself as Leroy and explains that he was hired to hold Sam hostage to ensure Jerry delivers the pistol.
Sam explains to Leroy that Jerry became indebted to Margolese five years earlier after crashing into Margolese's car while running a red light. At the accident site, the police discovered someone tied up in Margolese's trunk whom he intended to kill. Margolese was sent to prison for five years, and Jerry was forced to run errands for Margolese during that time. Bonding with Leroy, Sam correctly deduces that he is gay and encourages him to pick up Frank, a traveling postal worker. The three of them reach Las Vegas, and Leroy and Frank spend the night together.
In Mexico, Jerry is briefly arrested after a police officer notices Beck's blood in his car. Confiscating the pistol, the officer elaborates on its cursed history and takes it to a pawn shop. Ted arrives and reveals that the infamous Leroy has been sent after Sam. Jerry overhears a call with Nayman ordering Ted to kill him. They recover the pistol from the pawn shop, but Jerry confronts Ted and leaves with the gun. Realizing he grabbed Ted's passport instead of his own, he returns to find Ted has already fled.
In Las Vegas, the well-dressed hitman murders the innocent Frank and returns for Sam but is killed by a vengeful Leroy. Sam and Leroy fly to Mexico to meet Jerry, who crashes the car in an argument with Sam. Leroy finds the pistol and prepares to kill Jerry, but Jerry kills him first. He explains to a distraught Sam that Leroy was an imposter—his driver's license reveals he is actually Winston Baldry—and that Jerry once met the real Leroy, the well-dressed black hitman.

documents.title: Dreamcatcher
documents.tagline: A circle of friendship. A web of mystery. A pattern of fear.
documents.overview: Four boyhood pals perform a heroic act and are changed by the powers they gain in return. Years later, on a hunting trip in the Maine woods, they're overtaken by a vicious blizzard that harbors an ominous presence. Challenged to stop an alien force, the friends must first prevent the slaughter of innocent civilians by a military vigilante ... and then overcome a threat to the bond that unites the four of them.
documents.plot:
Dreamcatcher is a science fiction horror film directed by Lawrence Kasdan, based on the novel of the same name by Stephen King. The movie was released in 2003 and stars Morgan Freeman, Thomas Jane, Damian Lewis, Donnie Wahlberg, and Jason Lee.

The story begins with four friends - Jonesy (Jason Lee), Beaver (Donnie Wahlberg), Pete (Thomas Jane), and Henry (Morgan Freeman) - who have been inseparable since childhood. They share a deep bond and are known for their unique friendship. The movie takes place in 1980, during the height of the Vietnam War.

The story begins with Jonesy, who has recently returned from Vietnam, suffering from amnesia due to his experiences as a soldier. He is unable to recall any memories before his time in the war. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers that he and his friends have been chosen by an alien entity known as "The Gray" (also referred to as "The Others") to be its hosts on Earth.

The Gray has a plan to invade Earth using four human hosts, each with unique skills and abilities. The aliens intend to use the hosts' bodies to take over their minds and eventually conquer humanity. Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry are chosen for this purpose, but they soon realize that they must work together to stop The Gray's plans.

As the story unfolds, the four friends embark on a perilous journey across the United States, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way. They encounter various alien creatures, including giant spiders, mutated humans, and otherworldly beings. Along the way, they also uncover clues about their past and the true nature of The Gray's plan.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they struggle to work together and trust each other. Jonesy, in particular, grapples with his amnesia and tries to come to terms with his past. Beaver is haunted by a traumatic event from his childhood, while Pete struggles with his own demons.

As the stakes grow higher, the friends discover that The Gray's plan involves using their combined skills to create an army of alien-human hybrids. They must use all their strength, courage, and ingenuity to stop this plan and save humanity.

The movie culminates in a climactic showdown between the four friends and The Gray's minions. In the end, Jonesy, Beaver, Pete, and Henry manage to defeat the aliens and destroy their plans for world domination. However, not before they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make sacrifices to save humanity.

Overall, Dreamcatcher is a thrilling science fiction horror film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among fans of Stephen King's works.

documents.title: Reign of Fire
documents.tagline: Fight Fire With Fire
documents.overview: In post-apocalyptic England, an American volunteer and a British survivor team up to fight off a brood of fire-breathing dragons seeking to return to global dominance after centuries of rest underground. The Brit -- leading a clan of survivors to hunt down the King of the Dragons -- has much at stake: His mother was killed by a dragon, but his love is still alive.

documents.title: Brotherhood of the Wolf
documents.tagline: The year is 1766... The hunt for a killer has begun.
documents.overview: In 18th century France, the Chevalier de Fronsac and his Native American friend Mani are sent by the King to the Gevaudan province to investigate the killings of hundreds by a mysterious beast.
documents.plot:
During the French Revolution, Marquis d'Apcher writes his memoirs in his castle. He recounts his experiences in 1764, when a mysterious beast terrorized the county, or historical area, of Gévaudan. Grégoire de Fronsac, a knight and the royal naturalist of King Louis XV, and his Iroquois companion Mani, arrive to capture the beast. Fronsac becomes interested in Marianne de Morangias, the daughter of a local count, whose brother, Jean-François, was also an avid hunter and a world traveller, whose arm was mangled and rendered useless while overseas. Fronsac is also intrigued by Sylvia, an Italian courtesan at the local brothel.
While investigating another victim, Fronsac finds a fang made of steel. A traumatized child witness swears that the beast is controlled by what seems to be a human master. As the investigation proves unfruitful, the king's weapons master, Lord de Beauterne, arrives to put an end to the beast, and Fronsac is sent back to Paris. He realizes that the beast is actually an instrument of a secret society: The Brotherhood of the Wolf, which is working to undermine public confidence in the king and ultimately take over the country. Back in Gévaudan, the attacks by the real beast continue, and Fronsac returns to put an end to the beast's killings. At a secret rendezvous with Marianne, they are attacked by the beast, where it mysteriously refrains from attacking her.
Fronsac, Mani, and a young Marquis set out into the forest and set up an array of traps to capture the beast; it is severely injured but escapes. Mani sets off alone in pursuit, where he finds a catacomb used as the beast's holding pen, inhabited by the Brotherhood. Outnumbered, Mani is shot and killed. Fronsac discovers Mani's body and performs an autopsy, finding a silver bullet—Jean-François' signature choice of ammunition. In a fit of rage, a vengeful Fronsac goes to the catacombs and slaughters many members, but is overpowered by the local authorities and imprisoned.
Sylvia visits him in jail and reveals that she is a spy for the Holy See. She explains that Henri Sardis, the local priest and leader of the Brotherhood, believes that he is restoring worship of God to France. Pope Clement XIII has decided that Sardis is insane, and has sent her to eliminate him. She then poisons Fronsac, saying that he knows too much. Meanwhile, Jean-François comes to Marianne's room and reveals to her that he is the beast's master; it recognized his scent on her when it came near her, which is why it did not attack. He then rapes her when she rejects his advances.
Sylvia's agents exhume Fronsac and he appears at one of the Brotherhood's sermons. He kills several members, including Jean-François, who reveals that he had regained use of his supposedly mangled arm. Sardis escapes into the mountains, but is mauled to death by a pack of wolves. Fronsac and the Marquis go to the beast's lair, where it lies severely wounded.

documents.title: Hotel Chevalier
documents.overview: In a Paris hotel room, Jack Whitman lies on a bed. His phone rings; it's a woman on her way to see him, a surprise. She arrives and the complications of their relationship emerge in bits and pieces. Will they make love? Is their relationship over? (A prequel to The Darjeeling Limited, 2007.)
documents.plot:
In a hotel lobby, the concierge answers a phone call from a guest's room. Jack (Jason Schwartzman) lies on a hotel bed in a yellow bathrobe, watching the black-and-white American war film Stalag 17 and reading the newspaper. After ordering room service from the concierge in broken French, he receives a call from Rhett, his ex-girlfriend. She tells him she is on her way from the airport and asks for his room number. Despite objecting that he did not tell her she could come, Jack consents nevertheless. He then hurriedly attempts to tidy the room – pausing to play the opening bars of the song "Where Do You Go To (My Lovely)?" by Peter Sarstedt on his stereo system – and runs a bath.
Jack is again lying on the bed, now in a gray suit. Hearing a knock, he starts the song playing again before opening the door to Rhett (Natalie Portman). After staring at him for several seconds, Rhett breaks the silence by asking what music is playing. Receiving no response, she steps into the room and presents Jack with a bouquet of flowers. When she moves to kiss him on the mouth, he turns his head away and they embrace instead. He closes the door and asks how she found him; she replies that it "wasn't actually that hard". She moves around the room browsing through his possessions, brushes her teeth with his toothbrush and declines to take the bath he had run for her.
Stepping back into the bedroom, Rhett turns to face the man and confronts him, asking slowly "what the fuck is going on?" Jack motions for her to join him on the bed and at her prompting, he reveals in the ensuing conversation that he has been living in the hotel room for "more than a month", and that he had left to escape their relationship. They lie back on the bed looking at one another before being interrupted by the arrival of room service. Once alone again, the two kiss and Jack begins to undress Rhett. They have an uncomfortable exchange about not having slept with other people and when Jack notices bruises on her arm after undressing her further, Rhett chooses not to comment on them. Lying on top of him, she tells Jack that she does not want to lose his friendship, that she loves him and never meant to hurt him. He responds coldly that he "will never be [her] friend", but holds her when she embraces him. "Where Do You Go To (My Lovely)?" starts again and Jack offers to show Rhett his view of Paris.
Rhett is perched against an armoire, Jack approaches and covers her naked body with the yellow bathrobe, and the two move towards the window. After they step out on the balcony, Jack draws a toothpick from his pocket and hands it to Rhett with an upwards nod, which she reciprocates. After looking out for another few seconds she clasps his neck lightly and they step back inside.

documents.title: Racing Stripes
documents.tagline: Cheer 'til you're horse!
documents.overview: Shattered illusions are hard to repair -- especially for a good-hearted zebra named Stripes who's spent his life on a Kentucky farm amidst the sorely mistaken notion that he's a debonair thoroughbred. Once he faces the fact that his stark stripes mark him as different, he decides he'll race anyway. And with help from the young girl who raised him, he just might end up in the winner's circle.

documents.title: The Shipping News
documents.tagline: You'll never guess what you'll find inside...
documents.overview: An emotionally-beaten man with his young daughter moves to his ancestral home in Newfoundland to reclaim his life.
documents.plot:
When Quoyle was a young boy, his father Guy tossed him into a lake, expecting him to swim naturally. Images of flailing in water and nearly drowning often resurface in Quoyle's memory when he is under stress.
Quoyle, now an ink setter at a small newspaper in Poughkeepsie, New York, lives a lonely life. He becomes infatuated with and marries a vivacious local woman named Petal. She is an unfaithful wife and negligent mother to their six-year-old daughter, Bunny. Petal runs off with a lover, taking Bunny with her. Soon after, Petal and her boyfriend are killed in a car accident. The police return Bunny to Quoyle, informing him that Petal had sold her to a black market adoption operation for $6,000.
Shortly before those events, Quoyle's elderly parents die by suicide together. Quoyle's aunt, Agnis Hamm, arrives to pay her respects to her late half-brother, though her real motive is to steal Guy's ashes (which she later dumps down an outhouse hole and urinates on). Agnis is moving to the ancestral family home in Newfoundland, which has been abandoned for 44 years. She agrees to stay a few more days to help Quoyle through his recent turmoil, then persuades him to move to Newfoundland with her.
While struggling to build a new life, restore the derelict house, and take care of Bunny, Quoyle meets Wavey Prowse, a widow whose young son, Harry, has a learning disability. They gradually develop a deepening relationship. Wavey eventually admits she pretends to be widowed, ashamed that her philandering husband left when she was pregnant.
Quoyle learns that the ancient Quoyles were pirates who ran ships aground and savagely pillaged them. When those Quoyles were driven out, they moved their house over a frozen lake to its present location, now known as Quoyle's Point. Quoyle's cousin Nolan, an old hermit, reveals that young Agnis was raped and impregnated by her teenaged half-brother (Quoyle's father), resulting in an abortion.
Quoyle applies for an ink setter job at the Gammy Bird. Owner and publisher Jack Buggit instead hires him as a reporter covering auto wrecks and the town's shipping news. With no journalism experience, Quoyle struggles to produce decent articles, incurring managing editor Tert Card's constant scorn.
Reporter Billy Pretty tutors and encourages Quoyle. When Quoyle's article about a millionaire's vintage yacht docked in town is popular with readers, Jack assigns him a weekly column profiling an interesting boat in port. Meanwhile, Agnis resumes her former occupation as a boat upholsterer to help support the family. She later confides to Quoyle that the woman she loved died six years earlier from leukemia.
Rather than running his newspaper full time, Jack Buggit commercially fishes to prevent his adult son Dennis, who nearly died at sea, from obtaining his own commercial license, which are limited. Jack drowns while securing his boat in an oncoming storm.

documents.title: Freddy vs. Jason
documents.tagline: Evil will battle evil.
documents.overview: In an attempt to free himself from a state of forgotten limbo, evil dream-demon Freddy Krueger devises a plan to manipulate un-dead mass murderer Jason Voorhees  into slicing-and-dicing his way through the teenage population of Springwood.  But when the master of dreams loses control of his monster, a brutal fight to the death is the only way out.
documents.plot:
Freddy vs. Jason is a 2003 American horror film directed by Ronny Yu and written by Damian Shannon and Mark Swift. The movie is a crossover between two popular horror franchises: A Nightmare on Elm Street and Friday the 13th.

The film begins with Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), the dream demon from Springwood, Ohio, who has been trapped in a magical realm known as the "Dream World" for over 25 years. However, due to a series of events, Freddy is able to escape and enter the real world, where he finds himself in Crystal Lake, New Jersey.

Meanwhile, Jason Voorhees (Ken Kirzinger), the masked killer from Camp Crystal Lake, has also escaped his own realm and entered the real world. The two horror icons soon discover that they are being hunted by a group of teenagers who are trying to survive their encounters with both Freddy and Jason.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Freddy is using his powers to manipulate the dreams of the teenagers, while Jason is using his brute strength to terrorize them in the real world. The two horror icons engage in a series of battles, with Freddy using his claws and wit to try and outsmart Jason, who relies on his physical strength to overpower his opponents.

As the body count rises, the teenagers begin to realize that they are being manipulated by both Freddy and Jason, who are working together to eliminate them. The group soon discovers that the only way to stop both horror icons is to find a way to destroy their respective realms and trap them back in their own worlds.

In the climactic final battle, the teenagers use a magical artifact known as the "Dream Crystal" to create a portal between the Dream World and the real world. Freddy and Jason are drawn into the portal, where they engage in an epic battle that takes place within both the dream and reality realms.

Ultimately, the teenagers emerge victorious, but not without sustaining significant injuries. As the dust settles, it becomes clear that Freddy has been defeated, but at a great cost: he is trapped in the Dream World, unable to escape. Jason, on the other hand, returns to his own realm, where he will continue to terrorize Camp Crystal Lake.

The film ends with a sense of closure for both horror franchises, as the surviving teenagers reflect on their harrowing experiences and the lessons they learned about facing their fears. While Freddy vs. Jason received mixed reviews from critics at the time of its release, it has since become a cult classic among horror fans, who appreciate its campy humor, over-the-top violence, and nostalgic value.

Overall, Freddy vs. Jason is a fun and entertaining crossover film that brings together two beloved horror franchises in a way that is both faithful to their respective worlds and fresh enough to feel new.

documents.title: Alvin and the Chipmunks
documents.tagline: The Original Entourage
documents.overview: A struggling songwriter named Dave Seville finds success when he comes across a trio of singing chipmunks: mischievous leader Alvin, brainy Simon, and chubby, impressionable Theodore.
documents.plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks is a 2007 American musical comedy based on the characters created by Ross Bagdasarian Sr., directed by Tim Hill from a screenplay by Jon Vitti, Will McRobb and Chris Viscardi. Jason Lee plays the songwriter Dave Seville, David Cross the record executive Ian Hawke and Cameron Richardson Dave's former girlfriend Claire, while Justin Long, Matthew Gray Gubler and Jesse McCartney voice the chipmunks Alvin, Simon and Theodore.

The three talking chipmunk brothers live in a fir tree that is cut down and taken to Los Angeles after JETT Records buys it as a Christmas tree. In the same building, the struggling songwriter Dave Seville has his latest demo rejected by Ian Hawke, his old college roommate and the label's chief executive. The chipmunks follow Dave home, and after an initial panic he discovers they can sing, striking a deal to give them food and a home in return for performing his songs.

The partnership starts badly. Stage fright ruins their first audition for Ian, the chipmunks accidentally cost Dave his advertising job, and Alvin's attempts at matchmaking spoil a dinner with Claire. To make amends, the brothers go to Ian's mansion on their own and sing Dave's song "Christmas Don't Be Late", winning a record contract and making Dave their manager. As they grow attached to Dave and start to see him as family, he keeps them at arm's length.

Ian pushes for ever more aggressive promotion, and when Dave insists the chipmunks are too young for celebrity, Ian convinces them that Dave is holding them back. After a quarrel, and finding an old letter in which Dave wrote about returning them to the forest, the brothers move in with Ian, who showers them with luxury while working them to exhaustion on tour and telling them Dave no longer cares. When Ian announces a year-long world tour, Dave enlists Claire's help to sneak into their concert at the Orpheum Theatre. Realising they have been deceived, the chipmunks sabotage the show. Ian locks them in a cage for a flight to Paris, but they escape, reunite with Dave, and Ian's career collapses.

Critics were largely negative, with 28% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but the film opened second behind I Am Legend and grossed $365.4 million worldwide on a budget of $55 to 60 million, launching a series of three sequels.

documents.title: I Am Legend
documents.tagline: The last man on Earth is not alone
documents.overview: Robert Neville is a scientist who was unable to stop the spread of the terrible virus that was incurable and man-made. Immune, Neville is now the last human survivor in what is left of New York City and perhaps the world. For three years, Neville has faithfully sent out daily radio messages, desperate to find any other survivors who might be out there. But he is not alone.
documents.plot:
I Am Legend is a post-apocalyptic science fiction film directed by Francis Lawrence, based on the novel of the same name by Richard Matheson. The movie stars Will Smith as Robert Neville, a military scientist who finds himself to be one of the last humans on Earth.

The story begins in 2006, where Robert Neville (Will Smith) is working for the United States Army at a biological research facility in New York City. He is part of a team that has been studying a virus known as the "Krippin Virus" which causes its hosts to become violent and zombie-like creatures after infection. The virus was created by a scientist named Dr. Krippin, who had been experimenting with it before his death.

As the outbreak occurs, Robert Neville is one of the few survivors, but he soon realizes that he is not alone on Earth. He finds himself surrounded by hordes of infected humans, which he has dubbed "Virals." The Virals are fast, agile, and seemingly unstoppable, making them a formidable threat to human survival.

As the years pass, Robert Neville becomes increasingly isolated, with no contact with other humans. He spends his days scavenging for food and supplies, while also trying to find a cure for the virus. He sets up traps and defenses around his home in an attempt to protect himself from the Virals, but he knows that it's only a matter of time before they break through.

One day, Robert Neville receives a package containing a small dog, which becomes his companion and friend. The dog helps him to stay sane and provides emotional support during his lonely existence. As the years go by, Robert Neville begins to notice changes in himself, as he starts to exhibit some of the same characteristics as the Virals.

The turning point comes when Robert Neville discovers that the virus is not just a simple infection, but rather a complex genetic mutation that has altered his own DNA. He realizes that he may be one of the few remaining humans who are immune to the virus, and that he may hold the key to finding a cure.

As Robert Neville delves deeper into the mystery of the virus, he becomes increasingly obsessed with finding a way to restore humanity to its former glory. He sets out on a perilous journey across New York City, searching for any signs of life or clues to the virus's origins.

In the end, Robert Neville discovers that the only remaining human survivor is a young girl who has been living in an abandoned church. Together, they form a bond and work towards finding a cure for the virus. However, as they near their goal, Robert Neville realizes that he may be too late to save humanity, and that the world may never be the same again.

The movie ends with Robert Neville and the young girl escaping from New York City in a helicopter, leaving behind the ruins of civilization. As they fly away, Robert Neville looks out at the desolate landscape, knowing that he has lost his way and that the world will never be the same again.

documents.overview: Cousins, Bo and Luke Duke, with the help of their eye-catching cousin, Daisy and moonshine-running Uncle Jesse, try and save the family farm from being destroyed by Hazzard County's corrupt commissioner, Boss Hogg. Their efforts constantly find the 'Duke Boys' eluding authorities in 'The General Lee', their 1969 orange Dodge Charger that keeps them one step ahead of the dimwitted antics of the small southern town's Sheriff, Roscoe P. Coltrane.

documents.title: The Orphanage
documents.tagline: A tale of love.  A story of horror.
documents.overview: A woman brings her family back to her childhood home, which used to be an orphanage, intent on reopening it. Before long, her son starts to communicate with a new invisible friend.
documents.plot:
The Orphanage is a Spanish horror film directed by Juan Antonio Bayona, released in 2007. The movie tells the story of a woman named Laura, played by Belén Rueda, who returns to the orphanage where she grew up as an adult.

Laura's childhood was marked by tragedy when her younger brother died under mysterious circumstances at the orphanage. She has always felt a deep sense of guilt and responsibility for his death. As an adult, Laura is haunted by nightmares and a feeling of being watched. She decides to return to the orphanage, now abandoned and rumored to be haunted, in an attempt to lay her brother's spirit to rest.

Upon arrival, Laura discovers that the orphanage has been renovated into a nursing home for elderly people. However, she soon realizes that the residents are not what they seem. They appear to be in a state of catatonia, and their eyes seem to follow her everywhere she goes. As Laura delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to uncover dark secrets about the orphanage's past.

Laura's investigation leads her to a room where her brother's grave is supposed to be located. However, when she searches for it, she finds that it has been moved and is now in a different location. This discovery sets off a chain of events that reveals the truth about the orphanage's dark history.

As Laura digs deeper, she discovers that the orphanage was once home to a group of children who died under mysterious circumstances. The children's spirits are trapped between the world of the living and the afterlife, and they are unable to move on. Laura realizes that her brother's death is connected to these children's deaths and that she has been carrying the guilt of their deaths with her all along.

In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Laura herself was one of the children who died at the orphanage. Her memories of the event were false, implanted by her adoptive parents to protect her from the truth. The entire story is a product of Laura's imagination, and she has been trying to uncover the truth about her own past.

The movie ends with Laura finally finding peace and closure. She realizes that she was not responsible for her brother's death and that she has been carrying the guilt of others' deaths all along. The film's ending is open to interpretation, leaving the audience to wonder whether Laura's memories were real or just a product of her imagination.

Overall, The Orphanage is a haunting and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of grief, guilt, and the power of the human mind. The movie features stunning visuals and a standout performance from Belén Rueda, who brings depth and nuance to the complex character of Laura.

documents.title: Charlie Wilson's War
documents.tagline: When the world wasn't looking, he changed it forever.
documents.overview: The true story of Texas congressman Charlie Wilson's covert dealings in Afghanistan, where his efforts to assist rebels in their war with the Soviets had some unforeseen and long-reaching effects.
documents.plot: A Texas congressman sets a series of events in motion when he conspires with a CIA operative to aid Afghan mujahideen rebels fighting the Soviets.

documents.overview: Following a childhood tragedy, Dewey Cox follows a long and winding road to music stardom. Dewey perseveres through changing musical styles, an addiction to nearly every drug known and bouts of uncontrollable rage.

documents.title: Underdog
documents.tagline: ONE NATION... UNDER DOG
documents.overview: A lab accident gives a hound named Shoeshine some serious superpowers -- a secret that the dog eventually shares with the young boy who becomes his owner and friend.
documents.plot:
Underdog is a 2007 animated superhero comedy film that tells the story of a lovable and underappreciated dog named Underdog who dreams of becoming a hero. The movie explores several themes, including the importance of believing in oneself and one's abilities.

At its core, Underdog is a tale about self-discovery and empowerment. The main character, Underdog, is an ordinary dog with extraordinary potential, but he lacks confidence and recognition from those around him. As he navigates his way through various challenges and obstacles, Underdog learns to trust himself and his unique abilities, ultimately discovering that being different is not a weakness, but a strength.

The film also touches on the theme of friendship and loyalty. Underdog's relationships with his owner, Polly Purebred, and other characters in the story serve as a reminder of the importance of having supportive friends by your side. Through their interactions, the movie shows how these bonds can help us overcome adversity and achieve our goals.

Furthermore, Underdog pokes fun at societal expectations and the pressures to conform. The character of Sweet Polly Purebred, for instance, is a perfect example of this theme. She's a beautiful, high-society dog who struggles with her own identity and sense of purpose, highlighting the tension between being true to oneself and meeting the expectations of others.

Overall, Underdog is a heartwarming story about embracing one's individuality, finding confidence in oneself, and the power of friendship and loyalty.

documents.title: Lars and the Real Girl
documents.tagline: The search for true love begins outside the box.
documents.overview: Extremely shy Lars finds it impossible to make friends or socialize. His brother and sister-in-law worry about him, so when he announces that he has a girlfriend he met on the Internet, they are overjoyed. But Lars' new lady is a life-size plastic woman. On the advice of a doctor, his family and the rest of the community go along with his delusion.
