documents.title: Death in Venice
documents.tagline: The celebrated story of a man obsessed with ideal beauty.
documents.overview: Composer Gustav von Aschenbach travels to Venice for health reasons. There, he becomes obsessed with the stunning beauty of an adolescent Polish boy named Tadzio who is staying with his family at the same Grand Hôtel des Bains on the Lido as Aschenbach.
documents.plot:
Death in Venice (Italian: Morte a Venezia) is a 1971 historical drama film directed and produced by Luchino Visconti, who adapted Thomas Mann's 1912 novella with Nicola Badalucco. It stars Dirk Bogarde as Gustav von Aschenbach and Björn Andrésen as Tadzio, with Mark Burns, Marisa Berenson and Silvana Mangano. Shot in Technicolor by Pasqualino De Santis, it uses music from Gustav Mahler's Third and Fifth Symphonies and is the second part of Visconti's "German Trilogy", between The Damned (1969) and Ludwig (1973).

In poor health, the composer Aschenbach travels to Venice to rest. As his ship arrives, a garishly made-up old man accosts him with suggestive remarks, and he turns away in disgust. Staying at the Grand Hotel des Bains on the Lido, he notices a Polish family and becomes captivated by their beautiful adolescent son, Tadzio. The boy's image recalls heated debates with his friend and pupil Alfred over whether beauty is created by art or exists in nature and is superior to it. Aschenbach watches Tadzio on the beach, and after an encounter in the hotel lift in which the boy seems to give him an inviting look, he resolves in agitation to leave. When his luggage is misdirected at the station, however, he is secretly glad to return, though he sees a man collapse at the station, and the hotel manager dismisses foreign press reports as exaggerated.

Aschenbach makes Tadzio his muse but cannot master his longing and drifts into daydreams about the unreachable boy, who notices his gaze and occasionally returns it, though they never speak. A travel clerk in Saint Mark's Square reluctantly admits that cholera is spreading through the city, and Aschenbach imagines warning Tadzio's mother. He follows the family to St Mark's Basilica, and a talkative barber dyes and paints him into a likeness of the old man from the ship. Trailing the family through the streets, he collapses by a well in pained laughter, and he dreams of a disastrous concert in Munich and Alfred's reproaches. Learning the family is departing, Aschenbach, now gravely ill, sits on the empty beach watching Tadzio wade into the sea to Mahler's Adagietto. The boy turns and points toward the horizon, and Aschenbach dies in his deck chair.

The film premiered in London on 1 March 1971 and competed at the 24th Cannes Film Festival. Critics have admired its sumptuous visuals, with Derek Malcolm of The Guardian calling it a slow, precise and beautiful achievement; Rotten Tomatoes reports 70% approval.

documents.title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
documents.tagline: The Greatest Adventure History Has Ever Revealed
documents.overview: Benjamin Franklin Gates and Dr. Abigail Chase re-team with Riley Poole and, now armed with a stack of long-lost pages from John Wilkes Booth's diary, Ben must follow a clue left there to prove his ancestor's innocence in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
documents.plot:
National Treasure: Book of Secrets is a 2007 American action-adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and written by Jim Kouf. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Benjamin Gates, a treasure hunter with a passion for American history.

The film begins with Benjamin Gates (Nicolas Cage) being approached by the Treasury Department to help find a lost document known as the "Book of Secrets." The book is said to contain information about the Founding Fathers' involvement in the Knights Templar and their alleged discovery of the Holy Grail. However, the book has been stolen from the National Archives, and it's up to Gates to retrieve it.

Gates teams up with his partner, Riley Poole (Dustin Hoffman), a computer expert, and Abigail Chase ( Diane Kruger), an archaeologist. Together, they embark on a perilous journey across the United States, following a series of cryptic clues left behind by the book's thief.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Gates and his team uncover a conspiracy involving the British government, which is trying to discredit Benjamin's claims about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar. The team also discovers that Abigail Chase is actually the daughter of John Adams, one of the Founding Fathers, making her a direct descendant of the president.

The plot thickens as Gates and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, they meet Patrick Gates (Sean Bean), Benjamin's long-lost father, who reveals that he was also involved in the Knights Templar and had been searching for the Book of Secrets.

As the story unfolds, Gates and his team finally reach the location of the lost document: a hidden chamber beneath the White House. However, they soon realize that they are not alone, as they are confronted by the British government's agents, who will stop at nothing to keep the truth about the Founding Fathers' involvement with the Knights Templar from being revealed.

In the end, Gates and his team successfully retrieve the Book of Secrets, but not before a thrilling showdown with the rival treasure hunters. The film concludes with Benjamin Gates returning the book to its rightful place in the National Archives, while Abigail Chase comes to terms with her newfound heritage as a descendant of John Adams.

Throughout the movie, Nicolas Cage delivers his signature blend of humor, wit, and action hero charm, making National Treasure: Book of Secrets an entertaining and thrilling adventure that explores the fascinating world of American history and cryptography.

documents.title: Zathura: A Space Adventure
documents.tagline: Adventure Is Waiting
documents.overview: After their father is called into work, two young boys, Walter and Danny, are left in the care of their teenage sister, Lisa, and told they must stay inside. Walter and Danny, who anticipate a boring day, are shocked when they begin playing Zathura, a space-themed board game, which they realize has mystical powers when their house is shot into space. With the help of an astronaut, the boys attempt to return home.
documents.plot:
Zathura: A Space Adventure is a science fiction film directed by Jon Favreau, released in 2005 by Columbia Pictures.

The story begins with two brothers, Walter (Josh Hutcherson) and Danny (Jensen Ackles), who are struggling to find common ground after their parents' divorce. Their lives take an unexpected turn when they stumble upon a mysterious board game called Zathura, which was left behind by their father. The game is unlike any other, as it seems to have a life of its own and emits a strange energy.

As soon as the brothers start playing the game, their house is suddenly sucked into a wormhole, transporting them to a distant planet called Pegasus-4. There, they encounter an alien named Captain Rainluff (Ben Kingsley), who claims that Zathura is a game created by an advanced civilization to test the skills of its players.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Walter and Danny's sibling rivalry causes them to disagree on how to play the game. As a result, they inadvertently trigger a catastrophic event that threatens to destroy their spaceship and the entire planet. The brothers must put aside their differences and work together to survive and find a way back home.

As they navigate through the challenges of Pegasus-4, Walter and Danny encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and malfunctioning spacecraft. Along the way, they also discover that Zathura is more than just a game - it's a test of their courage, wits, and teamwork.

Throughout their journey, the brothers learn valuable lessons about trust, loyalty, and the importance of family. In the end, they successfully complete the challenges of Zathura and find a way back to Earth, but not before discovering that their father is alive and well, having been presumed dead in a previous adventure.

The film features stunning visual effects, heart-pumping action sequences, and a healthy dose of humor, making it an entertaining ride for audiences of all ages. With its themes of brotherly love and the power of teamwork, Zathura: A Space Adventure is a delightful and thrilling adventure that will leave viewers eager for more.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: Failure to Launch
documents.tagline: To leave the nest, some men just need a little push.
documents.overview: Tripp, an attractive man in his thirties, is still living with his parents Al and Sue. Tripp's best friends Demo and Ace are also still living in their parents' homes and seem proud of it. Al and Sue are not happy, however, and are fascinated when friends whose adult son has recently moved away from home reveal they hired an expert to arrange the matter and couldn't be happier with the result.
documents.plot: At 35, Tripp has an interesting job, a hip car, a passion for sailing, an active dating life, and a great house - trouble is, he still lives with his parents, Al and Sue, who are not happy about it. Al and Sue are fascinated when friends whose adult son has recently moved away from home reveal they hired an expert to help. In desperation to push Tripp out of the nest once and for all, Al and Sue hatch a plan to hire Paula, an "interventionist," who has a formula in these cases.

documents.title: One Missed Call
documents.tagline: What will it sound like when you die?
documents.overview: Several people start receiving voice-mails from their future selves -- messages which include the date, time, and some of the details of their deaths.
documents.plot:
A paramedic rescues a young girl from the blazing Saint Luke's hospital before unsuccessfully inquiring about her mother's whereabouts. Sometime afterwards, undergraduate Shelley Baum hears her cat meowing near her house's koi pond. After she heads over to investigate, a hand appears and drowns her and her cat. Days later, college students Beth Raymond and Leann Cole discuss Shelley's funeral. Leann's cellphone rings in a lullaby-esque ringtone, with a call from Shelley. She opens it to an eerie voicemail of herself, dated June 12 at 10:17 PM. Subsequently, suffering from disturbing hallucinations, she calls Beth while returning from a study session. Beth rushes to her location but arrives just as Leann falls off an overpass and is struck by a train. A red candy pops out of her mouth, and her severed hand dials a number on her phone. At Leann's funeral, her ex-boyfriend Brian Sousa departs after experiencing hallucinations. Outside a coffee shop, he shows Beth Leann's post-mortem voicemail, dated minutes away. An acetylene tank explosion from the adjacent construction site launches debris into the air, and a rebar impales Brian's torso. A red candy is ejected from his mouth, and he collapses.
The next day, Beth meets police detective Jack Andrews, who mentions that his sister Jean interned with Shelley at Saint Luke's and died herself two days prior. They determine the events are interrelated and he provides his contact card. Beth consoles her friend Taylor Anthony, who is distraught by a premonitory feeling of being the next victim, so Beth removes the batteries from both their cellphones to disable them. That night, Taylor's cellphone rings; she opens it to see a video of her apparent demise. The following morning, Jack and Beth research geriatric nurse Marie Layton, originator of the calls, and find the autopsy report of her eldest daughter Ellie, who died from an acute asthmatic episode. The file, mentioning "no bruising but evidence of past scars" with an attached CPS file for further consultation, indicates that Jean, a psychiatric nurse, questioned Marie at Saint Luke's and noted nine admissions between April and May for Ellie and her sister Laurel, concerning several causes, leading Beth to assume that Marie had FDIA.
Meanwhile, TV producer Ted Summers, who approached Taylor earlier, prepares to record her exorcism, explaining that spiritual energy operates in the same electromagnetic spectrum as light/microwaves and is therefore transmissible via cellular phones from which it manifests as hallucinations. Noticing the show's advertisement on TV, Beth races to the site, arriving to an unseen force fatally choking Taylor. Her phone then sounds with a voicemail dated for tomorrow. Taking Beth home, Jack learns about her past in which her mother was abusive towards her (in particular burning her daughter with cigarettes), and her father, aware of his wife's abuse, hanged himself in their house's attic.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG IV

documents.title: The Village
documents.tagline: There is no turning back
documents.overview: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.
documents.plot:
A small remote village, apparently 19th-century, lives in fear of nameless humanoid creatures, known only as "Those We Do Not Speak Of", that inhabit the surrounding woods. Staffed watchtowers and tall poles with oil lamps line the village perimeter for protection. The color red is banned, as it attracts the creatures.
Following a young villager's death due to illness, Lucius Hunt is denied the elders' permission to travel through the woods and retrieve medical supplies from "the towns" to avoid similar tragedies. Later, Lucius's widowed mother, Alice, questions his desire to visit "the towns", which the elders describe as wicked. The elders appear to have secrets, and each keeps a locked black box containing unknown items. Lucius secretly ventures into the woods, though he later tells the elders and claims it was safe. Soon after, skinned animal carcasses appear in the village. One night, the creatures enter the village, leaving red paint splashes on people's doors as a warning.
Elder Edward Walker's daughter Kitty is attracted to Lucius, but he loves Ivy, Kitty's visually impaired and empathic younger sister. Kitty marries another, which allows Ivy and Lucius to become betrothed. Before they can marry, Noah Percy, a young man with an apparent developmental disability, stabs Lucius out of jealousy, seriously wounding him. As the elders consider Noah's fate, he remains locked in a small building.
Edward defies the other elders by sending Ivy, accompanied by two young men, to the towns to retrieve medicine for Lucius. Before she leaves, Edward reveals that the creatures are actually the elders disguised as monsters to deter younger members from leaving. The skinned animal remains were not part of their plan, since one of the village elders took their lie too far and must be stopped. In the woods, the boys become frightened and abandon Ivy. She continues on alone and is stalked by a creature, which she tricks into fatally falling into a deep hole. Unbeknownst to Ivy, the creature was Noah, wearing a costume. Meanwhile, Edward and his wife Tabitha unlock their box, which contains photos of themselves and the other elders when they were younger. The group is standing outside a modern-day counseling center, revealing that it is actually the late 20th or early 21st century.
Ivy climbs over a high wall. On the other side, she encounters Kevin, a Walker Wildlife Reserve park ranger, who is shocked that she came from the woods. Ivy gives him a list of medicines she must acquire.
It is revealed that Edward, a former history professor, founded the village over two decades earlier. He had recruited people he met at a grief counseling clinic, hoping to isolate themselves from societal violence. Edward's family fortune funds the wildlife reserve, built the village inside it, and paid off the government to make it a no-fly zone.
Ivy returns to the village with the medication obtained from Kevin, never seeing the modern world.

documents.title: The Wedding Date
documents.tagline: Love doesn't come cheap.
documents.overview: With the wedding of her younger sister fast approaching, Kat Ellis faces the undesirable prospect of traveling alone to London for the ceremony. While this is bad enough, Jeffrey, the man who left her as they moved closer to marriage, happens to be the groom's best man. Determined to show everyone -- most of all Jeffrey -- that her romantic life is as full and thrilling as ever, Kat hires a charming male escort as her date.

documents.title: The Weather Man
documents.tagline: Dave Spritz is about to take his best shot . . . at life
documents.overview: A Chicago weather man, separated from his wife and children, debates whether professional and personal success are mutually exclusive.
documents.plot:
The Weather Man is a 2005 American dark comedy-drama directed by Gore Verbinski and written by Steve Conrad. Nicolas Cage stars as a Chicago television weatherman in the midst of a midlife crisis, with Michael Caine as his father and Hope Davis as his estranged wife, and Gemmenne de la Peña and Nicholas Hoult as his children. It was released on October 28, 2005.

David Spritz is a well-paid weatherman on a Chicago news program, but he commands little respect: strangers regularly hurl fast food at him in the street, perhaps, he suspects, out of resentment at his easy, lucrative job. He also lives in the shadow of his father, Robert Spritzel, a Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist who is quietly disappointed by his son's inability to grow up and take charge of his life and his children. His marriage to Noreen has collapsed, and he struggles to connect with his children, Shelly and Mike. When Robert is diagnosed with lymphoma and given months to live, David's sense of failure deepens. He takes up archery, finding in it a rare source of focus and calm, and he tries, mostly in vain, to live up to his father's advice that the right thing and the hard thing are often the same.

Hoping to prove himself to his father and win back Noreen, David auditions for a weatherman position on the national morning show Hello America, a job that would quadruple his salary but require moving to New York. He takes Shelly with him to the audition, bonding with her as he helps her find a new wardrobe. While he is away, he learns that Mike has fought off his counselor, who made sexual advances toward him. Despite his anxiety and a night of heavy drinking, David impresses the producers and is offered the job. Back home, he strikes Noreen's new boyfriend, Russ, and confronts and beats the counselor.

At a "living funeral" arranged for Robert, David asks Noreen to reconcile and move to New York with him, but she has decided to marry Russ. In a final conversation, David breaks down, and Robert gently tells him that he still has time to clear the garbage out of his life before he dies. Months later, David has taken the job and moved to New York. People no longer throw things at him, which he wryly suspects may have something to do with the bow he now carries.

The film grossed about $19 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive; Rotten Tomatoes reports 60% approval, with a consensus praising its fine performances and dry, dark humor, and Metacritic gave it 61 out of 100.

documents.title: Something's Gotta Give
documents.tagline: Schmucks are people too.
documents.overview: Harry Sanborn is an aged music industry exec with a fondness for younger women like Marin, his latest trophy girlfriend. Things get a little awkward when Harry suffers a heart attack at the home of Marin's mother, Erica. Left in the care of Erica and his doctor, a love triangle starts to take shape.
documents.plot: When perpetually single, aging music industry exec Harry Sanborn, and his latest trophy girlfriend, Marin, arrive at her mother's beach house in the Hamptons, they find that her mother, playwright Erica Barry, also plans to stay for the weekend. Erica is scandalized by the relationship and Harry's sexist ways. But when Harry has a heart attack while there, and the doctor prescribes bedrest, his only option is to stay at the Barry home. Left in the care of Erica and his doctor, a love triangle starts to take shape.

documents.title: Australia
documents.tagline: Welcome to Australia!
documents.overview: Set in northern Australia before World War II, an English aristocrat who inherits a sprawling ranch reluctantly pacts with a stock-man in order to protect her new property from a takeover plot. As the pair drive 2,000 head of cattle over unforgiving landscape, they experience the bombing of Darwin by Japanese forces firsthand.

documents.title: In the Valley of Elah
documents.tagline: Sometimes finding the truth is easier than facing it.
documents.overview: A career officer and his wife work with a police detective to uncover the truth behind their son's disappearance following his return from a tour of duty in Iraq.
documents.plot:
On November 1, 2004, Hank Deerfield, a gravel trucker and retired military police sergeant living in Monroe, Tennessee with his wife Joan, is notified that his son Mike, a soldier recently returned from Iraq, has gone missing. Hank drives to Mike's base in New Mexico to look for him; leaving home, he helps a school custodian raise the American flag correctly. At Fort Rudd, Hank meets his son's squad, and secretly takes Mike's cell phone from his belongings. Watching videos recovered from the phone, he attempts to report Mike's disappearance to police detective Emily Sanders who is unable to help out. He reaches out to a friend formerly at Army CID, also without success.
When Mike's burned and dismembered body is discovered, Fort Rudd claims jurisdiction over the investigation, believing a pipe found under Mike's mattress and recent heroin smuggling arrests on base point to a drug-related murder. Hank persuades Sanders to show him the crime scene, and realizes a green car spotted at the scene was actually blue. Belittled by her male colleagues, Sanders convinces the local sheriff to pursue the investigation, and Mike's squadmate SPC Gordon Bonner reaches out to Hank.
After viewing her son's remains, Joan returns home and receives a package Mike mailed to himself, which Hank urges her not to open. Mike's credit card history leads Sanders and Hank to a restaurant where he ate with at least two others shortly before his death. Sanders gets copies of sworn statements from Mike's squad by Army investigators, who prevent her from interviewing them herself. She dines with Hank and he tells her young son the story of the Biblical David's battle with Goliath in the Valley of Elah.
Hank learns that Mike and Corporal Steve Penning were kicked out of a strip club the night Mike was killed. Penning, Bonner, and Specialist Ennis Long admit to Sanders they lied in their statements, and after Mike got the four of them kicked out of the club, he fought Bonner in the parking lot then paid the bill at the restaurant. The group visited a prostitute before leaving Mike, who was looking to buy drugs. Hank refuses to believe Mike's fellow soldiers could be involved in his death.
Hank and the police determine that Private Robert Ortiz, who is AWOL, has a history of drug smuggling and a blue car. Following the police as they raid his residence, Hank subdues the fleeing Ortiz and beats him until detectives intervene. Ortiz is arrested, but Bonner is found hanged with Mike's grandfather's watch in his pocket. Sanders concludes that Bonner, who also owned a blue car, killed Mike. She learns that Angie, a soldier's wife who came to her for help, has been murdered by her husband.
Hank sends his son's remains home and Penning helps jump-start his truck, reminiscing about Mike. Sanders matches Penning's handwriting to the signature on Mike's last credit card statement, proving they used his credit card at the restaurant.

documents.title: Ken Park
documents.tagline: Who are you?
documents.overview: Ken Park focuses on several teenagers and their tormented home lives. Shawn seems to be the most conventional. Tate is brimming with psychotic rage; Claude is habitually harassed by his brutish father and coddled, rather uncomfortably, by his enormously pregnant mother. Peaches looks after her devoutly religious father, but yearns for freedom. They're all rather tight, or so they claim.
documents.plot:
Ken Park is a 2002 psychological teen film directed by Larry Clark and Edward Lachman and written by Harmony Korine, who built the screenplay from Clark's journals and stories after Clark became dissatisfied with his own draft. Set in Visalia, California, it portrays the abusive and dysfunctional lives of four teenagers connected by the suicide of an acquaintance, the title character. James Ransone plays Tate, Tiffany Limos plays Peaches, James Bullard plays Shawn and Stephen Jasso plays Claude, with Adam Chubbuck as Ken Park and a supporting cast including Maeve Quinlan, Amanda Plummer, Wade Williams, Julio Oscar Mechoso and Richard Riehle. Although planned for digital video, it was shot on 35 mm film.

The film opens with Ken Park, a teenage skateboarder, riding into a skate park, setting up a camcorder and shooting himself. His death frames the story, which cuts between four other teenagers who knew him and the failures of the adults around them. Shawn, the most stable of the four, is secretly having an affair with his girlfriend's mother, while her family remains unaware. Claude endures physical and emotional abuse from his alcoholic father, who despises him for not being masculine enough, while his pregnant mother does little to protect him; after a disturbing drunken advance by his father, Claude runs away from home. Peaches lives with her intensely religious widowed father, who sees her as the embodiment of her dead mother; when he discovers her with her boyfriend Curtis, he beats the boy, punishes her harshly and forces her into a disturbing mock wedding ritual. Tate, a volatile and sadistic youth who lives with grandparents he resents, eventually murders them over petty grievances, records a confession explaining his actions for the police, and is arrested. The separate strands converge only at the end, when Shawn, Claude and Peaches come together, and a final flashback returns to Ken in the days before his death, revealing that his girlfriend was pregnant.

Ken Park premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in 2002 but has not been released in the United States since, which Clark attributed to the producer's failure to secure music rights. It was refused classification in Australia in 2003 because of its graphic sexual content and depictions of underage sexual activity, and police shut down a protest screening in Sydney hosted by critic Margaret Pomeranz. Critical reception was mixed, with a 46% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Van Helsing: The London Assignment
documents.overview: It tells of the events before the film, in which monster hunter Gabriel Van Helsing travels to London to investigate a series of horrific, and decidedly supernatural murders, being committed by the mad scientist Dr. Jekyll, in the form of his evil alter-ego, Mr. Hyde.

documents.title: Venom
documents.tagline: He never hurt a soul until the day he died.
documents.overview: A group of teenagers fear for their lives in the swamps of Louisiana, chased by Mr. Jangles, a man possessed by 13 evil souls, and now relentless in his pursuit of new victims.
documents.plot:
Venom is a 2005 American supernatural slasher film directed by Jim Gillespie, who reunited with screenwriter Kevin Williamson after their collaboration on I Know What You Did Last Summer. The ensemble cast features Agnes Bruckner as Eden Sinclair, Jonathan Jackson as Eric, Laura Ramsey as Rachel, Meagan Good as CeCe, D. J. Cotrona as Sean, Rick Cramer as tow truck driver Ray Sawyer and Method Man as Deputy Turner. The film was based on Backwater, an unproduced survival horror video game designed by John Zuur Platten and Flint Dille, and was shot in Louisiana, in Amite, Choctaw, Hammond and New Orleans.

In a small town, high school senior Eden and her friends spend their time at the local burger joint, where Sean's father Ray, a gruff tow truck driver, picks up an order. That night a Creole woman, CeCe's grandmother, who has just dug up a mysterious briefcase, swerves to avoid Ray's truck on a bridge and nearly plunges over the edge. Ray rescues her, but at her desperate urging he reaches back for the case as the car sinks into the water, and snakes burst out of it and bite him repeatedly. Both Ray and the old woman die. In the morgue, Ray rises again, kills the coroner and a police officer, and sets out on a murderous rampage through the teenagers' circle with the tools of his trade, including chains and a crowbar. CeCe, who took a charm from her grandmother's body, explains that the snakes contained evil that her grandmother had drawn out of wicked men to purify their souls, and that this evil has now possessed Ray. As their friends are picked off one by one, the survivors take refuge in the grandmother's house, which is protected by voodoo spells, and search for a way to destroy the seemingly unstoppable killer.

Venom was released by Miramax Films' Dimension Films label on September 16, 2005, the last Dimension release before the Walt Disney Company sold the label to The Weinstein Company. Its timing, days after Hurricane Katrina devastated southeast Louisiana, made the film seem unfortunately topical, and it was a box-office failure. Critics gave it negative reviews; it holds a 13% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it a voodoo horror film without the mojo whose unimaginative rampage quickly lulls viewers to sleep.

documents.title: Perfect Stranger
documents.tagline: How Far Would You Go To Keep A Secret?
documents.overview: A journalist goes undercover to ferret out businessman Harrison Hill as her best friend's killer. Posing as one of his temps, she enters into a game of online cat-and-mouse.

documents.title: Cloverfield
documents.tagline: Some thing has found us.
documents.overview: Five young New Yorkers throw their friend a going-away party the night that a monster the size of a skyscraper descends upon the city. Told from the point of view of their video camera, the film is a document of their attempt to survive the most surreal, horrifying event of their lives.
documents.plot:
Cloverfield is a 2008 monster horror film directed by Matt Reeves and produced by J.J. Abrams' production company Bad Robot Productions, in association with Universal Pictures.

The film begins on March 12, 2008, in New York City, where we meet our protagonist, Rob Hawkins (played by Michael Stuhlbarg), a young man who is preparing to leave for his job at a financial firm in Tokyo. However, before he can depart, he receives an unexpected phone call from his brother, Jason (played by T.J. Miller), who informs him that their father has died.

As Rob tries to make sense of the situation, we are introduced to other main characters: Marlena Heisencutter (played by Lizzy Caplan), a friend of Rob's who is also preparing for her own trip abroad; Matty Reynolds (played by Mike Vogel), a friend of Jason's who is trying to get in touch with his brother; and Hud (played by Adam Brody), a friend of the group who is initially hesitant to join them on their adventure.

The group decides to embark on a road trip from New York City to New Jersey, where they plan to meet up with Jason. However, as they drive through the city, they notice that something is amiss - buildings are damaged, cars are overturned, and there is a sense of chaos in the air.

As they continue their journey, they come across a massive monster, known as "Cloverfield," which is wreaking havoc on the city. The creature is enormous, with glowing red eyes and a powerful roar that can be heard for miles. The group soon realizes that Cloverfield is not just a mindless beast - it's a highly intelligent and destructive force that seems to be targeting specific locations.

As the group tries to escape the monster's path, they begin to uncover clues about its origins and motivations. They discover that Cloverfield is an extraterrestrial creature that has been awakened by human activity in the city. The creature is drawn to the sounds of human communication, which it uses to navigate and hunt its prey.

Throughout the film, the group faces numerous challenges as they try to survive the monster's attacks. Along the way, they also experience personal struggles and conflicts, including romantic tensions and family drama.

As the night wears on, the group finds themselves trapped in a deserted warehouse, where they are forced to confront Cloverfield head-on. In a tense and suspenseful climax, they manage to fend off the creature long enough for Rob's brother Jason to escape with his life.

The film ends with Rob, Marlena, Matty, and Hud watching as Jason drives away from the city, leaving behind the devastation and destruction caused by Cloverfield. As they reflect on their experience, we see a series of news reports and footage of the monster's rampage, which serves as a reminder that the world is not always a safe or predictable place.

Overall, Cloverfounder is a tense and thrilling horror film that explores themes of friendship, survival, and the human condition in the face of catastrophic events.

documents.title: Dan in Real Life
documents.tagline: Something's happening to Dan. It's confusing. It's awkward. It's family.
documents.overview: Advice columnist, Dan Burns is an expert on relationships, but somehow struggles to succeed as a brother, a son and a single parent to three precocious daughters. Things get even more complicated when Dan finds out that the woman he falls in love with is actually his brother's new girlfriend.
documents.plot:
Dan Burns is a newspaper advice columnist, author, widower, and single parent to his three daughters, living in North Jersey. Dan and his daughters take a weekend trip to the oceanside Rhode Island home of Dan's parents for an annual family gathering. In attendance are Dan's older brother and sister with their families, as well as Dan's younger brother Mitch, who is known for his carefree lifestyle and robust dating history.
The morning after arriving in Rhode Island, Dan meets Marie in a bookshop and the two are instantly attracted to each other. They spend the morning sharing a pastry over heartfelt conversation, although she gently warns him that she has a new boyfriend and leaves.
Dan returns to his parents' house and announces that he has "met someone,” whereupon the whole family encourages him to "go for it.” Within minutes of this, Mitch introduces his new girlfriend, who turns out to be Marie. The family, and particularly Dan’s daughters, take an instant liking to Marie. Dan is disheartened upon seeing Mitch’s feelings for Marie, and resists his father's advice about looking for love after his wife’s death four years earlier. To avoid awkwardness, Dan and Marie decide against telling the family of their meeting, but spend the next few days in frustration as they realize their instantaneous connection.
Dan butts heads with his middle daughter, Cara, who grows more exasperated with Dan's dismissal of her relationship with her high school boyfriend Marty, whom Cara claims to have fallen in "love" with in three days. Upon his mother's insistence, Dan reluctantly agrees to a blind date with his siblings' once unattractive childhood friend, Ruthie "Pig Face" Draper, who has since grown into a beautiful and successful physician. Mitch and Marie join them for a double date and Dan delights in making Marie jealous of him and Ruthie.
Tension grows between Dan and Marie, culminating at the family's football game and talent show, where Dan plays guitar as Mitch sings "Let My Love Open the Door"; during the bridge and unbeknownst to the family, Dan sings to Marie. Marie, who has been reading Dan's written work over the weekend, tearfully confesses that since meeting Dan she has realized her feelings for Mitch are platonic and cannot bear to keep pretending otherwise. The next morning, Marie breaks up with Mitch and leaves.
Marie later calls Dan and reveals that she is still in town, and they meet at a bowling alley to talk. The meeting evolves into a date and finally a passionate kiss, interrupted when Dan's entire family arrives to bowl and are shocked to find them. Angry and betrayed, Mitch punches Dan in the face and Marie hurries out in tears.
Humiliated, Dan's three daughters angrily turn on him. Mitch, despite his apparent devastation earlier, forgives Dan and immediately rebounds with Ruthie, suggesting that his feelings for Marie had not been very strong to begin with.

documents.title: Coach Carter
documents.tagline: It begins on the street. It ends here.
documents.overview: Based on a true story, in which Richmond High School head basketball coach Ken Carter made headlines in 1999 for benching his undefeated team due to poor academic results.
documents.plot:
Coach Carter is a biographical sports drama film released in 2005, directed by Thomas Carter and starring Samuel L. Jackson as Ken Carter, a high school basketball coach.

The movie is based on the true story of Ken Carter, who coached the Richmond High School basketball team in Richmond, California, in 1999-2000. The film begins with Coach Carter, a former NBA player, taking over as the new head coach of the Richmond High School basketball team. He is determined to teach his players not only about basketball but also about life and responsibility.

Initially, the team struggles due to poor attendance, lack of motivation, and behavioral issues. Coach Carter sets out to change this by implementing a strict set of rules and expectations for his players. He requires them to maintain a minimum GPA, attend classes regularly, and participate in community service. The players are initially resistant to these new rules, but Coach Carter's firm but fair approach eventually starts to take effect.

As the season progresses, the team begins to improve on the court, winning several games and gaining confidence. However, off the court, the players continue to struggle with their personal lives, including poverty, family problems, and gang involvement. Coach Carter becomes a mentor and father figure to his players, helping them to overcome their challenges and find a better path in life.

One of the key players, Kenyon Stone (played by Rob Brown), is particularly struggling with his own demons. He comes from a troubled home and has been involved with gangs. Coach Carter takes Kenyon under his wing, teaching him about responsibility and self-discipline. Through their relationship, Coach Carter helps Kenyon to turn his life around, earning a college scholarship and eventually becoming a successful businessman.

As the season reaches its climax, the team faces off against their arch-rivals, and Coach Carter's players must come together to overcome their personal struggles and win the game. In a thrilling finale, the team emerges victorious, but more importantly, they have learned valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of education.

The movie ends with Coach Carter reflecting on the season and the progress his players have made. He is proud of what he has accomplished, not just as a coach but also as a mentor and role model. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as the players look to the future, armed with the knowledge and skills they have gained under Coach Carter's guidance.

Overall, Coach Carter is an inspiring true story about the power of sports to transform lives and communities. The movie features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Samuel L. Jackson as Coach Carter, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of a complex and dedicated coach.

documents.title: The Punisher
documents.tagline: There is no justice, there is only revenge.
documents.overview: When undercover FBI agent Frank Castle's wife and son are slaughtered, he becomes 'the Punisher' -- a ruthless vigilante willing to go to any length to avenge his family.
documents.plot:
The Punisher is a 2004 superhero film directed by Jonathan Hensleigh and starring Thomas Jane as Frank Castle, aka The Punisher.

The movie begins with Frank Castle, a former Marine, who witnesses his entire family being brutally murdered in front of him by a group of armed robbers. This traumatic event sets off a chain reaction that drives Frank to seek revenge against those responsible for the senseless violence and death he witnessed.

Frank's quest for vengeance leads him to become The Punisher, a vigilante determined to punish those who have escaped justice. He starts by targeting organized crime groups, particularly the Russian mafia, which is led by Kravinoff (John Malkovich). Frank's actions attract the attention of the police department and the FBI, who are initially unaware that he is a vigilante.

As The Punisher continues his crusade against organized crime, he becomes increasingly isolated from society. He adopts a new identity for himself, using a fake name and creating a persona that strikes fear into the hearts of those around him. Frank's actions also attract the attention of Elektra Natchios (Jennifer Garner), a skilled martial artist and assassin who is initially unaware of The Punisher's true identity.

Throughout the movie, Frank's character undergoes significant development as he grapples with his own morality and the consequences of his actions. He begins to question whether his quest for vengeance is truly just or if it has become an all-consuming obsession that is destroying him from within.

As The Punisher delves deeper into the world of organized crime, he discovers a sinister plot by Kravinoff to sell nuclear warheads on the black market. Frank must use his skills and resources to stop Kravinoff's operation and prevent a catastrophic disaster.

The movie culminates in an intense showdown between The Punisher and Kravinoff, with Frank ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars. In the aftermath of the battle, Elektra finally discovers The Punisher's true identity, and the two share a moment of mutual understanding and respect for each other's skills and motivations.

The Punisher ends on a somber note, with Frank reflecting on the cost of his actions and the toll they have taken on his life. He realizes that his quest for vengeance has become an all-consuming force that threatens to destroy him from within. The movie concludes with Frank walking away from the city, leaving behind the chaos and destruction he has caused in pursuit of justice.

Overall, The Punisher is a gritty and intense action film that explores themes of revenge, morality, and the blurred lines between good and evil.

documents.title: Airport '77
documents.tagline: Flight 23 has crashed in the Bermuda Triangle... passengers still alive, trapped underwater...
documents.overview: Flight 23 has crashed in the Bermuda Triangle after a hijacking gone wrong. Now the surviving passengers must brave panic, slow leaks, oxygen depletion, and more while attempting a daring plan, all while 200 feet underwater.
documents.plot:
Airport '77 is a disaster film directed by Jerry Jameson, released in 1977 by Universal Pictures. The movie takes place at Washington National Airport and revolves around a series of catastrophic events that unfold on a fateful day.

The story begins with the introduction of several characters, including Steve McCauley (Burt Reynolds), a former test pilot who has retired from flying due to a near-fatal accident. Steve is now working as an airport security inspector, tasked with ensuring the safety of air traffic at Washington National Airport.

As the day unfolds, a series of strange occurrences start to happen. A small plane carrying a group of passengers and crew crashes on the runway, causing a massive fire that blocks the entire airport. The authorities are initially unable to respond effectively due to the chaos caused by the crash, leading to further accidents and mishaps.

Meanwhile, Steve is dealing with his own personal demons, including a troubled relationship with his girlfriend, Elaine (Susan Blakely). As the day progresses, Steve becomes increasingly frustrated with the incompetence of the airport's management and the lack of preparedness for emergencies.

As the situation spirals out of control, Steve takes matters into his own hands, using his flying skills to rescue those trapped in the burning plane. He also teams up with a young air traffic controller, Mark (Jack Warden), who helps him navigate the chaos and coordinate the response efforts.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the characters face numerous challenges, including treacherous weather conditions, equipment failures, and human error. The film's climax features an intense sequence of events, including a dramatic rescue mission and a confrontation with the airport's corrupt management.

Ultimately, Steve emerges as a hero, having saved countless lives and brought order to the chaotic situation. As he reflects on the day's events, Steve comes to terms with his past mistakes and finds closure with Elaine.

Airport '77 is an action-packed disaster film that explores themes of personal responsibility, teamwork, and redemption. The movie features impressive aerial sequences, suspenseful plot twists, and a strong performance from Burt Reynolds as the protagonist. While some critics have panned the film's predictability and lack of originality, Airport '77 remains a beloved classic among fans of disaster movies and action films.

Overall, Airport '77 is an entertaining and thrilling ride that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its memorable characters, intense plot developments, and heart-pumping action sequences, this movie is sure to delight audiences who enjoy disaster films and adventure stories.

documents.title: Ruby & Quentin
documents.overview: After hiding his loot and getting thrown in jail, Ruby, a brooding outlaw encounters Quentin, a dim-witted and garrulous giant who befriends him. After Quentin botches a solo escape attempt, they make a break together. Unable to shake the clumsy Quentin Ruby is forced to take him along as he pursues his former partners in crime to avenge the death of the woman he loved and get to the money.
documents.plot:
Ruby & Quentin (French: Tais-toi!, "Shut up!") is a French crime comedy caper of 2003 directed by Francis Veber. Jean Reno plays Ruby, a taciturn gangster bent on revenge, and Gérard Depardieu plays Quentin, a dim-witted, endlessly talkative petty thief, with Richard Berry as the detective Vernet, André Dussollier as the prison psychiatrist, Jean-Pierre Malo as the crime boss Vogel and Leonor Varela in the dual role of Katia and Sandra.

Quentin bungles a hold-up at a currency exchange booth, asks the cashier for directions to the nearest bank and is arrested after ducking into a cinema showing Ice Age and settling down to enjoy the film. Ruby, meanwhile, worked for Vogel and had an affair with his boss's wife; after Vogel killed her, Ruby stole his loot in revenge and was caught hiding it. In prison he refuses to eat or speak, worrying the psychiatrist but failing to fool the investigating detective. Quentin, whose ceaseless chatter has driven every previous cellmate to violence, is placed in Ruby's cell as an experiment. He instantly adores his silent companion, whose distant gaze reminds him of the horses he tended as a stable boy.

Ruby fakes a suicide attempt to reach the prison infirmary, and Quentin copies him to end up in the next bed. Ruby bribes a nurse in Vogel's pay to help him escape, but Quentin has his own plan involving a drunken old friend who drives a crane, and the two end up on the run together. Ruby tries again and again to get rid of his clinging companion, but every attempt fails. Pursued by Vogel's bodyguards, they steal and lose a series of cars, break into the mansion of a tiny former jockey and end up in his wife's Chanel suits, and swap clothes with two bigots. Quentin snaps Ruby's dislocated shoulder back into place and keeps stealing police cars. In the derelict bistro in his home village, where Quentin dreams of opening a café, they meet a homeless woman who looks just like Vogel's dead wife; Ruby, smitten, gives her money and a fresh start in a hotel. The pair talk their way into Vogel's hideout, where a shoot-out leaves Vogel incapacitated and Quentin apparently dying. To his own surprise Ruby weeps for him, and Quentin tricks him into promising to open the bistro together once he recovers.

The film was released in French cinemas on 22 October 2003.

documents.title: Futurama: Bender's Big Score
documents.tagline: Just when you thought it was safe to watch something else!
documents.overview: The Planet Express crew return from cancellation, only to be robbed blind by hideous "sprunging" scam artists.  Things go from bad to worse when the scammers hack Bender, start traveling through time, and take Earth over entirely!  Will the crew be able to save the day, or will Bender's larcenous tendencies and their general incompetence doom them all?

documents.title: Meet the Spartans
documents.tagline: The bigger the hit, the harder they fall.
documents.overview: The heroic Leonidas, armed with nothing but leather underwear and a cape, leads a ragtag group of 13 Spartans to defend their homeland against the invading Persians (whose ranks include Ghost Rider, Rocky Balboa, the Transformers, and a hunchbacked Paris Hilton). No one is safe when the Spartans take on the biggest icons in pop culture!
documents.plot:
Meet the Spartans is a 2008 American parody film written and directed by Jason Friedberg and Aaron Seltzer. Chiefly a spoof of the 2006 film 300, it also mocks many other films, television shows, celebrities and pop culture events of the time, in the manner of the pair's Date Movie and Epic Movie. The cast includes Sean Maguire, Carmen Electra, Ken Davitian, Kevin Sorbo and Diedrich Bader.

A Spartan elder inspects three babies, rejecting an ugly talking ogre baby, while another is adopted by Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie and the muscular Leonidas is accepted and trained for kingship. Cast into the wild, Leonidas survives the winter and hunts down a gangsta penguin named Mumble, then returns to be crowned in a penguin-skin hat and wins Margo, who gives him the combination to her armoured chastity belt. Years later, a Persian messenger arrives with the Spartan politician Traitoro to demand Sparta's submission to King Xerxes, and when the envoy flirts with Margo, Leonidas kicks him into a pit, followed by his guards and assorted celebrities. Warned by the Oracle, portrayed as Ugly Betty, that he will die if he goes to war, Leonidas marches for Thermopylae anyway with just thirteen soldiers who met the army's stringent standards, including the Captain, his son Sonio and the unfit Dilio. A deformed Paris Hilton, rejected as a soldier, knows of a secret goat path. The Spartans beat Xerxes's Immortals in a dance contest and drive them off a cliff, refuse Xerxes's bribe of a trip to the Palms Hotel and Casino and defeat the Persians in a "Yo Momma" contest in which Dilio is blinded. Hilton betrays them to Xerxes, while in Sparta Margo battles the treacherous Traitoro in a Spider-Man 3 spoof and defeats him with a hand vacuum. In the final battle, Rocky Balboa kills Sonio, the Captain falls to Xerxes, and Xerxes uses a "Transformer Cube" to become the giant Xerxestron, but trips over his own extension cord and crushes Leonidas and the remaining Spartans. The blind Dilio brings the news home, and a year later leads a larger army that marches the wrong way and ends up in Malibu. The film closes with the characters singing "I Will Survive" on the American Idol stage.

Released by 20th Century Fox on January 25, 2008, Meet the Spartans opened at number one in the United States, and grossed about $84 million worldwide on a $30 million budget. Critics panned it, giving it a 2% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and it has appeared on several lists of the worst films ever made.

documents.title: Duplex
documents.tagline: Alex and Nancy finally found their dream home...and then they moved in.
documents.overview: When a young couple buys their dream home, they have no idea what the sweet little old lady upstairs is going to put them through!

documents.title: 2001: A Space Travesty
documents.tagline: The most outer spaced-out comedy ever!
documents.overview: When odd reports are received through official channels stating that the President of the United States is being held captive on a secret international moon base called Vegan and that he has been replaced on Earth by a clone, the US Marshall Service immediately sends their 'best' man, Dix, on the mission.
documents.plot:
2001: A Space Travesty is a 2000 satirical science fiction comedy film directed by Allan A. Goldstein. Leslie Nielsen stars as Marshal Richard "Dick" Dix, a bumbling special agent, with Ophélie Winter, Peter Egan, Ezio Greggio, Alexandra Kamp and Verona Pooth in supporting roles. Despite its title, the film parodies 2001: A Space Odyssey in only a few sequences, aiming its spoofs at a wide range of science fiction films and at American politics of the era. It was filmed in Canada as an international co-production.

Dix, a special agent, ends a terrorist hostage situation at a fast-food restaurant in his own chaotic fashion, to the annoyance of the police chief. At headquarters, his superior introduces him to Cassandra Menage, who explains that the President of the United States, a thinly veiled caricature of Bill Clinton who is never named, has been kidnapped and replaced by a clone. Dix is sent by space shuttle to Vegan, a base on the Moon where the cloning is believed to have taken place, causing mayhem throughout the journey.

On arrival, Dix is greeted at security by Lieutenant Bradford Shitzu and is soon confronted by strange incidents involving the aliens who live in the colony. He shares quarters with Captain Valentino DiPasquale, played by Greggio, and sets out to question the main suspect, Dr. Griffin Pratt, who gives him a tour of his cloning facility. Along the way he meets the alluring scientist Dr. Uschi Künstler and attends a party where the suspects are gathered. Stumbling from one misunderstanding to another, and accompanied by a constant stream of sight gags, slapstick and sexual innuendo, Dix tries to uncover the conspiracy behind the cloning, locate the real president and bring him safely back to Earth, while thwarting a plot that threatens the leadership of the free world.

The film received poor reviews. The website Need Coffee acknowledged Nielsen's deadpan comic style but recommended the film only to viewers in the mood for silly, puerile humor, while Jason James of The Nut Gallery gave it one star out of five. It was one of a number of broad spoof comedies that Nielsen headlined in the years following the success of The Naked Gun films, trading on his deadpan persona.

documents.title: 36th Precinct
documents.tagline: Revenge is not justice.
documents.overview: The film takes place in Paris, where two cops are competing for the vacant seat of chief of police while in the middle of a search for a gang of violent thieves. The movie is directed by Olivier Marchal, a former police officer who spent 12 years with the French police before creating this story, which is taken in part from real facts that happened during the 1980s in France.
documents.plot:
36th Precinct (French: 36 Quai des Orfèvres), also known as The 36, is a 2004 French crime film directed by Olivier Marchal, a former police officer. Named after the historic address of the Paris Judicial Police headquarters on the Île de la Cité, it stars Daniel Auteuil as Léo Vrinks and Gérard Depardieu as Denis Klein, rival police commanders competing for the post of chief of the Paris criminal police, with Roschdy Zem and Valeria Golino. It is loosely based on real 1980s events.

Vrinks, head of the BRI, and Klein, head of the BRB, both hope to succeed their chief, Robert Mancini, who is being promoted, and the job will likely go to whoever catches a violent gang of armored-car robbers. Vrinks's wife, Camille, was once Klein's lover. Vrinks is an effective detective with loyal officers and shady informants, while the heavy-drinking Klein is less capable and less scrupulous. Vrinks's methods backfire when an informant on weekend release, Hugo Silien, tricks him into driving the getaway car while he kills a gangster who once testified against him. In exchange for Vrinks's silence and alibi, Silien gives up the gang's members and hideout. During the stakeout, a drunken Klein breaks procedure and alerts the robbers; most are arrested, but Vrinks's best friend is killed in the gunfire.

Learning from a prostitute who witnessed Silien's crime that Vrinks was involved, Klein ensures that his rival is prosecuted, making Vrinks's evidence inadmissible and clearing himself of blame. When Silien later meets Camille to offer her money, Klein, tapping her phone, orders his men to force her car off the road despite the danger, and both die in the crash. Klein then fires Silien's gun into Camille's body and his own into Silien's to make it appear he acted in self-defense. Seven years later, Vrinks leaves prison and reunites with his daughter. Klein now heads the criminal police. A former colleague, Titi, is beaten into a coma by Bruno, a thug Vrinks's team once humiliated in a mock execution. Vrinks confronts Klein at a police ball and urges him to kill himself, but when Klein follows him out shouting threats, Bruno, lying in wait, shoots Klein dead, apparently having been given Klein's name by Titi. Vrinks and his daughter leave to start a new life abroad.

Marchal named the informant Silien in tribute to the character in the classic French crime film Le Doulos. The film received eight César Award nominations and was remade in South Korea in 2019 as The Beast.

documents.title: Equilibrium
documents.tagline: In a future where freedom is outlawed, outlaws will become heroes.
documents.overview: In a dystopian future, a totalitarian regime maintains peace by subduing the populace with a drug, and displays of emotion are punishable by death. A man in charge of enforcing the law rises to overthrow the system.
documents.plot:
Equilibrium is a 2002 science fiction action film directed by Kurt Wimmer and produced by Michael De Luca and Jennifer Lynch. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where emotions have been outlawed, and citizens are forced to take a daily dose of a medication called "Serenity" to numb their feelings.

The story follows John Preston (played by Christian Bale), a high-ranking enforcer in the government's Department of Public Safety, who is responsible for maintaining order and suppressing any dissent. Preston is a skilled fighter and is known for his ability to eliminate threats with precision and efficiency. He lives a sterile life, devoid of emotions, and is content with his role as a servant of the state.

However, Preston's life takes a dramatic turn when he is assigned to investigate the murder of a young woman named Vittorio Gassovski (played by Sean Bean), who was found dead in an alleyway. As Preston delves deeper into the case, he begins to experience strange and unsettling emotions, which are forbidden in his society.

Preston's investigation leads him to a group of rebels, led by a mysterious woman named Hyrdro (played by Emily Watson). The rebels are fighting against the government's oppressive regime, which has outlawed all forms of emotional expression. As Preston gets to know the rebels, he begins to question his own existence and the morality of his actions.

As Preston becomes more deeply embroiled in the rebellion, he is forced to confront his own emotions and make a choice between his loyalty to the government and his newfound sense of humanity. The movie builds towards a climactic showdown between Preston and the leader of the Department of Public Safety, Minister Cole (played by Toby Stephens).

Throughout the film, Wimmer explores themes of individuality, free will, and the importance of human emotions in a world that seeks to suppress them. The movie features a unique blend of action, drama, and philosophy, which sets it apart from other sci-fi films.

Ultimately, Preston must decide where his loyalties lie and whether he is willing to sacrifice everything for the sake of humanity. The film's ending is both thought-provoking and visually stunning, leaving the audience with a lasting impression of the importance of emotions in our lives.

Overall, Equilibrium is a gripping and thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that explores complex themes and features impressive action sequences. Christian Bale delivers a standout performance as John Preston, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both fascinating and flawed.

documents.title: Maid in Manhattan
documents.tagline: ...love checks in.
documents.overview: Marisa Ventura is a struggling single mom who works at a posh Manhattan hotel and dreams of a better life for her and her young son. One fateful day, hotel guest and senatorial candidate Christopher Marshall meets Marisa and mistakes her for a wealthy socialite. After an enchanting evening together, the two fall madly in love. But when Marisa's true identity is revealed, issues of class and social status threaten to separate them. Can two people from very different worlds overcome their differences and live happily ever after?

documents.title: Juno
documents.tagline: A comedy about growing up… and the bumps along the way.
documents.overview: Faced with an unplanned pregnancy, an offbeat young woman makes an unusual decision regarding her unborn child.
documents.plot: Faced with an unplanned pregnancy, sixteen year old high-schooler, Juno MacGuff, makes an unusual decision regarding her unborn child.

documents.title: Carrie
documents.tagline: If you've got a taste for terror… take Carrie to the prom!
documents.overview: Carrie White, a shy and troubled teenage girl who is tormented by her high school peers and her fanatically religious mother, begins to use her powers of telekinesis to exact revenge upon them.
documents.plot:
16-year-old Carrie White is a shy high school student in Chamberlain, Maine, who is frequently bullied by her peers. When Carrie experiences her first period while showering after gym class, she panics, having never been taught about menstruation. Her female classmates laugh and throw tampons and sanitary pads at her until the gym teacher, Miss Collins, intervenes. Her abusive and religiously fanatical mother, Margaret, tells Carrie that her period was caused by sin and locks Carrie in a "prayer closet" to pray to God for forgiveness. At school, Miss Collins reprimands Carrie's tormentors by punishing them with exercise detention, threatening to suspend them and revoke their prom tickets if they refuse. Carrie's longtime bully, Chris Hargensen, eventually refuses and gets banned from the prom.
Plotting vengeance against Carrie, Chris and her delinquent boyfriend Billy Nolan break into a farm and slaughter pigs to drain their blood into a bucket, which they place above the school's stage in the gym. Carrie realizes she can control objects with her mind when she is upset. She learns that her abilities result from telekinesis and begins researching books on the subject. Sue Snell, a classmate who feels remorseful for her part in bullying Carrie, asks her popular athlete boyfriend, Tommy Ross, to invite Carrie to prom. Carrie believes the proposition is a prank, but he insists it is genuine, and she eventually accepts. When Carrie informs Margaret of her plans to attend the prom, Margaret angrily forbids her. Despite her protests, Carrie rebels as Margaret witnesses evidence of her daughter's telekinetic powers, denouncing Carrie as a witch corrupted by sin.
During prom, Chris and Billy hide under the stage while her best friend, Norma, and other conspirators switch the ballots to ensure Carrie wins the Prom Queen title. As Carrie stands onstage with Tommy, finally beginning to feel accepted by her peers, Sue realizes Chris and Billy's plan and tries to intervene. Miss Collins spots Sue and, thinking that she is plotting a prank, throws her out of the prom. Chris and Billy douse Carrie in the pigs' blood before sneaking out of the school. The empty bucket hits an angered Tommy on the head, knocking him unconscious. Norma begins laughing with other students, causing Carrie to hallucinate that everyone is mocking her, believing it was their plan all along. She telekinetically seals the exits and attacks the students with a fire hose, injuring several and killing Norma. A falling basketball backboard crushes Miss Collins after she and the students attempt to carry Tommy's body, and Carrie electrocutes her principal and English teacher, one of the two bursting into flames, setting the gym on fire. She exits the burning school and seals the doors behind her, leaving the trapped staff and classmates to die. As Carrie walks home, Chris attempts to run her over, but Carrie causes the car to swerve and roll over.

documents.title: Carrie
documents.tagline: If only they knew she had the power.
documents.overview: Carrie White is a lonely and painfully shy teenage girl with telekinetic powers who is slowly pushed to the edge of insanity by frequent bullying from both classmates at her school, and her own religious, but abusive, mother.
documents.plot:
Carrie is a 2002 American supernatural horror television film based on Stephen King's 1974 novel, the second adaptation of the book after Brian De Palma's 1976 film. Written by Bryan Fuller and directed by David Carson, it stars Angela Bettis as Carrie White, with Patricia Clarkson as her mother Margaret, Rena Sofer, Kandyse McClure and Emilie de Ravin. Produced by Trilogy Entertainment Group and MGM Television for NBC and filmed in Vancouver, it was conceived as a stand-alone film that could also serve as a pilot for a possible series. It aired on NBC on 4 November 2002.

The story unfolds through police interviews conducted by Detective John Mulcahey, who is investigating a devastating fire and the disappearance of a high-school student, Carrie White. Classmate Sue Snell and gym teacher Rita Desjarden recount the preceding events in flashbacks. A week before the senior prom at Ewen High School, Carrie is a lonely, shy girl tormented by popular students led by Chris Hargensen. When Carrie experiences her first menstrual period in the gym shower, the other girls humiliate her until Ms. Desjarden intervenes. When the principal sends her home and calls her by the wrong name, Carrie's anger makes his desk move.

At home, Carrie's fanatically religious mother, Margaret, who believes menstruation is a sign of sin, locks her in a prayer closet. Ms. Desjarden punishes the bullies with detention, threatening to bar them from the prom if they skip it, and Chris, refusing, is banned. Carrie begins to explore her telekinetic powers. Sue, feeling guilty, persuades her boyfriend, Tommy Ross, to take Carrie to the prom, while Chris and her boyfriend, Billy Nolan, plan a cruel prank. At the prom, Carrie enjoys a rare moment of happiness and is crowned queen, but when a bucket of pig's blood is dumped on her, she unleashes her powers in a rampage of destruction across the school and the town. Unlike the novel, the film ends with Carrie surviving, as Sue helps her escape and the authorities believe she is dead.

The film was poorly received by critics, with a 32 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it brought nothing new and paled in comparison with the 1976 version. Several critics questioned the need for a new adaptation, though Bettis's performance received some praise. The planned series was never produced.

documents.title: There Will Be Blood
documents.tagline: There Will Be Greed. There Will Be Vengeance.
documents.overview: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview, moves to oil-rich California. Using his son to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainview's motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.
documents.plot:
There Will Be Blood is a 2007 American epic drama film directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, written by Anderson, and starring Daniel Day-Lewis as Daniel Plainview, a ruthless oil tycoon. The film is set in the early 20th century in Southern California.

The movie begins with an elderly Daniel Plainview (played by Paul Dano) who has been searching for his long-lost brother, Eli (played by Dillon Freasier), and finally finds him after years of searching. However, it's revealed that Eli was actually a figment of Daniel's imagination, created to cope with the loss of his real brother.

The story then shifts to 1898, where we meet Daniel Plainview (played by Daniel Day-Lewis) as a young man who has just arrived in California with his mother. He is determined to make a name for himself and strike it rich in the oil fields. After his mother's death, Daniel becomes obsessed with finding oil, driven by a desire to prove himself and secure his place in the world.

Daniel meets Eli Sunday (played by Paul Dano), a young preacher who claims to have found an oil well on his property. Daniel sees an opportunity to make a fortune and convinces Eli to let him drill for oil on his land. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Daniel's obsession with oil is not just about making money, but also about proving himself as a man.

As Daniel's fortunes rise, he becomes increasingly ruthless in his business dealings, using underhanded tactics to eliminate his competitors and anyone who gets in his way. He also becomes embroiled in a series of complex relationships with the people around him, including Eli Sunday, who is torn between his faith and his desire for wealth.

One of Daniel's most significant relationships is with Abigail Plainview (played by Danny Huston), his adopted son from his previous marriage. However, it's revealed that Abigail was actually a figment of Daniel's imagination as well, created to cope with the loss of his real son.

As the story reaches its climax, Daniel becomes embroiled in a bitter rivalry with Eli Sunday, who is determined to expose Daniel's true nature and bring him down. The two men engage in a series of intense confrontations, both physical and spiritual, as they clash over their values and principles.

In the end, Daniel Plainview emerges victorious, but at great cost. He has lost everything that truly mattered to him - his relationships, his integrity, and even his own sense of self. The film ends with an elderly Daniel Plainview, who is now a shadow of his former self, sitting alone in his mansion, surrounded by the trappings of wealth and power.

Throughout the film, Paul Thomas Anderson masterfully explores themes of ambition, greed, and the corrupting influence of power. Daniel Day-Lewis's performance as Daniel Plainview is widely regarded as one of the greatest performances in cinema history, earning him an Academy Award for Best Actor.

documents.title: Elite Squad
documents.tagline: On the streets of Rio only the elite survive
documents.overview: In 1997, before the visit of the pope to Rio de Janeiro, Captain Nascimento from BOPE (Special Police Operations Battalion) is assigned to eliminate the risks of the drug dealers in a dangerous slum nearby where the pope intends to be lodged.
documents.plot:
Elite Squad (Portuguese: Tropa de Elite) is a 2007 Brazilian crime film directed by José Padilha, who wrote the screenplay with Bráulio Mantovani and Rodrigo Pimentel, based on the novel Elite da Tropa by Luiz Eduardo Soares, André Batista and Pimentel. Padilha's first narrative feature, it stars Wagner Moura as Captain Roberto Nascimento of Rio de Janeiro's Battalion of Special Police Operations (BOPE), with Caio Junqueira and André Ramiro.

In 1997, Nascimento leads a BOPE operation to secure the Turano favela ahead of Pope John Paul II's overnight stay at the nearby archbishop's residence. With his wife, Rosane, pregnant, he is looking for a successor so that he can move to a desk job. Rookie military police officers André Matias and Neto Gouveia, best friends, are given menial tasks by corrupt superiors: Neto runs the motor pool and Matias files complaints. Matias also studies law, where he begins dating Maria and meets her friends, who work at an NGO in territory controlled by the drug lord Baiano. He befriends Romerito, a nearsighted boy. Disgusted by corruption, Neto and Matias divert bribe money to repair police cars. When their captain sends a fellow officer to a funk party in Morro da Babilônia in what may be a setup, the two friends try to protect him and set off a deadly gunfight with traffickers, ending only when Nascimento's team rescues the officers.

Matias, photographed by the press after the shootout, joins Neto in applying to BOPE,. Both men survive BOPE's brutal training. After his relationship with Maria ends, Matias arranges to give Romerito a pair of glasses, but Edu, one of Maria's friends, tips off Baiano, who sets an ambush. Neto goes in Matias's place and is fatally shot. Seeing his BOPE tattoo, Baiano goes into hiding, but first has two NGO workers executed. After the funeral, BOPE raids the favela daily, torturing dealers for information; learning of Edu's role, Matias beats him at a peace march. When BOPE finally corners Baiano, Nascimento orders Matias to execute him with a shotgun, avenging Neto and completing his initiation, and the screen fades to white at the sound of the shot.

The film was a box office hit and a cultural phenomenon in Brazil. It won the Golden Bear at the 2008 Berlin Film Festival, though international reviews were mixed, with 51% on Rotten Tomatoes. Its sequel, Elite Squad: The Enemy Within, followed in 2010, and in 2015 Abraccine ranked the original 30th among the greatest Brazilian films.

documents.title: The Bucket List
documents.tagline: Find the joy.
documents.overview: Corporate billionaire Edward Cole and working class mechanic Carter Chambers are worlds apart. At a crossroads in their lives, they share a hospital room and discover they have two things in common: a desire to spend the time they have left doing everything they ever wanted to do and an unrealized need to come to terms with who they are. Together they embark on the road trip of a lifetime, becoming friends along the way and learning to live life to the fullest, with insight and humor.
