documents.title: Sahara
documents.tagline: Dirk Pitt. Adventure has a new name.
documents.overview: Scouring the ocean depths for treasure-laden shipwrecks is business as usual for a thrill-seeking underwater adventurer and his wisecracking buddy. But when these two cross paths with a beautiful doctor, they find themselves on the ultimate treasure hunt.
documents.plot: Seasoned adventurer and treasure hunter Dirk Pitt, a former Navy SEAL, sets out for the African desert with his wisecracking buddy Al in search of a confederate ironclad battleship rumored to have vanished long ago, the main draw being the treasure supposedly hidden within the lost vessel. When the daring duo come across Dr. Eva Rojas, a beautiful scientist who is juggling an escape from a warlord and a mission to stop the spread of a powerful plague, their desert expedition begins to heat up.

documents.title: Chicken Run
documents.tagline: This ain't no chick flick. It's poultry in motion.
documents.overview: Having been hopelessly repressed and facing eventual certain death at the British chicken farm where they are held, Ginger the chicken along with the help of Rocky the American rooster decide to rebel and lead their fellow chickens in a great escape from the murderous farmers Mr. and Mrs. Tweedy and their farm of doom.
documents.plot:
Chicken Run is a stop-motion animated comedy film directed by Peter Lord and Nick Park, produced by DreamWorks Pictures, Aardman Animations, and Amblin Entertainment. The movie was released on August 11, 2000.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to a large farm where chickens live in a coop. The main character, Ginger (voiced by Julia Sawalha), is a clever and resourceful chicken who dreams of escaping the farm. She has lost her mother at a young age and has been raised by the farm's owner, Mrs. Tweedy (voiced by Miranda Richardson). However, Mrs. Tweedy's intentions are far from pure, as she plans to use the chickens' eggs for her own gain.

Ginger befriends Rocky (voiced by Mel Gibson), a tough but lovable rooster who becomes her ally in her quest for freedom. Together, they come up with a plan to escape the farm using a stolen tractor. However, their plan is soon discovered by Mrs. Tweedy and her accomplice, a sly and cunning dog named Fat Amy (voiced by Julie T. Wallace).

As the story unfolds, Ginger and Rocky face numerous obstacles and challenges as they try to outsmart Mrs. Tweedy and her cohorts. Along the way, they meet other chickens who join their cause, including Pepper (voiced by Timothy Spall), a clever and resourceful chicken who helps them with their escape plan.

The plot development is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience engaged and entertained. The animation is beautifully done, with intricate details and textures that bring the characters to life. The voice acting is also superb, with each character bringing their own unique personality to the story.

As the chickens near their goal of freedom, they face one final challenge: a showdown with Mrs. Tweedy and her dog. In the end, Ginger and Rocky's plan succeeds, and the chickens are finally able to escape the farm. However, not everyone is happy about this turn of events, and some chickens must make difficult choices in order to ensure their survival.

The ending is both heartwarming and humorous, with a sense of closure for the characters. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Ginger and Rocky flying off into the sunset, free at last from the confines of the farm.

Overall, Chicken Run is a delightful and entertaining film that is sure to appeal to audiences of all ages. With its clever plot, lovable characters, and beautiful animation, it's no wonder that this movie has become a classic of stop-motion animation.

documents.title: Brothers
documents.tagline: There are two sides to every family.
documents.overview: When his helicopter goes down during his fourth tour of duty in Afghanistan, Marine Sam Cahill is presumed dead. Back home, brother Tommy steps in to look over Sam’s wife, Grace, and two children. Sam’s surprise homecoming triggers domestic mayhem.
documents.plot:
[No information found]

However, I can provide some general information about the movie "Brothers" released in 2009.

"Brothers" is a drama film directed by Jim Sheridan and starring Tobey Maguire, Natalie Portman, and Jake Gyllenhaal. The movie follows the story of three brothers who are struggling to cope with their past and find their way in life.

The film begins with the death of the eldest brother, Sam (Jake Gyllenhaal), a soldier who was killed in action during the Iraq War. His younger brother Bobby (Tobey Maguire) is left to care for his infant son, while his middle brother Tommy (Jake Gyllenhaal's real-life twin brother, but played by Jake Gyllenhaal) returns home from serving in Afghanistan.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each of the brothers has been struggling with their own demons. Bobby is trying to balance his life as a single father, while Tommy is dealing with PTSD and feelings of guilt over not being able to protect Sam. The two brothers' differing experiences during the war have left them both emotionally scarred.

Throughout the film, the brothers are forced to confront their past and work through their emotions in order to move forward. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about family, loyalty, and redemption.

The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Tobey Maguire and Jake Gyllenhaal, who deliver nuanced and emotionally charged portrayals of their characters. The film's themes of grief, guilt, and redemption are timely and thought-provoking, making "Brothers" a powerful and moving drama.

documents.title: Tropic Thunder
documents.tagline: Get Some.
documents.overview: Ben Stiller, Jack Black and Robert Downey Jr. lead an ensemble cast in 'Tropic Thunder,' an action comedy about a group of self-absorbed actors who set out to make the most expensive war film. After ballooning costs force the studio to cancel the movie, the frustrated director refuses to stop shooting, leading his cast into the jungles of Southeast Asia, where they encounter real bad guys.
documents.plot:
Tropic Thunder is a satirical action comedy film directed by Ben Stiller, released in 2008 by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie follows the story of four self-absorbed actors who drop into the jungle to film a war movie.

The film begins with Tugg Speedman (Ben Stiller), a washed-up action hero struggling to revive his career. He is joined by Kirk Lazarus (Robert Downey Jr.), a method actor who undergoes a drastic transformation to play a black Australian soldier in the war movie. The two are accompanied by Jeff Portnoy (Jack Black), a comedic actor known for his outrageous performances, and Damien Cockburn (Steve Coogan), a British actor who is more serious about his craft.

The four actors embark on a disastrous journey into the jungle to film their war movie, which they hope will revitalize their careers. However, things quickly take a turn for the worse as they are dropped off in the middle of nowhere with limited supplies and no clear direction from their director, Les Grossman (Tom Cruise).

As the actors struggle to survive and complete their scenes, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and each other's egos. The group soon realizes that they are not prepared for the harsh conditions of the jungle and that their inexperience will put them in grave danger.

Throughout the film, the characters' personalities and flaws are on full display. Tugg Speedman is shown to be a self-centered actor who only cares about his own career, while Kirk Lazarus is revealed to be a shallow and pretentious actor who uses his transformation as an excuse for his lack of talent. Jeff Portnoy, on the other hand, is depicted as a lovable but immature actor who often provides comic relief.

As the story unfolds, the actors are forced to confront their own mortality and the reality of their situation. They must work together to survive and complete their scenes, which leads to some unexpected moments of camaraderie and growth.

In the end, the actors manage to escape the jungle with their lives, but not without some serious consequences. The film ends on a bittersweet note, as the actors reflect on what they have learned from their experience in the jungle.

Overall, Tropic Thunder is a hilarious and satirical take on the Hollywood film industry, with plenty of laughs and memorable moments along the way. The film's cast delivers standout performances, and Ben Stiller's direction brings the story to life with humor and heart.

documents.title: Titan A.E.
documents.tagline: When Earth Ends, The Adventure Begins.
documents.overview: A young man finds out that he holds the key to restoring hope and ensuring survival for the human race, while an alien species called the Drej are bent on mankind's destruction.
documents.plot:
In 3028 A.D., a groundbreaking scientific project known as "The Titan Project" incurs the wrath of the Drej, a hostile race of aliens made of pure energy, who fear that it will allow humans to challenge them. Determined to wipe out humanity due to the potential of the project, the Drej (who the Drej Queen orders to kill all humans) initiate a massive attack on Earth, forcing the human race to evacuate the planet. During the evacuation, Professor Sam Tucker—head researcher on the Titan Project—leaves his young son Cale in the care of his Vusstran friend Tek and flees Earth in the spaceship Titan. Before he leaves, he gives Cale a gold ring, promising him that there will be hope for humanity as long as he wears it. The Drej destroy Earth, and the surviving humans flee into space.
15 years later, the remnants of humanity live on as refugees, but face extinction with no home planet of their own. Ex-military officer Joseph Korso, a former friend and confidant of the late Sam, tracks down a jaded and cynical Cale, who works in the salvage yard of space station Tau 14. Korso reveals that a holographic map leading to the location of the Titan is encoded in Cale's ring, and invites Cale to join the crew of his spaceship, the Valkyrie, as they seek the Titan. Accepting Korso's offer, Cale escapes the Tau 14 with him as the Drej pursue them and wanting Cale killed. On the Valkyrie, Cale befriends human pilot Akima Kunimoto, and 3 alien crew members: first mate Preedex "Preed" Yoa, surly weapons officer Stith, and eccentric astronomer Gune.
Cale's map leads the crew of the Valkyrie to the planet Sesharrim, where an alien race called the Gaoul help them interpret the map, revealing that the Titan is hidden in the Andali Nebula. Drej fighters then attack the planet and abduct Cale (who the Drej actually want alive) and Akima in order to copy the map and imprision Cale. Akima is rescued by the crew due to having been jettisoned by the Drej Queen, while Cale, after hearing the Drej Queen's new plan to kill the humans, escapes the Drej mothership in a stolen fighter and makes his way back to the Valkyrie. The map changes to reveal that the Titan is hidden in the Ice Rings of Tigrin, a labyrinthine ice field in space. While resupplying at human space station New Bangkok, Cale and Akima discover that Korso and Preed teamed up with the Drej (only to sell the Titan's location to them) and manage to escape the Valkyrie and are left stranded on New Bangkok when Korso leaves for the Titan. Determined to beat Korso to the Titan, they fix up a dilapidated spaceship with help from the station's inhabitants.
Cale and Akima navigate the ice rings of Tigrin in a race against the Valkyrie and dock with the Titan. They discover the DNA coding of various animals (which either are, or will be) onboard and a pre-recorded message left by a now-deceased Sam (who was killed by the Drej due to not facing the truth), explaining that the ship was designed to create planets.

documents.overview: Mere seconds before the Earth is to be demolished by an alien construction crew, Arthur Dent is swept off the planet by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher penning a new edition of "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy."

documents.title: Alpha Dog
documents.tagline: One crime. 38 witnesses. No way back.
documents.overview: Johnny Truelove likes to see himself as tough. He's the son of an underworld figure and a drug dealer. Johnny also likes to get tough when things don't go his way. When Jake Mazursky fails to pay up for Johnny, things get worse for the Mazursky family, as Johnny and his 'gang' kidnap Jake's 15 year old brother and holds him hostage. Problem now is what to do with 'stolen boy?'
documents.plot:
In 1999, Johnny Truelove works as a young drug dealer while making a living in the San Gabriel Valley. Johnny's father, Sonny, supplies him with marijuana, which he distributes with his gang of friends: Frankie Ballenbacher, Johnny's right-hand man and best friend; Tiko Martinez, the group's muscle; Elvis Schmidt, who is ridiculed for being in debt to Johnny; and Jake Mazursky, a local drug addict also in debt with Johnny. Jake attempts to borrow money from his father, Butch, and stepmother, Olivia, while his younger half-brother Zack looks up to him and longs to escape his home life.
A fight breaks out when Jake tries to pay Johnny only part of his debt, leading Johnny to get him fired from his telemarketing job by ratting on him to his boss that Jake is on drugs, and Jake to retaliate by breaking into and trashing Johnny's house with a couple of his friends. Johnny brings Frankie and Tiko to confront Jake, but he is nowhere to be found. Spotting Zack on the side of a road, the gang impulsively kidnaps him, planning to hold him until Jake pays up, and drive to Palm Springs. Frankie is left to watch Zack while Johnny and Tiko return to San Gabriel for prior commitments. That night, while attending a street fiesta, Frankie offers Zack a chance to leave, but he declines, wanting a break from home and not wanting to cause more problems for Jake, and the two strike up an unlikely friendship. Meanwhile, Jake violently interrupts a party that he believes Johnny may be attending, knocking several people unconscious before telling everyone there that he is looking for Truelove.
Staying at the house of Frankie's father, Juergen, Zack meets Frankie's friends Keith Stratten, Julie Beckley (with whom he falls in love), Sabrina Pope (Frankie's girlfriend), and Susan Hartunian, the only one concerned about his abduction. Johnny comes over and contemplates with Frankie on what to do. Frankie suggests that they pay Zack to keep quiet about the kidnapping and send him home, to which Johnny agrees. However, after a threatening phone-call from Jake and learning from his lawyer that he could face life in prison for his actions, Johnny goes to Elvis and offers to cancel his debt if he kills Zack, handing him a submachine gun before going out with his girlfriend, Angela Holden, to celebrate her birthday. Believing Zack will be returning home that night, Frankie and his friends throw a raucous party at a hotel, during which Zack goes skinny dipping with Julie and her friend Alma, leading to a threesome wherein he loses his virginity.
Julie, Alma, Susan, and Sabrina all happily say goodbye to Zack and leave. A little while later, Elvis arrives and argues with Frankie over Johnny's plan to kill Zack. While Frankie runs off, Elvis politely introduces himself to Zack, then takes Keith to dig a grave in the nearby mountains. Frankie returns and gives Zack a final chance to escape, but Zack declines, oblivious to the danger he's in.

documents.title: Speed Racer
documents.tagline: Go!
documents.overview: Speed Racer is the tale of a young and brilliant racing driver. When corruption in the racing leagues costs his brother his life, he must team up with the police and the mysterious Racer X to bring an end to the corruption and criminal activities. Inspired by the cartoon series.

documents.title: Vantage Point
documents.tagline: 8 Strangers. 8 points of view.  1 Truth.
documents.overview: The attempted assassination of the American president is told and re-told from several different perspectives.
documents.plot:
In Salamanca, Spain, an assassination attempt on U.S. President Henry Ashton (William Hurt) unfolds from several different vantage points.
GNN producer Rex Brooks directs news coverage from a mobile television studio as the president arrives to a ceremony at the city's Plaza Mayor, for the start of an international summit against terrorism. The mayor of Salamanca introduces the President, who is shot twice as he reaches the podium, soon followed by an explosion outside the plaza. Moments later, a secondary explosion at the podium kills and injures numerous people.
Before the President takes the stage, Secret Service agent Thomas Barnes (Dennis Quaid) notices a curtain fluttering in a supposedly vacated building, and observes American tourist Howard Lewis filming the audience. After the President is shot, Barnes tackles a man named Enrique rushing to the podium. Following the second explosion, Barnes barges into the GNN studio to view their footage. He receives a call from another Secret Service agent, who reports he is pursuing the suspected assassin; Barnes is then startled by an image from GNN's live feed.
Enrique (Eduardo Noriega), a Spanish police officer guarding the Mayor, overhears his girlfriend Veronica being embraced by a stranger and plan to meet later under an overpass. Enrique confronts Veronica, who assures him of her love as he hands her a bag. When the President is shot, Enrique rushes to protect the Mayor but is tackled by Barnes. Enrique witnesses Veronica toss the bag under the podium, causing the second explosion. Escaping the Secret Service, Enrique confronts an unseen individual at the overpass.
In the crowd, Howard Lewis chats with a man called Sam, while a little girl named Anna bumps into him. Howard notices Barnes looking at the nearby window, and films him with his camcorder. Following the explosion at the podium, Howard chases Enrique and the pursuing Secret Service agents. At the overpass, Howard views the agents from afar shooting at Enrique as he greets an individual in a police uniform under the overpass. Wounded, Enrique falls to the ground. As a speeding ambulance is about to hit Anna, Howard runs into the road after her.
Previously, Ashton, having been informed of a credible threat, returns to his hotel room while his body double proceeds to the plaza. Ashton and his personnel discuss the reason and origin for the terrorists' plot, and the return of Barnes to active duty; they watch on TV the double being shot and the first explosion. One adviser is intent on Ashton giving immediate order for retaliation against the village of origin of the terrorists they are aware of, when the second explosion shatters the room's windows. The staffer insists in earnest on retaliation, but Ashton refuses, so the negotiations can continue. A masked assailant bursts into the room, shoots the advisers, and abducts Ashton.

documents.title: Open Season
documents.tagline: All Fur One. One Fur All.
documents.overview: Boog, a domesticated 900lb. Grizzly bear finds himself stranded in the woods 3 days before Open Season. Forced to rely on Elliot, a fast-talking mule deer, the two form an unlikely friendship and must quickly rally other forest animals if they are to form a rag-tag army against the hunters.
documents.plot:
Open Season is a 2006 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Columbia Pictures Animation and released by Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie follows the story of Otis, a bear who lives in a forest filled with various animals.

The beginning of the movie starts with Otis (voiced by Matthew Fox) being an outcast among his fellow bears due to his unusual appearance and behavior. He is often bullied and ridiculed by the other bears, which makes him feel isolated and alone. However, Otis has a unique gift - he can talk.

One day, Otis meets a group of animals who are planning to take over the forest, led by a sly and cunning raccoon named Cody (voiced by Joe Pesci). The animals plan to overthrow their human oppressors and establish a new order in the forest. However, things don't go as planned, and the animals soon find themselves facing a common enemy - a group of hunters who are determined to wipe out all the animals in the forest.

As Otis tries to navigate his way through this chaos, he meets a young rabbit named Judy (voiced by Brittany Murphy) who becomes his love interest. Together, they try to stop Cody and his gang from taking over the forest. Along the way, Otis discovers that he has a special connection with Judy and that she is not just any ordinary rabbit.

The plot development of the movie takes a turn when Otis and Judy team up with a group of animals who are determined to protect their home from the hunters. They come across a wise old owl named Sam (voiced by Steve Buscemi) who helps them on their mission. As they journey through the forest, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their courage and determination.

In the end, Otis and his friends successfully defeat Cody and his gang, saving the forest from destruction. However, not before realizing that there is more to life than just fighting for survival. The movie ends with Otis and Judy sharing a romantic moment, and the other animals celebrating their victory.

Throughout the movie, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both entertaining and engaging. The voice acting is also top-notch, with each character having its own unique personality and quirks. Overall, Open Season is a fun and action-packed animated film that explores themes of friendship, love, and acceptance.

It's worth noting that while the movie received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of animation and comedy. The success of the movie led to two sequels, Open Season 2 (2008) and Open Season 3 (2010), as well as various merchandise and spin-offs.

documents.title: Like Stars on Earth
documents.tagline: Every Child Is Special.
documents.overview: Ishaan Awasthi is an eight-year-old whose world is filled with wonders that no one else seems to appreciate. Colours, fish, dogs, and kites don't seem important to the adults, who are much more interested in things like homework, marks, and neatness. Ishaan cannot seem to get anything right in class; he is then sent to boarding school, where his life changes forever.
documents.plot:
Ishaan is an 8-year-old boy living in Mumbai, who has trouble following school. He is assumed by all to simply hate learning and deemed a troublemaker, and is belittled for it. He has even repeated the 3rd standard due to his academic failures from the previous year. Ishaan's imagination, creativity and talent for art and painting are often disregarded. Ishaan's father, Nandkishore Awasthi, is a successful executive who expects his sons to excel. His mother, Maya is a homemaker who gave up her career and is frustrated by her inability to educate Ishaan, despite caring for Ishaan. His elder brother Yohaan is an exemplary student and tennis player in whose shadow Ishaan remains, though he is the most supportive of Ishaan.
One day, his parents are called by the principal to discuss his behavior and grades. Due to Ishaan's continued failures, lack of improvement, and rebellious behavior, the principal suggests they look into special schools, but Nandkishore rejects this and sends him to a boarding school much to Maya and Yohaan's dismay. Alone there, Ishaan rapidly sinks into a state of fear, anxiety and depression, which is only worsened by the teachers' strict and abusive regime. Ishaan's only friend is Rajan Damodaran, a physically disabled boy who is one of the top students and resides with his family there, as his father is part of the school's board. Ishaan contemplates suicide one day, but Rajan intervenes and stops him while also informing Ishaan that Mr. Holkar, the boarding school's strict and abusive art teacher, has left and is being replaced by someone else.
Ram Shankar Nikumbh, a young, cheerful and optimistic instructor at the Tulips School for young children with developmental disabilities, joins as the boarding school's temporary art teacher the same day, replacing Mr. Holkar. Ram's teaching style is markedly different from Holkar's, and he quickly notes Ishaan's unhappiness after Ishaan fails to draw anything during the class. Ram reviews Ishaan's work and concludes that his academic shortcomings are indicative of dyslexia. Ram then visits Ishaan's house in Mumbai, where he is surprised to discover Ishaan's hidden interest in art. Ram demonstrates to Maya and Yohaan how Ishaan has extreme difficulty in understanding letters and words due to dyslexia and his trouble in sports stems from his poor motor ability (which also applies to his difficulty in understanding multiple instructions, tying shoelaces, and judging the size, speed, and distance of a ball). However, Nandkishore labels it as an intellectual disability (as well as an excuse) and dismisses it as laziness, much to Ram's frustration.
Back at school, Ram brings up the topic of dyslexia in a class by offering a list of famous dyslexic people. Ram comforts Ishaan, telling him how he struggled as a child as well. Ram obtains the principal's permission to become Ishaan's tutor.

documents.title: London
documents.tagline: One young man's incredible journey of self-discovery
documents.overview: London is a drug laden adventure that centers on a party in a New York loft where a young man is trying to win back his ex-girlfriend.
documents.plot:
London is a 2005 American romantic drama written and directed by Hunter Richards. Chris Evans stars as a heartbroken young man who crashes his ex-girlfriend's farewell party, with Jason Statham, Jessica Biel, Joy Bryant, Kelli Garner and Isla Fisher in supporting roles. The electronic group The Crystal Method composed the score.

Syd has been deeply depressed since his girlfriend London left him. When a friend calls to tell him that she is throwing a going-away party before moving to California with her new boyfriend, Syd flies into a rage and wrecks his apartment. He decides to crash the party, bringing along Bateman, a banker who delivers cocaine to him as a favor to their mutual dealer. The party takes place at a condominium belonging to the parents of the socialite Rebecca, played by Fisher.

Syd and Bateman quickly barricade themselves in the bathroom, where they snort line after line of cocaine, drink tequila and hold long, rambling conversations about love, sex, God, women and pain. Over the course of the night, Bateman urges Syd to move on with his life. Their private party is joined by Maya and Mallory, who feign sympathy for Syd in order to share the free drugs. When Syd learns that London has arrived, Bateman challenges him to finally face her.

After a heated confrontation in front of the guests, Syd and London decide to leave and talk somewhere private. On the way out a brawl breaks out, and Syd and Bateman fight off the other men at the party, barely escaping. Syd and London reconcile in his car and spend the night together at her apartment. In the final scene, at the airport, Syd tells London that he loves her. Although moved by his words, she leaves him anyway.

The film was poorly received. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said it was undermined by unlikable characters and that the novelty of seeing actors play against type could not rescue it, and Metacritic gave it 24 out of 100. Roger Ebert awarded it one star out of four, while The New York Times called it a misfired attempt at provocation and philosophical exploration. The song "Roboslut" from the soundtrack later appeared in a Dance Dance Revolution game under a censored title.

documents.title: Smokin' Aces
documents.tagline: Nobody gets away clean.
documents.overview: When a Las Vegas performer-turned-snitch named Buddy Israel decides to turn state's evidence and testify against the mob, it seems that a whole lot of people would like to make sure he's no longer breathing.
documents.plot:
Las Vegas magician and wannabe gangster Buddy "Aces" Israel is in hiding at a Lake Tahoe hotel while his agent negotiates a potential immunity deal with FBI Deputy Director Stanley Locke. Special Agents Richard Messner and Donald Carruthers learn that ailing mob boss Primo Sparazza has issued a $1 million bounty on Israel and sent a mysterious "Swede" to bring him Israel's heart. Several assassins also seek the reward: master of disguise Lazlo Soot; hitwomen Sharice Watters and Georgia Sykes, hired by Sparazza's underboss; mercenary Pasquale Acosta; and psychotic neo-Nazi Tremors brothers: Darwin, Jeeves, and Lester.
Locke sends Messner and Carruthers to take Israel into protective custody. Bail bondsmen Jack Dupree, "Pistol" Pete Deeks, and Hollis Elmore have been hired to capture him as well. The bondsmen are attacked by the Tremors brothers, and only Elmore escapes alive. Messner visits the murder scene while Carruthers proceeds to the hotel, which each of the assassins has infiltrated. Carruthers recognizes Acosta, disguised as a security officer, in an elevator and both are seriously wounded in the ensuing gunfight.
Soot gains access to Israel's penthouse, posing as his henchman Hugo. Sir Ivy, Israel's second-in-command, confronts Israel for agreeing to inform on Ivy and his entourage as part of the plea deal and is subdued by hotel security. In Los Angeles, Locke abruptly withdraws from the deal with Israel but does not inform Messner and Carruthers. The Tremor brothers reach the penthouse floor and attack the security team and Ivy, who kills Jeeves and Lester. Israel, learning Locke has terminated the plea deal, attempts suicide but is unable to go through with it.
Finding Carruthers and Acosta, Sykes is cornered when Messner sets up a position around the elevator. Watters provides cover from a nearby hotel with an M82 sniper rifle, outgunning Messner's team. Acosta wounds Sykes, but is shot by a dying Carruthers. Believing Sykes is dead, Watters continues shooting at the FBI. Sykes escapes to the penthouse, where she stops Darwin Tremor before he can kill Ivy. Tremor escapes, and Messner, distraught over Carruthers' death, stops Ivy and Sykes on the stairwell but lets them go. Seeing the pair alive and free through her rifle scope, Watters is approached by FBI agents and gunshots are heard.
Locke and his team descend on the hotel and take Israel to the hospital. Soot escapes, while Acosta is carted away on a gurney, still alive, and Darwin is gunned down by Elmore. At the hospital, Messner learns the truth from Locke. Sparazza's heart is failing and Israel, being his illegitimate son, is the most compatible donor. Sparazza's actual identity is Freeman Heller, former undercover FBI agent who was assassinated by the FBI for blurring the lines between mobster and agent. After surviving the betrayal, Heller permanently adopted the identity of Sparazza.

documents.title: Over the Hedge
documents.tagline: Taking back the neighborhood... One snack at a time.
documents.overview: A scheming raccoon fools a mismatched family of forest creatures into helping him repay a debt of food, by invading the new suburban sprawl that popped up while they were hibernating – and learns a lesson about family himself.
documents.plot:
Over the Hedge is a 2006 American computer-animated comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of a group of forest animals who embark on a journey to find food and shelter.

The film begins with RJ, a wise-cracking raccoon (voiced by Bruce Willis), who lives in a suburban neighborhood with his friends Verne the skunk (voiced by Steve Carell), Hammy the squirrel (voiced by Patrick Warburton), Stinky the skunk's brother (voiced by Seth Green), and Ozzie the rabbit (voiced by Cody Cameron). The animals are struggling to find food in their neighborhood, as they have been fed a diet of junk food by their human neighbors.

One day, RJ discovers that his neighbor, Mr. McGregor (voiced by Garry Shandling), is planning to sell his house and move away. RJ comes up with a plan to sneak into the nearby suburban neighborhood to find food and shelter before Mr. McGregor leaves. The group of friends sets out on their journey, facing various obstacles and challenges along the way.

As they navigate through the suburban neighborhood, the animals encounter a variety of human characters, including a family of humans who are preparing for a move (the Smiths), a group of pesky dogs, and a menacing cat named Cat (voiced by Michael Chiklis). The animals must use their wits and cunning to evade these dangers and reach their destination.

Throughout the journey, RJ's leadership is put to the test as he struggles to keep his friends safe and on track. Verne's insecurities and Hammy's naivety often lead to comedic misunderstandings, while Stinky's mischievous antics cause trouble for the group. Meanwhile, Ozzie's innocence and kindness serve as a reminder of the importance of friendship and loyalty.

As the animals near their destination, they discover that it is not what they expected. The suburban neighborhood is filled with dangers and obstacles, but also with opportunities for food and shelter. RJ and his friends must work together to overcome these challenges and find a new home.

In the end, RJ and his friends succeed in finding a new home, but not without some unexpected surprises. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, as the animals learn to appreciate their new surroundings and the importance of friendship and teamwork.

Overall, Over the Hedge is a fun and entertaining animated film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and perseverance. With its lovable characters and engaging storyline, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved classic among both children and adults.

documents.title: The Libertine
documents.tagline: He didn't resist temptation. He pursued it.
documents.overview: The story of John Wilmot, a.k.a. the Earl of Rochester, a 17th century poet who famously drank and debauched his way to an early grave, only to earn posthumous critical acclaim for his life's work.
documents.plot:
The Libertine is a 2004 period drama and the first feature directed by Laurence Dunmore, adapted by Stephen Jeffreys from his own play. It stars Johnny Depp as John Wilmot, 2nd Earl of Rochester, the notorious poet and rake of the Restoration court, and Samantha Morton as the actress Elizabeth Barry, with John Malkovich as King Charles II, Rosamund Pike as Rochester's wife Elizabeth, Rupert Friend and Kelly Reilly. The film portrays the brilliant, self-destructive earl during the last years of his life.

In 1675, Rochester addresses the audience in a prologue, warning them that they will not like him. Recalled from banishment by King Charles II, who needs his support in the House of Lords, he returns to London and his "Merry Gang" of dissolute friends, including the young Billy Downs, whom he warns that he will die of their company. At the theater, he sees Elizabeth Barry being booed off the stage and, recognizing her talent, takes it upon himself to coach her as an actress. Under his guidance she becomes a sensation, and the two begin a complicated relationship.

Seeking money from France, the king commissions Rochester to write a play to honor the visit of the French ambassador and celebrate his reign. Rochester instead writes Sodom, an obscene satire that mocks the king, humiliating Charles in front of his guest. Forced to flee London, Rochester sinks into drink and disease, his face disfigured by syphilis, while his friend Downs is killed in a brawl. Eventually forgiven by the king, he returns to his long-suffering wife and makes a final, dramatic appearance in the House of Lords before his early death.

The film depicts Rochester as a man of great wit and talent destroyed by his own excesses, and it ends with an epilogue in which Rochester, fading into the candlelight, asks the audience whether they like him now.

An unfinished version of The Libertine was shown at the 2004 Toronto International Film Festival, and a substantially recut version premiered at AFI Fest in November 2005 before its British release that month. It grossed about 10.9 million dollars worldwide and received mixed to negative reviews, with 34 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Depp's zealous performance but faulted muddled direction and murky cinematography, and a Metacritic score of 44.

documents.title: Fearless
documents.tagline: Mastering others is strength. Mastering yourself makes you fearless.
documents.overview: Huo Yuan Jia became the most famous martial arts fighter in all of China at the turn of the 20th Century. Huo faced personal tragedy but ultimately fought his way out of darkness, defining the true spirit of martial arts and also inspiring his nation. The son of a great fighter who didn't wish for his child to follow in his footsteps, Huo resolves to teach himself how to fight - and win.
documents.plot: After going through a series of tragic events in his life, martial arts master Huo Yuanjia returns to Tianjin and must fight four international soldiers, in order to safeguard his nation's pride.

documents.title: Déjà Vu
documents.tagline: If you think it's just a feeling, go back... and look again.
documents.overview: Called in to recover evidence in the aftermath of a horrific explosion on a New Orleans ferry, Federal agent Doug Carlin gets pulled away from the scene and taken to a top-secret government lab that uses a time-shifting surveillance device to help prevent crime.
documents.plot:
Déjà Vu is a 2006 American science fiction action film directed by Tony Scott and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Denzel Washington, Jim Caviezel, Eva Mendes, and Benicio del Toro.

The story begins with ATF agent Doug Carlin (Denzel Washington), who is struggling to cope with the death of his wife in a car accident. He is haunted by flashbacks of that fateful day and feels guilty for not being able to save her. To escape his grief, Doug undergoes a revolutionary new technology called "pre-crime" which allows him to see glimpses of possible future events.

The pre-crime device uses advanced computer algorithms to analyze the brain activity of individuals and predict potential crimes before they occur. The government has been using this technology to prevent terrorist attacks, but it's also being used by rogue agents to alter the course of history for personal gain.

Doug is assigned to a special task force that uses the pre-crime device to investigate a series of seemingly unrelated crimes across the country. As Doug delves deeper into the case, he begins to experience strange visions of his wife's death and realizes that one of the predicted crimes is actually a murder that has already occurred - but in a different time period.

Doug becomes obsessed with preventing the murder from happening, and he travels back in time to November 7, 2004, where he encounters a younger version of himself. He also meets a woman named Kate (Eva Mendes), who becomes his ally in altering the course of events.

As Doug navigates the past, he discovers that the murder is connected to a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and terrorists. He must use his knowledge of future events to prevent the murder from occurring, while also trying to find a way back to his own time.

However, as Doug tries to alter the timeline, he realizes that every decision he makes has unintended consequences on the present and future. The more he changes, the more chaos ensues, and Doug begins to question whether he's truly making progress or just creating a new reality.

In the climactic final act, Doug must confront his own destiny and make a choice between saving his wife or altering the course of history. In the end, Doug manages to prevent the murder from occurring, but not without sacrificing his own life in the process.

The movie ends with Kate, who has been transported back to her own time, reflecting on the events that transpired. She realizes that Doug's actions have created a new reality where his wife is still alive, and she must come to terms with the consequences of altering the timeline.

Déjà Vu received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $200 million worldwide. The movie's complex plot and themes of time travel and free will were praised by some, while others found it confusing and predictable. Despite its flaws, Déjà Vu remains an entertaining sci-fi action film with a strong performance from Denzel Washington.

documents.title: Rambo
documents.tagline: Live for nothing, or die for something.
documents.overview: When governments fail to act on behalf of captive missionaries, ex-Green Beret John James Rambo sets aside his peaceful existence along the Salween River in a war-torn region of Thailand to take action.  Although he's still haunted by violent memories of his time as a U.S. soldier during the Vietnam War, Rambo can hardly turn his back on the aid workers who so desperately need his help.
documents.plot:
Rambo, also known as John Rambo, is a 2008 action film directed by and starring Sylvester Stallone, the fourth installment in the Rambo franchise and a sequel to Rambo III (1988). Co-written by Stallone and Art Monterastelli, it features Julie Benz, Paul Schulze, Matthew Marsden and Graham McTavish. The film was an independent production by Nu Image and Millennium Films, shot in Thailand, Mexico and the United States between January and May 2007.

During the Saffron Revolution in Burma, the brutal army officer Major Pa Tee Tint leads a campaign of terror against the Karen people, razing villages, massacring civilians, conscripting boys and enslaving women. Twenty years after his time in Afghanistan, Vietnam War veteran John Rambo lives a quiet life in northern Thailand, catching snakes and running a riverboat. A group of Christian missionaries from Colorado, led by Michael Burnett and Sarah Miller, asks him to take them up the Salween River into Burma to deliver medical aid. Rambo refuses repeatedly but is eventually persuaded by Sarah. On the way, pirates stop the boat and demand Sarah, and Rambo kills them all, horrifying the missionaries.

Shortly after he drops them off, Tint's troops attack the village, slaughter its inhabitants and capture Sarah, Michael and other survivors. Rambo is then hired to ferry a team of mercenaries, led by former SAS soldier Lewis, on a mission to rescue them. Although Lewis rejects his offer of help, Rambo follows, saving the team from a patrol with his bow before they raid Tint's camp at night and free the prisoners. Separated from the others with the young sniper School Boy and Sarah, Rambo stays ahead of their pursuers. When Lewis's group is captured and about to be executed, Rambo seizes a truck-mounted machine gun, and with the help of Karen rebels the soldiers are overwhelmed in a bloody battle. Rambo kills Tint as he tries to escape. Inspired by Sarah's words, Rambo then returns to the United States and walks up the road to his father's ranch in Bowie, Arizona.

Lionsgate and The Weinstein Company released the film in the United States on January 25, 2008. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Stallone's direction and performance, the action sequences and the score, but many objected to its extremely graphic violence and thin plot. It grossed $113.2 million worldwide against a budget of about $50 million, and was followed by Rambo: Last Blood in 2019.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG IV

documents.title: The Wave
documents.tagline: Evil is something that you learn
documents.overview: A school teacher discusses types of government with his class. His students find it too boring to repeatedly go over national socialism and believe that dictatorship cannot be established in modern Germany. He starts an experiment to show how easily the masses can become manipulated.

documents.title: Resident Evil: Extinction
documents.tagline: The Extinction Is Coming...
documents.overview: Years after the Racoon City catastrophe, survivors travel across the Nevada desert, hoping to make it to Alaska. Alice joins the caravan and their fight against hordes of zombies and the evil Umbrella Corp.
documents.plot:
A cloned Alice wakes up in a mansion, wanders through its halls, and is forced to escape several security traps. However, she is eventually killed by a bounding mine hidden in the floor. Her body is dumped into a pit filled with dozens of other Alice clones, representing the failed results of the Umbrella Corporation's ongoing Project Alice.
Five years after Umbrella's attempts to cover up the contamination of Raccoon City, the T-virus has spread around the world, causing ecological destruction to all life. The real Alice wanders the wasteland and, after fighting off marauders, discovers information in an abandoned notebook referring to a supposedly uninfected area in Alaska.
Simultaneously, a convoy of survivors led by Claire Redfield and Raccoon City survivors Carlos Oliveira and L.J. Wade travels across the country in search of supplies and safe harbor. While searching a motel, L.J. is bitten by a zombie. Fearing the harsh fate that awaits him, he chooses not to tell the other survivors about the injury. The next morning, the convoy is attacked by a murderous flock of infected crows. With the team nearly overwhelmed, Alice appears and destroys the remaining crows with her newfound telekinesis, though she falls unconscious. Awaking shortly thereafter, Alice is introduced to Claire and tells her about the notebook, convincing her to take the convoy to Alaska.
Dr. Isaacs' attempts to domesticate the infected lead to creating a new zombie breed. Albert Wesker's security officer, Captain Alexander Slater, reports on Isaacs' disregard for Umbrella regulations. Wesker tasks Slater with watching Isaacs, telling him to kill the scientist if he disobeys orders again. Tracing an energy pattern sent out by Alice's telekinesis, Umbrella triangulates her location. Desperate to reclaim Alice to achieve his goals, Dr. Isaacs sends his new zombies to ambush the convoy against Wesker's specific orders. During the attack, most of the convoy is killed, and L.J. succumbs to his infection, biting Carlos before he kills him. Umbrella tries to shut Alice down remotely, but she breaks free from Umbrella's programming and continues to fight. She finds Isaacs at the scene, and he is bitten as he flees via helicopter. Alice and a girl from Claire's convoy named K-mart use Isaacs' computer to track the helicopter's flight path, leading them to Umbrella's underground facility.
As the convoy arrives at the Umbrella Facility, Carlos, dying from his bite, sets out to sacrifice himself, giving some goodbyes to the convoy, including Alice. Carlos takes a tanker truck with dynamite to destroy the zombie horde blocking the entrance to the Umbrella Facility. The dynamite explodes, killing him. Alice and Claire get everyone else onto a helicopter to get them to safety, but Alice stays behind.
Entering the underground facility, Alice meets a holograph of the Red Queen's "sister" AI, the White Queen.

documents.title: 10,000 BC
documents.tagline: The legend. The battle. The first hero.
documents.overview: A prehistoric epic that follows a young mammoth hunter's journey through uncharted territory to secure the future of his tribe.
documents.plot:
10,000 BC is a 2008 American action-adventure directed by Roland Emmerich, who wrote it with Harald Kloser. It stars Steven Strait as the young hunter D'Leh, Camilla Belle as Evolet, Cliff Curtis as his mentor Tic'Tic, Mo Zinal as his rival Ka'Ren, Nathanael Baring as Baku and Mona Hammond as the tribe's shaman, Old Mother, with Omar Sharif as the narrator. The film follows a prehistoric tribe of mammoth hunters on an epic journey across an imagined ancient world.

The Yagahl, a tribe of hunter-gatherers living in the mountains, depend on woolly mammoths for survival, but the herds are becoming scarce. When a blue-eyed girl, Evolet, is brought into the camp, Old Mother prophesies that four-legged demons will come after the last mammoth hunt and that the girl and the hunt's champion will lead the tribe into a new way of life. Doubting the prophecy, D'Leh's father, the tribe's chief hunter, leaves to find another way to save his people, entrusting his son and the White Spear to his friend Tic'Tic. Years later, D'Leh wins the White Spear and Evolet's hand when he kills a mammoth, but because the triumph was a fluke, he gives up both.

Soon afterwards, riders on horseback raid the camp, killing several villagers and carrying off Evolet and others as slaves. D'Leh, Tic'Tic, Ka'Ren and Baku pursue them across vast lands, facing terror birds and befriending a saber-toothed tiger, which earns them the trust of the Naku tribe, who see D'Leh as a prophesied savior. Gathering a coalition of tribes, D'Leh follows the raiders to an advanced civilization ruled by a god-king called the Almighty, where enslaved tribespeople and captive mammoths are being forced to build pyramids. There D'Leh must lead a slave rebellion and rescue Evolet.

The film is a spectacle-driven fantasy rather than a historical reconstruction, and it was widely criticized for its anachronisms, including pyramid-like monuments, written language and metal tools thousands of years before such developments emerged.

Premiering in Berlin on February 10, 2008, 10,000 BC was released by Warner Bros. on March 7 and opened at number one in North America. It grossed about 270 million dollars against a 105 million dollar budget, but reviews were negative, with 10 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 34.
production_companies: The Department of Trade and Industry of South Africa

documents.title: Half Nelson
documents.tagline: Secrets don't let go
documents.overview: Despite his dedication to the junior-high students who fill his classroom, idealistic teacher Dan Dunne leads a secret life of addiction that the majority of his students will never know. But things change when a troubled student Drey makes a startling discovery of his secret life, causing a tenuous bond between the two that could either end disastrously or provide a catalyst of hope.
documents.plot:
Half Nelson is a 2006 American drama film directed by Ryan Fleck, who wrote it with Anna Boden, expanding their 2004 short film Gowanus, Brooklyn. It stars Ryan Gosling as Dan Dunne, an inner-city middle-school teacher secretly addicted to drugs, Shareeka Epps as Drey, the student who discovers his habit, and Anthony Mackie. The score was provided by the Canadian band Broken Social Scene.

Dan is a young history teacher at a Brooklyn middle school who sets aside the standard curriculum to teach his students through dialectics. Engaging and popular in the classroom, he spends his free time snorting and freebasing cocaine. Shaken by an unexpected visit from his ex-girlfriend, Rachel, at a school basketball game, he is caught freebasing in the locker room by one of his students, Drey. Drey lives with her overworked single mother; her father is absent and her brother, Mike, is in prison for dealing drugs for a neighborhood dealer named Frank. With little supervision, she relies on Dan for rides home and becomes a target for Frank, who encourages her to sell drugs for him.

As their friendship grows, Dan sees Frank as a corrupting influence and tries to persuade him to leave Drey alone, while Drey unsuccessfully tries to get Dan to talk about his addiction. After a tense exchange with Frank, a high Dan visits Isabel, a teacher he has dated, and forces himself on her before leaving with an apology. The next day he coldly rebuffs Drey, telling her they are not friends, and she turns to Frank, making her first drug sale for him. At a dinner at his parents' home, Dan is distant, and his brother's girlfriend, Cindy, catches him freebasing in the garage and makes him laugh with a joke. That same night Drey arrives at a motel room full of drug users to make a delivery and discovers that the buyer is Dan; they exchange the money in silence. When Dan misses school the next day, Drey turns down a ride from Frank and goes to his motel room, where she finds him hungover. He cleans himself up and the two sit together, and when Dan botches the timing of Cindy's joke, they both burst out laughing.

The film premiered in competition at the 2006 Sundance Film Festival and opened in limited release on August 11, 2006, grossing $4.9 million worldwide on a budget of $0.7 million. Critics acclaimed it, with a Metacritic score of 85 and 91% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Gosling received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.

documents.title: Harsh Times
documents.tagline: Take A Ride To The Edge
documents.overview: Jim Davis is an ex-Army Ranger who finds himself slipping back into his old life of petty crime after a job offer from the LAPD evaporates. His best friend is pressured by his girlfriend Sylvia to find a job, but Jim is more interested in hanging out and making cash from small heists, while trying to get a law enforcement job so he can marry his Mexican girlfriend.
documents.plot:
Former U.S. Army Ranger and Global War on Terrorism veteran Jim Davis has PTSD. Jim, determined to marry his Mexican girlfriend Marta, and bring her into the United States to start a life together, returns to Los Angeles, California. He reunites with his best friend Mike Alonzo, whose longtime girlfriend Sylvia is a young attorney "on the warpath" over his failure to get a job. Mike's previous job was outsourced and Sylvia encourages Jim to help Mike find new employment. After failing the psychological profile for a position in the LAPD, Jim gets drunk with Mike and they visit Jim's ex-girlfriend. A fight ensues when her current boyfriend shows up with a group of friends. Jim gets the upper hand and when Mike produces a gun, they rob the men of their possessions, including marijuana and a handgun. Jim leaves messages on Mike's answering machine with different voices, pretending to be companies responding to his resume. The fake callbacks put Sylvia in a good mood and Jim and Mike go to a "paisa" bar to try selling the stolen gun but leave after a potential buyer is killed. Mike is horrified, but Jim is excited by witnessing death again.
When Mike returns home drunk to an upset Sylvia, he plays back the answering machine messages and discovers Jim's voice was inadvertently captured at the end. Sylvia throws Mike out and he stays at Jim's place. Jim gets shortlisted for a position with the Department of Homeland Security, but, after cheating on a urine test, he fails a polygraph question about drug use. His only other prospect is from a government agent working out of Colombia who appreciates Jim's ability to "get things done." Jim accepts, warned not to marry a foreigner, and ordered to report to FLETC.
Mike visits Sylvia with the news he's gotten a real job with a company managed by an old friend. She calms down and they make love. Jim arrives and tells her Mike is coming to Mexico with him for the weekend as a last chance to hang out. Despite Sylvia's opposition, Mike accompanies Jim and Toussant to Mexico. They attend a party where Marta reveals she's pregnant. Jim responds violently, threatening to punch her in the stomach and shoot her in the head. Mike convinces Toussant and Jim it's time to leave. Jim drives home in a belligerent state as Toussant gives him an ultimatum to either seek counseling or he'll cut off all contact until he does.
Jim reveals to Mike he is transporting 20 kilograms of marijuana. When Mike protests, Jim pulls a gun, then breaks down, horrified at what he's becoming. Mike agrees to accompany Jim to the drug deal and realizes one of the buyers is the same man they had earlier robbed. A gunfight erupts and the man is killed. The rest of the buyers plead for their lives, but Jim kills them also. As Jim and Mike escape, a bystander in a nearby house shoots at their car hitting Jim in the back and face and paralyzing him. Jim urges Mike to "step up" and shoot him to end his suffering.

documents.title: Shine a Light
documents.tagline: A master director shining his light on the best rock band on the planet.
documents.overview: Martin Scorsese and the Rolling Stones unite in "Shine A Light," a look at The Rolling Stones." Scorsese filmed the Stones over a two-day period at the intimate Beacon Theater in New York City in fall 2006. Cinematographers capture the raw energy of the legendary band.
documents.plot:
Shine a Light is a 2008 concert documentary directed by Martin Scorsese that captures the Rolling Stones performing at the Beacon Theatre in New York City during their A Bigger Bang Tour. The title comes from a song on the band's 1972 album Exile on Main St. Produced by Shangri-La Entertainment among others, the film was the last release from Paramount Classics before the company was folded into Paramount Vantage, and it marked Scorsese's first use of digital cinematography, employed for the backstage scenes.

Scorsese filmed two benefit shows on 29 October and 1 November 2006, both added to the tour specifically for the shoot, although all the concert footage in the final cut comes from the second night. The concert is preceded by a brief, partly staged prologue showing the preparations showing the director and his crew getting ready for the shoot, and the music is intercut with archival news clips and old interviews with Jagger, Keith Richards, Charlie Watts and Ronnie Wood that trace the band's long career and its reputation for excess and endurance. Guest performers join the band on stage, including Jack White, the blues guitarist Buddy Guy and Christina Aguilera, while backing musicians such as Blondie Chaplin and Tim Ries also appear. The audience included Bill and Hillary Clinton, and the concerts raised money for the Clinton Foundation. The set list differed from the usual tour shows, and Jagger joked that this might be the only Scorsese film without "Gimme Shelter". Before the first show, Atlantic Records co-founder Ahmet Ertegun fell backstage and later died from his injuries, and the film is dedicated to him.

Originally planned for September 2007, the release was pushed back to 2008. The film had its world premiere at the 58th Berlin International Film Festival on 7 February 2008, opened in April with screenings in IMAX theaters as well as standard cinemas, and was accompanied by a soundtrack album on the Universal label. It grossed about $16.2 million worldwide. Reviews were mostly positive, with an 85% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 76, critics noting that while it offered little new for longtime fans, it vividly conveyed the energy of the band's live show.

documents.title: Before the Devil Knows You're Dead
documents.original_title: Before the Devil Knows You're Dead
documents.tagline: No one was supposed to get hurt.

documents.title: Caramel
documents.overview: In a beauty salon in Beirut the lives of five women cross paths. The beauty salon is a colorful and sensual microcosm where they share and entrust their hopes, fears and expectations.
documents.plot:
Caramel (Arabic: Sukkar banat) is a 2007 Lebanese comedy-drama and the feature directorial debut of Nadine Labaki, who co-wrote it with Rodney El Haddad and Jihad Hojeily and also stars. It premiered in the Directors' Fortnight at the 2007 Cannes Film Festival, where it was nominated for the Caméra d'Or. The title refers to a hair-removal method using heated sugar, and the film portrays Beirut not as a city defined by war but as a warm, lively place where people face universal problems.

The story centres on a beauty salon in Beirut and the intersecting lives of five women. Layale, who runs the salon and lives with her parents, is caught in a hopeless affair with a married man, waiting for his calls and arranging secret meetings that never quite work out. A shy traffic policeman, Youssef, watches her from across the street and is clearly in love with her, though she barely notices him.

Her colleague Nisrine, a Muslim, is about to marry her fiancé Bassam, but she is no longer a virgin and fears the consequences in a conservative society, so she secretly seeks out a doctor to have her virginity surgically restored. The third worker, Rima, is quietly attracted to women, and finds herself drawn to a mysterious customer with long hair who comes in to have it washed.

Jamale, a regular client and aspiring actress, is terrified of growing old, attending auditions alongside much younger women and going to great lengths to hide the signs of ageing. Next door, the seamstress Rose has devoted her life to looking after her eccentric elder sister Lili. When an elderly gentleman, Charles, brings in clothes to be altered, he and Rose begin a gentle romance, the first of her life, but she ultimately sacrifices it out of duty to Lili.

As the women support one another through these private struggles, the film touches on forbidden love, family tradition, sexuality, ageing and the conflict between duty and desire, while avoiding any direct reference to the country's politics or conflicts. It ends with Nisrine's wedding and small moments of hope.

Caramel was acclaimed by critics, with 94% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and became a notable international success for a Lebanese film, earning about 15 million dollars worldwide.

documents.title: The Wolfman
documents.tagline: When the moon is full the legend comes to life
documents.overview: Lawrence Talbot, an American man on a visit to Victorian London to make amends with his estranged father, gets bitten by a werewolf and, after a moonlight transformation, leaves him with a savage hunger for flesh.
documents.plot:
The Wolfman is a 2010 American horror film directed by Joe Johnston and produced by Universal Pictures. The movie is a remake of the 1941 classic of the same name, starring Lon Chaney Jr.

The story begins with Lawrence Talbot (played by Benicio del Toro), a young man who returns to his family's estate in England after being away for several years. His father, Sir John Talbot (played by Hugh Griffith), is dying and wants to pass on the family legacy to Lawrence. However, their relationship is strained due to Lawrence's troubled past.

Upon his return, Lawrence meets his half-brother, Jack (played by Anthony Hopkins), who has been taking care of the estate in his father's absence. Jack is a cruel and manipulative man who resents Lawrence for being the favored son. The two brothers engage in a heated argument, which ends with Jack's death.

Lawrence soon discovers that he has become a werewolf after being bitten by a mysterious woman named Anna Valerious (played by Emily Blunt). As the full moon approaches, Lawrence begins to experience strange and terrifying transformations, losing control of his actions and succumbing to his primal instincts.

As the story unfolds, Lawrence becomes increasingly isolated and withdrawn, unable to cope with his newfound condition. He turns to Anna for help, but she is revealed to be a vampire who has been using her powers to manipulate him. The two engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Lawrence struggling to maintain control over his transformations.

Meanwhile, Jack's death is revealed to have been orchestrated by Anna, who had been seeking revenge against the Talbot family for their past wrongdoings. As the full moon rises, Lawrence becomes more and more aggressive, putting those around him in danger.

In a climactic confrontation, Lawrence manages to defeat Anna and destroy her powers, but not before she reveals that he is indeed a werewolf and that his condition will be passed down to his descendants. The movie ends with Lawrence, now fully embracing his curse, walking away from the estate, ready to face the challenges of his new life as a monster.

Throughout the film, director Joe Johnston pays homage to the classic Universal Monsters movies, incorporating nods to Dracula and Frankenstein into the narrative. The Wolfman is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of identity, family, and the struggle for control over one's own destiny.

documents.title: The Kite Runner
documents.tagline: There is a way to be good again.
documents.overview: After spending years in California, Amir returns to his homeland in Afghanistan to help his old friend Hassan, whose son is in trouble.
documents.plot:
The Kite Runner is a 2007 American drama directed by Marc Forster from a screenplay by David Benioff, adapted from Khaled Hosseini's 2003 bestselling novel. Khalid Abdalla stars as the adult Amir, with Atossa Leoni, Shaun Toub, Homayoun Ershadi and the young actors Zekeria Ebrahimi and Ahmad Khan Mahmoodzada. The story spans decades of Afghan upheaval, from the fall of the monarchy to the Taliban era.

In San Francisco in 2000, Afghan-American novelist Amir receives a phone call from Rahim Khan, his late father's old friend, now living in Peshawar. The film then returns to Kabul in 1978, where ten-year-old Amir lives a privileged life as the son of a wealthy, freethinking Pashtun businessman he calls Baba. His closest companion is Hassan, the son of Baba's loyal Hazara servant Ali, who serves as Amir's devoted "kite runner" in the city's kite-fighting contests. After Amir wins a tournament, Hassan chases down the last fallen kite for him and is cornered and sexually assaulted by the bully Assef. Amir witnesses the attack but does nothing, and, consumed by shame, he drives Hassan away by framing him for theft, prompting Ali and his son to leave the household.

After the Soviet invasion, Baba and Amir flee to Pakistan and settle in California, where Amir grows up, marries Soraya, the daughter of an exiled general, and becomes a writer. Summoned to Peshawar, the dying Rahim Khan tells him that Hassan and his wife were killed by the Taliban, that their son Sohrab is in an orphanage in Kabul, and that Hassan was in fact Amir's half-brother. Seeking redemption, Amir travels into Taliban-ruled Afghanistan and finds that Sohrab is being held by a Taliban official who turns out to be Assef. After a brutal confrontation, Amir escapes with the boy and eventually brings him to America, where he teaches Sohrab to fly kites as Hassan once did for him.

Much of the film was shot in Kashgar in western China. Most of the dialogue is in Dari. Fearing reprisals against the child actors over the assault scene, the studio delayed the release by six weeks to December 14, 2007, and helped relocate the boys; the film was banned in Afghanistan. It grossed $73.2 million on a $20 million budget, received moderately positive reviews and was nominated for the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film, while Alberto Iglesias's score earned Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations.

documents.title: The Lovely Bones
documents.tagline: The story of a life and everything that came after...
documents.overview: After being brutally murdered, 14-year-old Susie Salmon watches from heaven over her grief-stricken family -- and her killer. As she observes their daily lives, she must balance her thirst for revenge with her desire for her family to heal.
documents.plot:
In 1973, 14-year-old Susie Salmon dreams of becoming a photographer. One day, Ray, a boy she has a crush on, asks her out. As Susie walks home through a cornfield, she runs into her neighbor, George Harvey, who coaxes her into an underground "kid's hideout" he has built. Inside, Susie grows uncomfortable and attempts to leave; Harvey grabs her and the scene fades until she is seen rushing past her alarmed classmate Ruth Connors, fleeing Harvey's den.
When Susie fails to return home from school, her father, Jack, searches for her, while her mother, Abigail, waits for the police. In town, Susie sees Jack, who does not respond to her when she calls. Susie runs home to find Harvey soaking in a bathtub. After seeing the bloody bathroom and her bracelet hanging on the sink faucet, Susie realizes she never actually escaped the hideout and Harvey murdered her. She is pulled into the "In-Between", which is neither Heaven nor Earth. From there, Susie watches over her family. Holly, a friend she makes, urges her to let go but she resists.
Jack believes Susie was murdered by someone she knew. He researches neighbors and eventually suspects Harvey is the killer. Detective Fenerman is unable to find proof, as Harvey has carefully concealed the evidence. Susie's sister, Lindsey, agrees with Jack's suspicions, but their casework takes a toll on Abigail. Abigail's alcoholic mother, Lynn, moves into the house. Feeling alienated from her husband, Abigail goes to California.
Susie, in her afterlife, learns that Harvey, who has targeted Lindsey as his next victim, has murdered six other girls, including Holly. Harvey has stuffed Susie's body into a large safe in his basement.
One night, Jack, carrying a baseball bat, trails Harvey into the cornfield. However, Jack accidentally stumbles across a teen couple named Clarissa and Brian. Brian, thinking they will be assaulted, bludgeons Jack nearly to death while Clarissa begs him to stop, and Harvey watches nearby. As Jack recuperates, Lindsey breaks into Harvey's house looking for evidence that he killed Susie. Upstairs, she finds a notebook containing a sketch of the underground den, a lock of Susie's hair, and news articles about Susie's disappearance.
Harvey returns and almost catches Lindsey, but she escapes and rushes home to discover that her mother has returned. She gives the notebook to her grandmother, who contacts the police. Harvey has already fled his home – taking the safe containing Susie's body with him.
Susie's afterlife begins expanding into a larger heaven, and she is greeted by Harvey's other victims. She resists Holly's urging her to enter Heaven along with the others, claiming she has one final thing to do. Meanwhile, Susie's classmates Ruth and Ray are present when Harvey drives up to dispose of the safe at a sinkhole dump site on the Connors' property. Susie returns to Earth and enters Ruth's body, causing Ruth to faint. Ray rushes to Ruth's aid only to realize she has become Susie.

documents.title: Penelope
documents.tagline: A fairytale like no other.
documents.overview: Forlorn heiress Penelope Wilhern is cursed, and the only way out is to fall in love with someone of suitable stock. But how can she find her soul mate when she's sequestered inside her family's estate with only her parents to keep her company. This untraditional fairy tale about a girl who bucks convention to create her own happy ending.
documents.plot:
Penelope is a fantasy romantic comedy directed by Mark Palansky from a screenplay by Leslie Caveny, first shown in 2006. Christina Ricci is Penelope Wilhern, an heiress born with a pig's snout because of a family curse, with James McAvoy as Johnny Martin, Catherine O'Hara and Richard E. Grant as her parents Jessica and Franklin, Peter Dinklage as the tabloid reporter Lemon, Simon Woods as the suitor Edward Vanderman III and Reese Witherspoon, who also produced the film, as the delivery girl Annie.

Generations ago, a servant, Clara, became pregnant by the aristocrat Ralph Wilhern, who married another woman at his parents' insistence; after Clara killed herself, her mother, a witch, cursed the family so that the next Wilhern daughter would have the face of a pig until loved by "one of her own kind". After five generations of sons, Penelope is born. Her mortified mother pretends the baby died and hides her in the family's London mansion, and once Penelope turns eighteen, a matchmaker parades blue-blooded suitors before her, convinced that marrying one will break the spell. All flee in horror, Edward among them, and he teams up with Lemon to prove she exists by hiring a gambler posing as the aristocrat Max Campion to photograph her with a hidden camera.

Talking through a one-way mirror, Penelope and "Max" fall for each other. When he sees her face he is startled but not afraid; ashamed, he destroys the camera, but refuses her plea to marry him. Fed up with confinement, Penelope runs away into the city with her face hidden by a scarf, selling photographs of herself to Lemon and befriending Annie. When her face is exposed in a pub, the public adores her, and Edward's father pressures his son into proposing. At the altar, Penelope realises she does not want to marry merely to lift the curse and declares that she likes herself as she is; because she has been loved by one of her own kind, herself, her snout vanishes. Now a schoolteacher, she learns that "Max" is really Johnny Martin and finds him at a Halloween party, where they kiss. The family butler, revealed to be the witch, silences Jessica with a last spell, and Lemon chooses not to photograph the happy couple.

Shot in London and at Pinewood Studios in early 2006 as Witherspoon's first production, Penelope premiered at the Toronto festival in September 2006, with Summit Entertainment later handling its American release. It grossed $21.2 million worldwide and drew mixed reviews, with 53% on Rotten Tomatoes.

With time running out and a deadly tracker on his trail, Burnett's commanding officer decides to risk his career and launch a renegade rescue mission to save his life.

documents.title: Highlander
documents.tagline: There can be only one.
documents.overview: He fought his first battle on the Scottish Highlands in 1536. He will fight his greatest battle on the streets of New York City in 1986. His name is Connor MacLeod. He is immortal.
documents.plot:
Highlander is a 1986 American fantasy adventure film directed by Russell Mulcahy and written by Gregory Widen. The movie stars Christopher Lambert as Connor MacLeod, a Scottish Highlander who discovers he is an immortal.

The story begins with Connor, a young man living in Scotland during the Jacobite rising of 1745. He witnesses the Battle of Culloden, where his clan is defeated, and he is mortally wounded. However, instead of dying, Connor is healed by Juan Sanchez Villa-Lobos Ramírez (Sean Connery), an immortal who has been watching over him.

Juan explains to Connor that immortals are born with a "prize," which is the essence of every human being's soul. The prize is what makes them unique and gives them their individuality. Immortals must find and kill other immortals in order to gain their prizes, thereby becoming more powerful and closer to achieving their ultimate goal: the Prize.

Connor learns that he has been chosen as a "Immortal" and that his prize is the soul of an unknown woman. He sets out on a journey across time and space to find her, while also being pursued by other immortals who seek to kill him.

As Connor travels through history, he encounters various characters, including Juan, who becomes his mentor and guide. Along the way, he meets other immortals, such as the Kurgan (Clancy Brown), a ruthless and cunning immortal who seeks to kill Connor and claim his prize for himself.

Throughout the movie, Connor's journey takes him from 18th-century Scotland to modern-day New York City. He faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including battles with other immortals and struggles with his own identity.

As the story unfolds, Connor becomes increasingly obsessed with finding the woman whose soul is his prize. He believes that she holds the key to understanding his purpose as an immortal and that their reunion will bring him peace and fulfillment.

The movie culminates in a final showdown between Connor and the Kurgan. The two immortals engage in a fierce battle, during which they exchange blows and insults. In the end, Connor emerges victorious, but not before the Kurgan reveals that he has been searching for the woman whose soul is Connor's prize.

In a surprising twist, it is revealed that the woman Connor was searching for all along is actually his own wife, who had died in childbirth. The movie ends with Connor finally finding peace and understanding, as he realizes that his true prize is not the soul of another person, but rather the love and connection he shares with those around him.

Overall, Highlander is a classic tale of immortality, adventure, and self-discovery. With its unique blend of action, drama, and fantasy elements, it has become a beloved cult classic among fans of science fiction and adventure movies.

documents.title: Gigli
documents.tagline: Life doesn't play by the rules.
documents.overview: Gigli is ordered to kidnap the psychologically challenged younger brother of a powerful federal prosecutor. When plans go awry, Gigli's boss sends in Ricki, a gorgeous free-spirited female gangster who has her own set of orders to assist with the kidnapping. But Gigli begins falling for the decidedly unavailable Ricki, which could be a hazard to his occupation.
documents.plot:
Gigli is a 2003 American romantic comedy crime film written, co-produced and directed by Martin Brest for Revolution Studios. Ben Affleck stars as Larry Gigli, a small-time Los Angeles mobster, and Jennifer Lopez as Ricki, a fellow enforcer sent to keep an eye on him, with Justin Bartha as Brian, Lenny Venito as Louis, Al Pacino as Starkman, Christopher Walken as Detective Stanley Jacobellis and Lainie Kazan in a supporting role.

Larry Gigli is a low-level hoodlum eager to prove that he is tougher and more capable than he really is. His boss, Louis, orders him to kidnap Brian, the intellectually disabled younger brother of a federal prosecutor, so that the prosecutor can be pressured into helping the New York mob boss Starkman stay out of prison. Larry lures Brian away by promising to take him "to the Baywatch", the television series he is obsessed with, but Louis does not trust him to handle the job alone and sends a woman calling herself Ricki to supervise. Larry is instantly attracted to her and resents taking orders from her, and his advances are rebuffed when she tells him that she is a lesbian. Hiding out in Larry's apartment, the trio grows more volatile; Brian keeps demanding to go to "the Baywatch" and runs up huge phone bills calling an Australian operator because he loves the accent. When Louis orders them to cut off Brian's thumb and mail it to the prosecutor, a horrified Larry instead steals a thumb from a corpse in a hospital morgue. As Larry opens up about himself and his frustrations, Ricki softens, and the two sleep together. Summoned before Starkman, they learn that he never approved the kidnapping and is furious, all the more because the thumb does not match Brian's fingerprints and so exposes the bluff. He kills Louis for drawing police attention and is ready to kill them too, until Ricki argues that only they can contain the damage. Spared, the pair decide to leave the mob. Driving along the coast with Brian, they come upon a beach video shoot that looks like Baywatch, and they let him off there, where he is delighted to meet an Australian woman. Larry urges Ricki to drive off without him, but she turns back, and they leave together to start a new life.

Released by Sony on 1 August 2003 amid intense coverage of the stars' off-screen romance, the film was savaged by critics, earning 6% on Rotten Tomatoes and 18 on Metacritic, and grossed $7.3 million on a budget of $75.6 million, one of the costliest flops in history.
