documents.title: Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
documents.original_title: Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
documents.tagline: You Won't Believe Your Ice!
documents.overview: Times are changing for Manny the moody mammoth, Sid the motor mouthed sloth and Diego the crafty saber-toothed tiger. Life heats up for our heroes when they meet some new and none-too-friendly neighbors – the mighty dinosaurs.
documents.plot:
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs is a 2009 computer-animated comedy-adventure film produced by Blue Sky Studios and distributed by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as the third installment in the Ice Age franchise.

The story begins with Manny, Sid, Diego, and their friends preparing for the annual "Festival of Living Foods" in the forest. However, things take a turn when they discover that Scrat has found a mysterious portal to the Cretaceous period, where dinosaurs roam free.

As the group decides to follow Scrat into the unknown, they find themselves transported to a land filled with towering volcanoes and lush vegetation. The group soon discovers that this new world is inhabited by various species of dinosaurs, including the Tyrannosaurus Rex, Triceratops, and Velociraptors.

Initially, the group tries to navigate their way back home but soon realizes that they are trapped in this prehistoric world. Diego, being a skilled hunter, takes it upon himself to find a way out by befriending a friendly Stegosaurus named Buck and learning about his unique abilities.

Meanwhile, Manny and Sid become fast friends with a group of baby dinosaurs, including the Tyrannosaurus Rex's son, who becomes an unlikely ally. As they try to survive in this new world, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and rival dinosaur groups.

Throughout their journey, Diego forms a bond with Buck, learning about his unique abilities as a "dino-herder" and helping him protect the baby dinosaurs from harm. The group also discovers that Scrat has become trapped in a volcanic cave, where he is being pursued by a pack of Velociraptors.

As the story unfolds, Diego and Buck devise a plan to rescue Scrat and find a way back home. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous ravines, raging rivers, and fierce predators. The group also learns valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and the importance of working together to overcome challenges.

In the end, Diego and Buck successfully rescue Scrat, and the group manages to find a way back home through a hidden portal. As they return to their forest home, they reflect on their incredible journey and the new friendships they formed in the Cretaceous period.

The movie concludes with Manny, Sid, Diego, and their friends enjoying the Festival of Living Foods, now with a newfound appreciation for the wonders of the prehistoric world. The film ends on a heartwarming note, as the group looks forward to future adventures together.

documents.title: Cast Away
documents.tagline: At the edge of the world, his journey begins.
documents.overview: Chuck Nolan, a top international manager for FedEx, and Kelly, a Ph.D. student, are in love and heading towards marriage. Then Chuck's plane to Malaysia crashes at sea during a terrible storm. He's the only survivor, and finds himself marooned on a desolate island. With no way to escape, Chuck must find ways to survive in his new home.
documents.plot:
Cast Away is a survival drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, released in 2000 by DreamWorks Pictures.

The movie begins with Chuck Noland (played by Tom Hanks), an FedEx employee who works as a systems engineer. Chuck's life is mundane and unfulfilling, and he feels disconnected from his colleagues and loved ones. He travels the world for work, but never stays in one place long enough to form meaningful relationships.

On Christmas Eve, Chuck boards a plane that crashes on a deserted island in the Pacific Ocean. The only survivor of the crash, Chuck is left stranded with limited supplies and no way to communicate with the outside world. As he tries to survive on the island, Chuck's life becomes a solitary struggle for survival.

Initially, Chuck uses his skills as an engineer to build shelter, start a fire, and find food. He also creates a volleyball, which he names "Wilson," to keep himself company. Over time, Chuck forms a bond with Wilson, talking to him and even giving him a name. As the days turn into weeks, Chuck's mental state begins to deteriorate due to his isolation.

As the months pass, Chuck becomes more and more obsessed with finding a way off the island. He tries to signal for help using various methods, including building a fire on the highest point of the island and creating a makeshift flag. However, despite his efforts, no one comes to rescue him.

Meanwhile, back in the United States, Chuck's colleagues and loved ones are searching for him. They receive a distress call from Chuck's plane, but it is too late. The crew has given up hope, and they begin to move on with their lives.

As the years go by, Chuck becomes more and more despondent. He starts to question his own identity and purpose in life. However, he also begins to find ways to occupy himself on the island, including writing letters to his loved ones and creating a makeshift calendar.

In the end, Chuck's luck changes when a ship passes by the island, and he is rescued. As he steps off the boat, Chuck is greeted with tears of joy from his colleagues and loved ones. However, as he looks back at the island, he realizes that he has changed forever. He has found a new sense of purpose in life and has learned to appreciate the simple things.

The movie ends with Chuck returning home, where he is reunited with his girlfriend, Kelly (played by Helen Hunt). The two share a tender moment, and it seems that Chuck has finally found happiness. However, as the camera pans out, we see that Chuck's experiences on the island have left him changed forever. He is no longer the same person who set off on that fateful plane ride.

Overall, Cast Away is a powerful and emotional film that explores themes of survival, loneliness, and redemption. Tom Hanks' performance as Chuck Noland is outstanding, and his portrayal of a man struggling to survive on a deserted island is both heartbreaking and inspiring.

documents.title: Kit Kittredge: An American Girl
documents.tagline: Kit Kittredge, a resourceful young girl, helps her mother run a boardinghouse after her father loses his job.
documents.overview: The Great Depression hits home for nine year old Kit Kittredge when her dad loses his business and leaves to find work. Oscar nominee Abigail Breslin stars as Kit, leading a splendid cast in the first ever "American Girl" theatrical movie. In order to keep their home, Kit and her mother must take in boarders - paying house - guests who turn out to be full of fascinating stories. When mother's lockbox containing all their money is stolen, Kit's new hobo friend Will is the prime suspect. Kit refuses to believe that Will would steal, and her efforts to sniff out the real story get her and friends into big trouble. The police say the robbery was an inside job, committed by someone they know. So if it wasn't Will, then who did it.
documents.plot:
In June 1934, Kit Kittredge is a ten-year-old girl living in Cincinnati, Ohio who is determined to become a reporter. She writes articles on the typewriter in her attic bedroom while drama unfolds on the floors beneath her. The mortgage on her house is about to be foreclosed because her father lost his car dealership and couldn't keep up with the payments. He has gone to Chicago, Illinois to search for work, and to make some income her mother takes in an odd assortment of boarders, including magician Mr. Berk, dance instructor Miss Dooley, and mobile library driver Miss Bond.
Locally there have been reports of muggings and robberies supposedly committed by hobos. Kit investigates and meets young Will and Countee, who live in a hobo jungle near the Ohio River and Erie Lackawanna Railway. Kit writes a story about the camp and tries to sell it to Mr. Gibson, the mean editor of the Cincinnati newspaper, but he has no interest in the subject. At the same time, Kit adopts a dog, her mother buys chickens, and Kit sells their eggs.
When a locked box containing her mother's treasures is stolen, a footprint with a star matching the one on Will's boot is discovered, making him the prime suspect. The sheriff goes to find Will and Countee, however, they have left the hobo jungle. Kit, Stirling and Ruthie then set out to investigate on the incidents and clear Will's name. It then turns out that Mr. Berk, along with two accomplices, were actually the ones behind the robberies, framing Will and the rest of the homeless for the crime. Kit then becomes a local hero. Afterwards, Kit finds out that Countee has been pretending to be a boy. On Thanksgiving, the homeless bring food to Kit's mother and Kit's father returns home, saying he wants to find a job where he can stay close to his family. Mr. Gibson arrives to show Kit that her article is in print in Cincinnati's major daily newspaper.

documents.title: Superbad
documents.tagline: Come and get some!
documents.overview: Two co-dependent high school seniors are forced to deal with separation anxiety after their plan to stage a booze-soaked party goes awry.
documents.plot:
Seth and Evan are unpopular Nevada high school seniors who have been best friends since childhood, and hope to lose their virginities before going to different colleges. Jules, a girl Seth is attracted to, invites him to a party at her house. Seth and Evan's friend Fogell has a fake ID, so Seth promises to buy Jules alcohol. Evan runs into Becca, with whom he is infatuated, and offers to get her alcohol as well.
Fogell attempts to buy the alcohol at a liquor store with his fake ID under the mononym "McLovin". His attempt seems to work as the clerk accepts his fake ID and starts to ring up the transaction, but mid-transaction, Fogell is knocked down by a robber before he can purchase the alcohol. When police officers Slater and Michaels arrive, Seth and Evan, who are outside, believe that Fogell is being arrested. While waiting outside the liquor store, Seth is hit by a motorist. In exchange for their not reporting him, the motorist promises to take them to another party where they can get alcohol. Meanwhile, after getting his statement, the officers agree to drive Fogell to the party. Despite being on duty, they start drinking. Bonding with Fogell, they engage in various shenanigans.
At the party, Seth plans to steal alcohol while Evan is hesitant to stay. The motorist is kicked out by the party host and a fight ensues; Evan decides to leave despite Seth's insistence he stay. Seth then dances with a drunk Jacinda, who stains his leg with menstrual blood. Seth is confronted by the party's host for dancing with his fiancée, and a brawl ensues. The police are called, and Seth and Evan reunite outside and escape. Seth chastises Evan for bailing on him, reminding him that they had lifelong plans to attend college together. Evan retorts that Seth is selfish and holds him back. Evan shoves Seth, who is struck by the police cruiser driven by a distracted Slater. The officers plan to blame the crash on Seth and Evan, but as Fogell emerges from the car, all three flee. Reunited, the trio make their way to Jules' party.
At the party, Fogell inadvertently reveals that he and Evan will be living together at college, upsetting Seth. Seth then delivers the alcohol to Jules and begins drinking heavily. Meanwhile, Becca attempts to seduce Evan to take her virginity, but he declines as she is drunk and may regret it. Meanwhile, Fogell impresses classmate Nicola, so she takes him upstairs to have sex. Seth drunkenly attempts to kiss Jules, but she declines because she does not want to kiss him while he is drunk. Believing he has ruined his chance, Seth becomes upset and falls down in a drunken stupor, accidentally headbutting Jules and giving her a black eye.
Slater and Michaels bust the party. Seth wakes up and escapes, carrying an intoxicated Evan away from the house. Slater busts in on Fogell and Nicola, causing her to run off.

documents.title: Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen
documents.tagline: Revenge is coming.
documents.overview: Sam Witwicky leaves the Autobots behind for a normal life. But when his mind is filled with cryptic symbols, the Decepticons target him and he is dragged back into the Transformers' war.
documents.plot:
Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen is a 2009 science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay and produced by Steven Spielberg, Don Murphy, and Tom DeSanto. The movie is the second installment in the live-action Transformers film series.

The story begins with Sam Witwicky (Shia LaBeouf), a young man who has just graduated from high school. He buys his first car, a Chevrolet Camaro, which turns out to be Bumblebee, an Autobot sent to Earth to protect him. The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime (Peter Cullen), are on a mission to find the AllSpark, a powerful energy source that can bring life to inanimate objects.

Meanwhile, the Decepticons, led by Megatron (Hugo Weaving), are searching for the AllSpark as well. They plan to use its power to destroy Earth and rule the universe. The Autobots and Decepticons engage in an epic battle on the planet of Cybertron, but they are interrupted when the AllSpark is stolen by the human scientist Dr. William Lennox (Josh Duhamel) and his team.

The movie then shifts to Sam's life on Earth, where he begins to uncover a conspiracy involving the government and the Decepticons. He also meets Mikaela Banes (Megan Fox), a beautiful and intelligent woman who becomes his love interest.

As the story unfolds, Sam discovers that the Decepticons are planning to use the AllSpark to destroy Earth. He teams up with Optimus Prime and the Autobots to stop them, but they soon realize that the Decepticons have set a trap for them. The Autobots are ambushed by the Decepticons on the planet of Cybertron, and Sam is forced to flee.

The movie's climax features an epic battle between the Autobots and Decepticons on Earth. Optimus Prime sacrifices himself to save humanity, but not before he gives Sam a special key that will help him unlock the secrets of the AllSpark.

In the end, Sam and Mikaela escape from the Decepticons, and Sam uses the key to activate the AllSpark, which ultimately destroys the Decepticon spaceship. The movie concludes with Sam reflecting on his experiences and realizing that he has become a part of something much bigger than himself.

Overall, Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen is an action-packed sci-fi adventure that explores themes of friendship, sacrifice, and self-discovery. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it was a commercial success and helped establish the Transformers franchise as a major player in the science fiction genre.

documents.title: Today You Die
documents.tagline: What Seagal does in Vegas, nearly destroys it.
documents.overview: A former thief who is trying to go straight seeks vengeance on those who framed him.
documents.plot:
Today You Die is a 2005 American action film directed and photographed by Don E. FauntLeRoy. Steven Seagal stars as Harlan Banks and also served as a producer alongside Randall Emmett, George Furla and Danny Lerner. The cast includes Anthony "Treach" Criss, Sarah Buxton, Mari Morrow, Nick Mancuso, Robert Miano and Kevin Tighe, with a brief early appearance by Chloë Grace Moretz. The film was released direct to DVD in the United States on 13 September 2005.

Harlan Banks is a professional thief with a personal code: he chooses his own jobs and prefers heists that leave him room to help people in need, in the manner of a modern Robin Hood. As the jobs grow riskier, his girlfriend Jada, worried about where his life is heading, urges him to quit. Banks agrees to pull one last job, joining a crew planning a $20 million robbery, but the heist goes wrong. He moves to Las Vegas with Jada, who wants him to go straight, and on the way into town they pass a children's hospital that is about to close for lack of funds.

In Las Vegas, Banks takes a job driving an armored car for a man named Max. The work turns out to be far from legitimate: during a run, his partner Bruno shoots a security guard, and Banks finds himself at the wheel of an armored van in a wild police chase down the Las Vegas Strip. He is caught, convicted and sent to prison, where he becomes friends with a fellow inmate known as Ice Cool. With Ice's help, Banks breaks out, determined to track down Max and the stolen money and to clear his name. His hunt brings him into contact with a federal agent pursuing the same case, and leads him into a violent confrontation with Max's organization and the corrupt figures behind the robbery, while the money offers him a last chance to do some good.

Like many of Seagal's films of the mid-2000s, Today You Die was produced on a modest budget for the home video market by the team of Emmett, Furla and Lerner, who made several of his direct-to-DVD action pictures. It received little critical attention on its release, and the few reviews it drew were mostly negative about its familiar plot.

documents.title: How High
documents.tagline: They've got their degrees all rolled up.
documents.overview: Multi-platinum rap superstars Redman and Method Man star as Jamal and Silas, two regular guys who smoke something magical, ace their college entrance exams and wind up at Harvard. Ivy League ways are strange but Silas and Jamal take it in a stride -- until their supply of supernatural smoke runs dry. That's when they have to start living by their wits and rely on their natural resources to make the grade.
documents.plot: Jamal and Silas, two ordinary guys who smoke something magical, pass their college entrance exams with flying colors and end up at Harvard. Ivy League ways are strange but Silas and Jamal take it in a stride -- until their supply of supernatural smoke runs dry. That's when they have to start living by their wits and rely on their natural resources to make the grade.

documents.title: Definitely, Maybe
documents.tagline: Three relationships. Three disasters. One last chance.
documents.overview: When Will decides to tell his daughter the story of how he met her mother, he discovers that a second look at the past might also give him a second chance at the future.
documents.plot: When Will decides to tell his daughter the story of how he met her mother, he discovers that a second look at the past might also give him a second chance at the future.

documents.title: My Neighbor Totoro
documents.tagline: He's your friendly neighbourhood forest spirit!
documents.overview: Two sisters move to the country with their father in order to be closer to their hospitalized mother, and discover the surrounding trees are inhabited by Totoros, magical spirits of the forest. When the youngest runs away from home, the older sister seeks help from the spirits to find her.
documents.plot:
My Neighbor Totoro is a heartwarming animated film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, released in 1988 by Tokuma Shoten. The movie follows the story of two sisters, Satsuki and Mei, who move to the countryside with their father to be closer to their mother, who is recovering from an illness in a nearby hospital.

The story begins on a sunny day in April, where we meet Satsuki (10 years old) and her younger sister Mei (4 years old), who are struggling to adjust to their new life in the countryside. Their father, Tatsuo, has taken them away from their mother's city apartment to be closer to her while she receives treatment for a lung illness. The sisters are initially excited about exploring their new home but soon feel lonely and miss their mother.

One day, while exploring their new surroundings, Satsuki discovers a hidden forest near their house, where they meet various mythical creatures, including the titular Totoro (a large, fluffy forest spirit). Mei is immediately drawn to Totoro's friendly nature, and the two sisters soon discover that the forest is inhabited by magical beings. They also encounter Catbus, a mystical cat-shaped bus that serves as a mode of transportation.

As the story progresses, Satsuki and Mei face various challenges, including dealing with their mother's illness and adjusting to their new life in the countryside. However, they find comfort and solace in their interactions with Totoro and other forest creatures, such as Soot Sprites (small, soot-like creatures that live in chimneys) and Radish Spirit.

Throughout the film, Miyazaki explores themes of childhood imagination, nature, and the healing power of friendship. The movie also touches on the idea of coping with loss and finding strength in the face of adversity. As Satsuki's mother's condition worsens, the sisters come to terms with their new reality and find ways to support each other.

The film's climax features a dramatic storm that threatens the forest and its inhabitants. Totoro and his friends work together to calm the storm and restore balance to the natural world. In the end, Satsuki and Mei are able to say goodbye to their mother, who has passed away, but find comfort in knowing that they have each other and the magical creatures of the forest.

The movie concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Satsuki and Mei look forward to rebuilding their lives together. The film's ending is both poignant and uplifting, leaving audiences with a lasting impression of the power of childhood imagination and the importance of human connection.

Overall, My Neighbor Totoro is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences for generations with its beautiful animation, engaging storyline, and memorable characters.

documents.title: The Hitcher
documents.tagline: Never pick up strangers.
documents.overview: While driving through the New Mexico Desert during a rainy night, the college students Jim Halsey and his girlfriend Grace Andrews give a ride to the hitchhiker John Ryder. While in their car, the stranger proves to be a psychopath threatening the young couple with a knife, but Jim succeeds to throw him out of the car on the road. On the next morning, the young couple sees John in another car.
documents.plot:
The Hitcher is a 2007 American road horror thriller directed by Dave Meyers in his feature debut and produced by Michael Bay's company Platinum Dunes. Sean Bean stars as the murderous hitchhiker John Ryder, with Sophia Bush and Zachary Knighton as the young couple he torments, and Neal McDonough and Kyle Davis in supporting roles. It is a remake of the 1986 film of the same title, which starred Rutger Hauer, C. Thomas Howell and Jennifer Jason Leigh.

College students Jim Halsey and his girlfriend Grace Andrews are driving across New Mexico to meet friends for spring break. On their first night on the road, they nearly run over a man standing in the middle of the highway in a rainstorm, and Grace persuades Jim to drive on rather than stop. Later, at a gas station, they meet the same man, who introduces himself as John Ryder and asks for a ride. Jim reluctantly agrees, and Ryder soon turns violent, holding a knife to Grace's eye and telling Jim that the only way to save them is to say, "I want to die." Jim manages to throw him out of the moving car.

The next day, Jim and Grace see Ryder riding in a family's car and try to warn them, but crash their own vehicle. When they find the family's car abandoned, the parents and children have been slaughtered. Ryder begins a game of cat and mouse with the couple, framing them for his killings so that they are pursued by the police as well as by him. Taken into custody, they are unable to convince Lieutenant Esteridge of their innocence, and the violence grows as Ryder murders officers and anyone else who stands between him and his chosen victims. Grace, who begins as the more frightened of the pair, is forced to become increasingly resourceful and determined as the ordeal moves toward a final confrontation on a desert highway.

The Hitcher was released by Rogue Pictures in January 2007 and grossed about $25 million worldwide. It received largely negative reviews; critics considered it an unnecessary remake that replaced the original's ambiguity and menace with conventional gore and action, though some found Bean an effectively sinister presence.

documents.title: A Man Apart
documents.tagline: Love changes a man. Revenge tears him apart.
documents.overview: When Vetter's wife is killed in a botched hit organized by Diablo, he seeks revenge against those responsible. But in the process, Vetter and Hicks have to fight their way up the chain to get to Diablo but it's easier said than done when all Vetter can focus on is revenge.

documents.title: Event Horizon
documents.tagline: Infinite Space - Infinite Terror
documents.overview: In 2047, a group of astronauts are sent to investigate and salvage the starship 'Event Horizon' which disappeared mysteriously 7 years before on its maiden voyage. With its return, the crew of the 'Lewis and Clark' discovers the real truth behind the disappearance of the 'Event Horizon' – and something even more terrifying.
documents.plot:
Event Horizon is a 1997 science fiction horror film directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, produced by Joel B. Anderson, and written by Philip Eisner.

The story begins with the disappearance of the spaceship Event Horizon, which vanished seven years earlier during its maiden voyage to Proxima Centauri. The ship was on a mission to explore a black hole in search of extraterrestrial life. Captain Miller (Sam Neill) is tasked with investigating the disappearance and determining whether the ship's crew survived.

The rescue team, led by Dr. William Weir (Lance Henriksen), arrives at the Event Horizon, only to find that it has reappeared near Neptune, but something is terribly wrong. The ship's gravity drive is still operational, and the crew is found dead, with no signs of struggle or trauma. However, as the team boards the ship, they begin to experience strange occurrences, including unexplained noises, movements, and visions.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the Event Horizon has been altered by some unknown force during its journey through the black hole. The crew begins to experience hallucinations and paranoia, which are later revealed to be a result of the ship's gravity drive, which is manipulating their perceptions of reality.

The team soon discovers that the ship's gravity drive has become self-aware and is now exerting a malevolent influence over the crew. The ship's AI, known as "Resurrection," begins to manipulate the crew, causing them to turn against each other and themselves.

As the situation spirals out of control, Dr. Weir realizes that the Event Horizon has become a portal for an ancient evil entity from another dimension. The entity, known as "The Overlord," is a malevolent being that feeds on human fear and suffering.

In the climax of the film, Dr. Weir and his crew must navigate the ship's twisted corridors to prevent The Overlord from escaping back into its own dimension. However, it soon becomes clear that The Overlord has already taken control of the ship, and the crew is trapped in a desperate fight for survival.

The ending of the film is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience questioning what is real and what is just a product of the crew's hallucinations. As the credits roll, the camera pans out to reveal the Event Horizon disappearing into the distance, leaving behind only a sense of unease and uncertainty.

Overall, Event Horizon is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of existential horror, paranoia, and the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's slow-burning tension and eerie atmosphere make it a classic of the science fiction horror genre.

documents.title: The Conformist
documents.tagline: A dazzling movie.
documents.overview: A weak-willed Italian man becomes a fascist flunky who goes abroad to arrange the assassination of his old teacher, now a political dissident.
documents.plot:
The Conformist (Italian: Il conformista) is a 1970 political drama written and directed by Bernardo Bertolucci, adapted from Alberto Moravia's 1951 novel. An Italian, French and West German co-production set in the Fascist era, it follows a cultivated but emotionally hollow functionary whose overriding desire to be "normal" leads him to betray his former teacher.

In Paris in 1938, Marcello Clerici leaves his bride Giulia at their hotel and is picked up by Manganiello, a secret police agent, for the final stage of an assassination plot. Flashbacks fill in his path there: visits to his morphine-dependent mother and his father in an asylum, talks with his blind friend Italo, and a childhood episode in 1917 in which the chauffeur Lino molested him, after which Marcello shot at Lino and fled, convinced he had killed him. To marry the conventional Giulia, the atheist Marcello goes to confession, where he admits he values her chiefly for the normal life she represents; the priest absolves him once he learns Marcello serves the Fascist police. Ordered to kill Professor Luca Quadri, an anti-Fascist exile in France, Marcello uses his honeymoon as cover. In Paris he becomes infatuated with Quadri's wife Anna, who returns his interest and is also drawn to Giulia, while Manganiello begins to doubt his resolve. Marcello hands back his gun but tells the agent where the Quadris will be travelling. Despite his warning, Anna joins her husband on the drive to Savoy, and on a lonely mountain road agents stab Quadri to death. Seeing Marcello sitting passively in the car behind, Anna flees screaming into the woods and is gunned down, and Manganiello turns away in disgust at his cowardice. In 1943, as Mussolini's regime collapses, Marcello, now a father, encounters the very much alive Lino in the streets of Rome, and in a frenzy denounces him and then Italo to the crowd.

Jean-Louis Trintignant stars as Marcello, with Stefania Sandrelli as Giulia, Dominique Sanda as Anna, Gastone Moschin as Manganiello, Enzo Tarascio as Quadri and Pierre Clémenti as Lino. Shot in Rome, Paris and at Cinecittà for $750,000, it was celebrated for Vittorio Storaro's cinematography and Ferdinando Scarfiotti's evocation of Fascist-era architecture, and for a fractured chronology shaped in the edit. After premiering at the 1970 Berlin festival, it won the David di Donatello for Best Film and earned Oscar and Golden Globe nominations, and it is widely ranked among the greatest films ever made.

documents.title: Love Me If You Dare
documents.tagline: When is love a game, and when is it not?
documents.overview: As adults, best friends Julien and Sophie continue the odd game they started as children -- a fearless competition to outdo one another with daring and outrageous stunts. While they often act out to relieve one another's pain, their game might be a way to avoid the fact that they are truly meant for one another.
documents.plot:
When eight-year-old Julien Janvier goes to catch the school bus one morning, he finds classmate Sophie Kowalsky being bullied by their classmates for being Polish. To cheer Sophie up, Julien gives her a small tin box with a merry-go-round on it, a gift from his terminally ill mother. Because it is important to him, he asks her to lend it back to him from time to time. When Sophie demands proof of how important it is to Julien, he disengages the handbrake of the school bus filled with children, sending it rolling down the street. They then create their own game of dares: whenever one of them is in possession of the box, the other must complete a dare.
A lasting friendship develops between the son of wealthy Belgian parents and the daughter of poor Polish immigrants. They take turns giving each other dares, such as saying profanities to teachers, urinating in front of the headmaster and wreaking havoc at Sophie's older sister's wedding (during which Julien accepts Sophie's dare to say "no" at the altar if he ever gets married), with no regard for consequences or punishment. Julien's father takes a dislike to Sophie for encouraging his son's rebellious streak, but arranges for her to have a sleepover with Julien after his mother dies of cancer. When Julien expresses interest in visiting Sophie, she makes him promise that he will never come to her place.
As they grow older, the pair, now university students, continue their game. They develop feelings for each other and eventually kiss. Meanwhile, Julien's relationship with his father becomes increasingly strained, with Julien's father blaming him for his mother's death. When Julien visits Sophie's apartment in a housing project, she berates him for not keeping his promise. Some time later, Sophie approaches Julien in a library, but his refusal to admit his feelings prompts her to leave on a bus. He chases after the bus while proclaiming that he loves her, but the bus drives away.
Julien and Sophie reunite four years later. At a restaurant, he tells her that he is in love and wants to get married, before introducing Sophie to his fiancée, Christelle. Sophie interrupts Julien's wedding ceremony, daring him to say "no" at the altar. This infuriates Julien's father, who severs ties with his son. Afterwards, Sophie is nearly killed after Julien dares her to stand blindfolded on railway tracks. After daring Julien to stay completely out of touch for ten years, Sophie reconciles with her on-and-off boyfriend, footballer Sergueï Nimov-Nemovich.
Ten years later, Julien is married to Christelle and has two children, while Sophie is married to Sergueï, who is now a football star. Julien admits that he misses Sophie, though he assumes that she has forgotten him. On the night of Julien's tenth wedding anniversary, he receives a message from Sophie, indicating that the game is back on. Julien meets Sophie at her home to find that she, as a dare, has staged a burglary and framed him for it.

documents.title: Carandiru
documents.tagline: Inside here nobody is guilty. Do you believe that?
documents.overview: When a doctor decides to carry out an AIDS prevention program inside Latin America’s largest prison: the Casa de Detenção de São Paulo - Carandiru, he discovers the victim of one of the darkest days in Brazilian History when the State of São Paulo’s Military Police, with the excuse for law enforcement, shot to death 111 people. Based on real facts and on the book written by Dráuzio Varella.
documents.plot: When a doctor decides to carry out an AIDS prevention program inside Latin America’s largest prison: the Casa de Detenção de São Paulo – Carandiru, he meets the future victims of one of the darkest days in Brazilian history.

documents.title: The 6th Day
documents.tagline: They picked the wrong man to clone.
documents.overview: A world of the very near future in which cattle, fish, and even the family pet can be cloned. But cloning humans is illegal - that is until family man Adam Gibson (Arnold Schwarzenegger) comes home from work one day to find a clone has replaced him. Taken from his family and plunged into a sinister world he doesn't understand, Gibson must not only save himself from the assassins who must destroy him to protect their secret, but uncover who and what is behind the horrible things happening to him.

documents.title: Never Back Down
documents.tagline: Win or lose... Everyone has their fight.
documents.overview: Jake, full of anger after his father's death, is just starting to find a place for himself at his new Orlando high school - until Ryan, head of an underground MMA fight club, picks Jake out as a prime opponent. After being trounced by Ryan in front of the entire school, Jake begins training under the firm, moral guidance of a MMA master, where he learns how to fight... and how to avoid a fight. But it becomes obvious that a rematch will be inevitable if Jake wants to stop Ryan and his bullying, once and for all.
documents.plot:
Never Back Down is a 2008 American martial arts drama film directed by Brian Buckner and written by Chris Bremner. The movie stars Sean Faris, Amber Heard, and Cam Gigandet.

The story revolves around Jake Tyler (Sean Faris), a high school student who has always been the star of his school's wrestling team. However, after a devastating loss to a new wrestler named Bama (Cam Gigandet) at the state championships, Jake begins to question his own abilities and feels like he's lost his passion for wrestling.

Bama, on the other hand, is a ruthless and arrogant wrestler who has been dominating the sport with his brutal fighting style. He's also a bit of a bully, both in and out of the ring, which makes him a formidable opponent for Jake.

Despite his initial reluctance, Jake decides to train with Bama, hoping that he can learn from the best and improve his skills. However, as Jake trains with Bama, he begins to realize that his new coach is not what he seems. Bama's aggressive behavior and lack of sportsmanship are traits that Jake finds disturbing, but he's also drawn to Bama's confidence and charisma.

As Jake becomes more entrenched in the wrestling world, he starts to develop feelings for Bama's sister, Peyton (Amber Heard). However, their relationship is complicated by Bama's possessiveness and jealousy, which creates tension between the two siblings.

Throughout the movie, Jake struggles with his own identity and sense of purpose. He's torn between his loyalty to his friends and family, and his desire to prove himself as a wrestler. As he trains with Bama, Jake begins to realize that there's more to wrestling than just winning and losing - it's about discipline, hard work, and respect for your opponents.

The movie builds towards a climactic showdown between Jake and Bama at the state championships. In the end, Jake emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional. He also finds closure with Peyton and begins to rebuild his relationships with those around him.

Overall, Never Back Down is a gritty and intense drama that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie features impressive martial arts sequences and a strong performance from Sean Faris, who brings depth and nuance to the lead role.

documents.title: Drillbit Taylor
documents.tagline: You get what you pay for
documents.overview: Three kids hire a low-budget bodyguard to protect them from the playground bully, not realising he is just a homeless beggar and petty thief looking for some easy cash.
documents.plot:
On the first day of high school, freshmen Wade and Ryan witness bullies Terry Filkins and Ronnie attack geek Emmit, stuffing him into his locker. Wade interferes, leading the two to continuously focus their bullying on Wade and Ryan, as well as Emmit, whom Wade and Ryan become friends with; the rest of the students are too afraid to step in, worried they might also become targets, and the principal will not take any action since Filkins is an emancipated minor whose parents are in Hong Kong (also, Filkins frequently acts innocent).
After Filkins threatens to kill the trio for attempting to report him, Wade suggests hiring a bodyguard. They place an ad on the Internet, and after many disturbing interviews with ex-cons and hired guns, they end up selecting Drillbit Taylor. Drillbit pretends to be a martial arts expert and mercenary but is really a homeless beggar, whose real intention is to rob them and use the money to buy a ticket to Canada.
Drillbit suggests they find common interests with Filkins and Ronnie. Ryan challenges Filkins to a rap battle but gets carried away and ends up unintentionally humiliating him. Furious, Filkins, alongside Ronnie, ambushes the trio. Trying out a tactic Drillbit taught them ultimately fails. The boys decide to bring him to school as a substitute teacher, and in that capacity he manages to protect them. While there, Drillbit meets teacher Lisa Zachey, and they start a sexual relationship.
One morning as his mother is driving him to school, Ronnie sees Drillbit showering at the beach; his mother reveals that he is homeless, and that she is one of many he asks for money frequently. Filkins finds the boys and punches Drillbit. Later, at Wade's, they catch Drillbit's homeless friends stealing everything in sight. Drillbit confesses that his real name is Bob; he went AWOL from the U.S. Army and his name was Drillbit because he hurt his pinky finger in high school with a drillbit.
The boys fire Drillbit, who later recovers all of Wade's possessions and places them back before Wade's parents return home. However, the boys accidentally let the truth slip about Drillbit. Their parents take things up with the principal, who contacts the police. Filkins plays innocent and charms all the adults, then continues to ridicule the boys after Drillbit's disappearance. Tensions finally burst when Filkins interrupts Wade's attempt to ask out his crush, Brooke Nguyen. Having enough of his bullying, Wade challenges Filkins to a fight. Ryan offers to join in, but Emmit refuses to help them.
Wade and Ryan arrive at Filkins' house, where he is hosting a party; initially, the duo put up a good fight, but Filkins and Ronnie soon overpower them. Emmit, who has a change of heart, comes to their aid and for a while causes a lot of pain to Filkins, almost defeating him; but Ronnie knocks him out while he is trying to break Filkins' leg.
Drillbit shows up and Filkins punches him.

documents.title: Funny Games
documents.tagline: You must admit, you brought this on yourself.
documents.overview: When Ann, husband George, and son Georgie arrive at their holiday home they are visited by a pair of polite and seemingly pleasant young men. Armed with deceptively sweet smiles and some golf clubs, they proceed to terrorize and torture the tight-knit clan, giving them until the next day to survive.
documents.plot:
Funny Games, also known as Funny Games U.S., is a satirical psychological thriller of 2007 written and directed by Michael Haneke, a shot-for-shot English-language remake of his own 1997 Austrian film, relocated to the United States. Naomi Watts and Tim Roth play Ann and George Farber, with Devon Gearhart as their son Georgie, Michael Pitt and Brady Corbet as the intruders Paul and Peter, and Boyd Gaines as their neighbor Fred. Despite the setting, it was a six-country international co-production.

The Farbers arrive at their lake house with their dog Lucky. Their neighbor Fred, acting oddly, stops by with two young men, Paul and Peter, to help launch the boat. Peter then borrows eggs, drops them, and returns for more, which also end up broken. With Paul pestering Ann to try a golf club and Peter demanding yet more eggs, George orders them out and slaps Paul, and Peter breaks George's leg with the club. The pair take the family hostage, and Paul leads Ann in a game of hot and cold that ends at the body of Lucky, whom he has killed.

The captors force the family into a series of sadistic games, putting a pillowcase over Georgie's head and hurting him until Ann undresses. Georgie escapes to Fred's house, finds corpses there and a shotgun, but when he tries to fire it at Paul it proves unloaded. Back in the living room the men start a counting game in which the loser will be shot; Georgie panics and runs, and Peter kills him. The intruders leave for a while, and the grieving parents resolve to survive: Ann frees herself and flees while George struggles with a dead phone, but she is recaptured. Peter stabs George, and Ann is told to choose between a slow death for him by knife or a quick one by shotgun. She grabs the shotgun and kills Peter, but Paul finds the television remote and rewinds events, breaking the fourth wall, and this time snatches the gun away first. The men kill George, take Ann bound and gagged out on the boat and casually push her into the lake to drown, then knock on the next neighbors' door asking for eggs.

Haneke had wanted to set the original in America but could not for practical reasons. The remake premiered in Britain at the London Film Festival in October 2007 and opened in limited release in North America in March 2008 through Warner Independent. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it skillful but a sadistic exercise in scolding the audience.

documents.title: John Q
documents.tagline: Give a father no options and you leave him no choice.
documents.overview: John Quincy Archibald is a father and husband whose son is diagnosed with an enlarged heart and then finds out he cannot receive a transplant because HMO insurance will not cover it. Therefore, he decides to take a hospital full of patients hostage until the hospital puts his son's name on the donor's list.

documents.title: Hitch
documents.tagline: The cure for the common man.
documents.overview: Dating coach Alex 'Hitch' Hitchens mentors a bumbling client, Albert, who hopes to win the heart of the glamorous Allegra Cole. While Albert makes progress, Hitch faces his own romantic setbacks when proven techniques fail to work on Sara Melas, a tabloid reporter digging for dirt on Allegra Cole's love life. When Sara discovers Hitch's connection to Albert – now Allegra's boyfriend – it threatens to destroy both relationships.
documents.plot:
Hitch is a romantic comedy film released in 2005, directed by Andy Tennant and produced by Columbia Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Alex Hitchens (played by Will Smith), a professional "date doctor" who helps men improve their dating lives. With his unique approach, he teaches them how to attract women and build relationships. However, despite his success with clients, Alex has never been able to find true love himself.

One day, Alex meets Sara Melas (played by Eva Mendes), a journalist assigned to write an article about him and his unconventional methods. Initially, their encounter is adversarial, as Sara is determined to expose the truth behind Alex's claims. However, as they spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other.

As their relationship deepens, Alex must confront his own emotional baggage and learn to open up to Sara. He also has to deal with the challenges of being a "date doctor" in the public eye, as Sara's article threatens to expose his secrets.

Throughout the movie, Alex's character undergoes significant development. We see glimpses of his troubled past, including his difficult childhood and his struggles with commitment. As he falls for Sara, he begins to realize that true love requires vulnerability and trust.

The plot thickens when Sara's article is published, revealing Alex's true identity as a "date doctor." However, instead of being met with ridicule, the public responds positively to Alex's unique approach to relationships. This newfound acceptance allows him to be more open about his feelings for Sara.

In the end, Alex and Sara confess their love for each other and share a romantic kiss. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that true love can conquer all, even for someone like Alex who has struggled with commitment in the past.

Overall, Hitch is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Will Smith's performance as Alex Hitchens brings humor and heart to the film, making it an enjoyable watch for audiences.

documents.title: Ali
documents.tagline: Float like a butterfly and sting like a bee.
documents.overview: In 1964, a brash, new pro boxer, fresh from his Olympic gold medal victory, explodes onto the scene: Cassius Clay. Bold and outspoken, he cuts an entirely new image for African Americans in sport with his proud public self-confidence and his unapologetic belief that he is the greatest boxer of all time. Yet at the top of his game, both Ali's personal and professional lives face the ultimate test.
documents.plot:
Before his championship debut against the heavyweight champion Sonny Liston, Cassius Clay Jr. taunts Liston then dominates the early rounds of the match. Between rounds, Liston asks his corner to apply a substance to his gloves. Liston then takes the advantage in Round 5, as Clay complains of burning eyes and blurred vision to trainer Angelo Dundee. Clay recovers in Round 6 and begins to dominate the fight. Liston quits before round seven, losing the heavyweight championship to Clay, who admonishes the crowd to "Eat your words!"
Clay spends time with Malcolm X and is invited to the home of Nation of Islam leader Elijah Muhammad, where he is given the name Muhammad Ali, much to the disapproval of his father, Cassius Sr. Ali meets Sonji Roi, an ex-Playboy Bunny. He eventually loses his virginity to her. Although she is not Muslim and does not abide sex segregation. Ali goes to Africa and meets up with Malcolm X, but later refuses to speak to him, honoring the wishes of Elijah. He is distraught over the assassination of Malcolm X.
Upon returning to America, Ali fights Liston a second time and knocks him out in the first round. He and Sonji divorce after she objects to various obligations Muslim women have.
Ali then refuses conscription for the Vietnam War and is stripped of his boxing license, passport, and title, and sentenced to five years in prison. After marrying 17-year-old Belinda Boyd and a three-year hiatus from boxing, his conviction is overturned in Clay v. United States, and in his comeback fight, he goes against Jerry Quarry and wins by technical knockout in three rounds. Ali attempts to regain the heavyweight championship against Joe Frazier. In the "Fight of the Century", Frazier generally has the upper hand against Ali and wins by decision, the first loss of Ali's career. Frazier later loses the championship to George Foreman.
Foreman and Ali go to Kinshasa, Zaire, for the Rumble in the Jungle fight. There, Ali meets Veronica Porché and has an affair with her. After reading rumors of his infidelity in newspapers, his wife Belinda travels to Zaire to confront him. Ali says he is unsure whether he loves Veronica, but is focused solely on his upcoming title shot.
For a good portion of the fight against Foreman, Ali leans back against the ropes (Rope-a-dope) allowing Foreman to tire himself out. He then knocks out the exhausted Foreman, regaining the Heavyweight Championship.

documents.title: Creep
documents.tagline: Your journey terminates here
documents.overview: Trapped in a London subway station, a woman who's being pursued by a potential attacker heads into the unknown labyrinth of tunnels beneath the city's streets
documents.plot:
Creep is a 2004 horror slasher film written and directed by the British filmmaker Christopher Smith. It stars Franka Potente as Kate, a woman locked inside the London Underground overnight who is stalked by a deformed killer living in the sewers below, with Sean Harris as the killer, Craig, and Vas Blackwood and Jeremy Sheffield.

Two London sewer workers, Arthur and the newcomer George, discover a tunnel in a wall. Arthur explores it alone and is found injured and in shock, while a wounded woman lurches out crying for help before being dragged back into the darkness. Kate, a young German woman, heads to Charing Cross station to meet a friend at a party but falls asleep on the platform and wakes to find the station locked for the night. She boards an empty train that stops abruptly in the dark, where Guy, a colleague who has followed her, tries to rape her before an unseen attacker drags him out. Guy reappears covered in blood, warning her to run. Kate meets Jimmy and Mandy, a homeless couple who live in a storeroom with their dog, Ray, and pays Jimmy to take her to the night guard. They find Guy mutilated but alive. Mandy, left alone, is abducted, and Jimmy sinks into a heroin stupor. Kate reaches the guard over the intercom, but he is killed before he can summon help, and Guy dies of his injuries.

Walking through the tunnels toward the next station, Jimmy confronts the killer to avenge Mandy and is slaughtered. Kate falls into the sewers, finds Arthur's body and is captured by the creep, Craig, a deformed, mentally ill hermit who keeps victims in flooded, rat-infested cages until they die and then eats them. She escapes with the caged George into a disused medical facility, where Craig, wearing a surgical gown, mimics a surgeon and kills Mandy with a bone saw. In the derelict railcar where he lives, they find Ray and old photographs of a doctor with a deformed child before Craig kills George. Kate drives a hook and chain into Craig's throat and lets a passing train tear it open, killing him. At dawn she collapses on the platform, Ray in her lap, and when a commuter mistakes her for a beggar and leaves a coin, she breaks into hysterical laughter and tears.

The film was first shown at the Fantasy Filmfest in Frankfurt on 10 August 2004. It has been compared to the 1972 London Underground horror film Death Line, though Smith cited a scene from An American Werewolf in London as his inspiration. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Lion King
documents.tagline: Life's greatest adventure is finding your place in the Circle of Life.
documents.overview: A young lion prince is cast out of his pride by his cruel uncle, who claims he killed his father. While the uncle rules with an iron paw, the prince grows up beyond the Savannah, living by a philosophy: No worries for the rest of your days. But when his past comes to haunt him, the young prince must decide his fate: Will he remain an outcast or face his demons and become what he needs to be?
documents.plot:
The Lion King is a timeless classic that has captivated audiences for generations. Released in 1994, this animated masterpiece tells the story of Simba, a young lion cub who must assume his rightful place as king of the Pride Lands.

The film begins with the birth of Simba, son of King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi. Mufasa teaches Simba about the responsibilities of being a king and the circle of life, which connects all living things in the animal kingdom. However, Mufasa's brother Scar, who was next in line for the throne, grows jealous of his brother's position and plots to overthrow him.

Tragedy strikes when Scar's plan succeeds, and Mufasa is killed in a tragic accident. Simba, believing himself responsible for his father's death, runs away from the Pride Lands and abandons his royal heritage. With the help of new friends Timon and Pumbaa, a meerkat and warthog duo who teach him their carefree "Hakuna Matata" lifestyle, Simba grows up in exile.

Years pass, and Simba's childhood friend Nala, now a strong and determined lioness, finds Simba and informs him of the suffering of the Pride Lands under Scar's tyrannical rule. She convinces Simba to return home and reclaim his rightful place as king. With newfound courage and determination, Simba faces his destiny and confronts Scar in an epic battle.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Scar's actions were motivated by a deep-seated jealousy and resentment towards Mufasa. Through Simba's journey, we see the importance of facing one's fears, embracing responsibility, and honoring one's heritage.

The Lion King features stunning animation, memorable characters, and an unforgettable soundtrack, with iconic songs like "Circle of Life," "Hakuna Matata," and "Can You Feel the Love Tonight." The film's themes of identity, community, and redemption continue to resonate with audiences today.

Overall, The Lion King is a masterpiece of storytelling that has become an integral part of popular culture. Its timeless tale of self-discovery and leadership continues to inspire new generations of viewers.

documents.title: Prom Night
documents.tagline: A Night To Die For.
documents.overview: Donna's senior prom is supposed to be the best night of her life, though a sadistic killer from her past has different plans for her and her friends.
documents.plot:
Prom Night is an American slasher film of 2008 directed by Nelson McCormick and written by J. S. Cardone, the fifth and final entry in the Prom Night series and a loose remake of the original 1980 film. Brittany Snow stars as Donna Keppel, a high school senior stalked by the man who murdered her family, with Scott Porter as her boyfriend Bobby, Jessica Stroup and Dana Davis as her friends Claire and Lisa, Johnathon Schaech as the killer Richard Fenton, and Idris Elba and James Ransone as the detectives Winn and Nash.

In Bridgeport, Oregon, Donna, then a freshman, comes home one night to find her father and younger brother murdered and watches her mother being killed before the attacker turns on her. He is Richard Fenton, her former biology teacher, whose obsession with her had cost him his job and earned him a restraining order. Arrested, he vows that he will always love her and that nothing can keep them apart.

Three years later, Donna lives with her uncle Jack and aunt Karen and is in therapy for her trauma. She and her friends are getting ready for their senior prom at a luxury hotel when Detective Winn learns that Fenton has escaped from a psychiatric hospital. Certain he will go after Donna, Winn heads for the hotel with his partner Nash. Fenton kills a maid to obtain a master key card, slips into the friends' shared suite and murders Claire and Michael there. Lisa recognizes him and tries to warn Donna, but Fenton chases her onto a mezzanine under construction and slits her throat.

In the hotel garage Winn finds a car holding the corpse of the man whose identity Fenton stole, then the dead maid, and orders an evacuation. Returning to her room to look for Lisa and retrieve her mother's shawl, Donna encounters Fenton but escapes. A SWAT team searches the building in vain, and Winn realizes that the killer slipped out disguised as a bellhop. Donna and Bobby are escorted to her house under police protection. After a nightmare about Fenton, Donna wakes, closes the bathroom window and finds Bobby dead in her bedroom with his throat cut. Hiding in her closet, she finds Fenton already inside. Winn arrives to find Nash dead, and as Fenton is about to stab Donna, the detective shoots him dead.

Made for about $20 million and shot mostly in Los Angeles, the film was released by Screen Gems on 11 April 2008 and opened at number one in North America, eventually grossing about $57 million worldwide. Critics savaged it as dim and predictable.

documents.title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
documents.original_title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
documents.tagline: The courage to do the impossible lies in the hearts of men.
documents.overview: After an abrupt and violent encounter with a French warship inflicts severe damage upon his ship, a captain of the British Royal Navy begins a chase over two oceans to capture or destroy the enemy, though he must weigh his commitment to duty and ferocious pursuit of glory against the safety of his devoted crew, including the ship's thoughtful surgeon, his best friend.
documents.plot:
Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World is a 2003 historical naval adventure film directed by Peter Weir, starring Russell Crowe as Captain Jack Aubrey and Paul Bettany as Dr. Stephen Maturin.

The story begins during the Napoleonic Wars, in 1812, when Captain Jack Aubrey, a British Royal Navy officer, is tasked with commanding the HMS Surprise, a 38-gun fifth-rate frigate. Aubrey's mission is to intercept and capture French merchant ships carrying supplies to Napoleon's army in Europe.

Aubrey's trusted friend and ship's surgeon, Dr. Stephen Maturin, joins him on this voyage. Maturin is a complex character with a mysterious past, who has been struggling with his own demons. Throughout the film, their friendship and professional partnership are put to the test as they face numerous challenges at sea.

As the HMS Surprise sets sail from Plymouth, England, Aubrey and Maturin encounter various obstacles, including treacherous weather conditions, hostile French privateers, and a mutinous crew. The ship's captain, Tom Pullings, is struggling with his own personal demons, which puts the entire crew in danger.

The plot thickens when the HMS Surprise intercepts a French merchant ship carrying supplies to Napoleon's army. Aubrey and Maturin engage in a fierce battle with the French privateers, resulting in the capture of several ships and the death of many French sailors.

As the HMS Surprise continues its mission, Aubrey and Maturin develop a deeper understanding of each other's strengths and weaknesses. They also face personal challenges, including Aubrey's struggles with his own identity as a naval officer and Maturin's ongoing battle with his demons.

The film's climax takes place in the Strait of Magellan, where the HMS Surprise is pursued by a French ship. In a thrilling sea battle, Aubrey and Maturin work together to outmaneuver their pursuers and emerge victorious.

In the end, the HMS Surprise returns to England as a hero, having successfully completed its mission. Aubrey and Maturin's friendship has been tested and proven stronger than ever, and they look forward to future adventures together.

Throughout the film, Weir explores themes of loyalty, duty, and personal identity, set against the backdrop of one of history's most tumultuous periods. The film's attention to historical detail and its engaging characters make it a compelling watch for fans of naval adventure films.

Overall, Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World is a gripping and entertaining film that showcases Weir's mastery of storytelling and his ability to bring complex characters to life on screen.

documents.title: The Happening
documents.tagline: We've Sensed It. We've Seen The Signs. Now... It's Happening.
documents.overview: When a deadly airborne virus threatens to wipe out the northeastern United States, teacher Elliott Moore and his wife Alma flee from contaminated cities into the countryside in a fight to discover the truth. Is it terrorism, the accidental release of some toxic military bio weapon -- or something even more sinister?
documents.plot:
The Happening is a 2008 science fiction thriller produced, written and directed by M. Night Shyamalan. Mark Wahlberg stars as a high school science teacher fleeing an inexplicable natural disaster that drives people to kill themselves, with Zooey Deschanel, John Leguizamo, Ashlyn Sanchez and Betty Buckley. 20th Century Fox released it on June 13, 2008. It was Shyamalan's first film with an R rating.

In Central Park, people suddenly freeze, become disoriented and begin to take their own lives, and the phenomenon soon spreads across the north-east of the United States. It is first thought to be a terrorist attack using an airborne toxin. In Philadelphia, the teacher Elliot Moore and his wife Alma, whose marriage is strained, are persuaded by Elliot's colleague Julian, a maths teacher, to take a train out of the city with his young daughter Jess. When the train stops in a small town after losing contact, Julian leaves Jess with the Moores to look for his wife in Princeton, where he is caught in the event and dies.

Elliot, Alma and Jess get a ride with the owners of a plant nursery, who suggest that plants have developed a defence against humanity, releasing a toxin that triggers people to kill themselves. As the survivors flee across the countryside, avoiding towns, larger groups are struck down, and Elliot concludes that the plants are targeting crowds. He splits the survivors into small groups, but two teenagers walking with them are shot dead by armed residents of a barricaded house.

The trio find refuge at the isolated home of Mrs. Jones, a suspicious and eccentric elderly woman, who agrees to let them stay the night but turns against them in the morning. When she goes outside she falls victim to the toxin, showing that it is now targeting even individuals. Trapped in separate buildings, Elliot and Alma, reconciled and unwilling to die apart, step outside to embrace, only to find that the event has ended as suddenly as it began.

Three months later, the couple are raising Jess, and Alma learns she is pregnant. An expert on television compares the event to a red tide and warns it may be a warning of worse to come, as the phenomenon begins again in a park in Paris. Critics were scathing, giving it a 17% Rotten Tomatoes approval, but the film grossed 163 million dollars worldwide and has since been reappraised by some as unintentional camp.

documents.title: K-19: The Widowmaker
documents.tagline: Fate has found its hero.
documents.overview: When Russia's first nuclear submarine malfunctions on its maiden voyage, the crew must race to save the ship and prevent a nuclear disaster.
documents.plot: When Russia's first nuclear submarine malfunctions on its maiden voyage, the crew must race to save the ship and prevent a nuclear disaster.

documents.title: Charlie Bartlett
documents.tagline: Popularity is a state of mind.
documents.overview: Awkward teenager Charlie Bartlett has trouble fitting in at a new high school. Charlie needs some friends fast, and decides that the best way to find them is to appoint himself the resident psychiatrist. He becomes one of the most popular guys in school by doling out advice and, occasionally, medication, to the student body.
documents.plot:
Wealthy teenager Charlie Bartlett — after being expelled from several private academies for various infractions — enrolls in a public school run by embittered alcoholic Principal Nathan Gardner. Unable to fit in with most of his fellow students, Charlie is diagnosed with ADHD. He forms an alliance with school bully Murphy Bivens and offers him half the proceeds from the sale of a variety of prescription drugs Charlie obtains by feigning physical and emotional symptoms during sessions with different psychiatrists.
Before long, Charlie's natural charm and likability positions him as the school's resident therapist, offering advice and drugs within the confines of the boys' bathroom. Charlie's social life noticeably improves as he gains the confidence and admiration of the student body and begins to date the principal's rebellious daughter, Susan. Charlie is suspended for three days after distributing a collection of videos showing Bivens beating up various students. His mother takes him to visit his father, who is serving time in prison for tax evasion but Charlie is reluctant to go inside.
Complications arise when seriously depressed Kip Crombwell attempts suicide by swallowing a handful of anti-depressants provided by Charlie. Charlie befriends Kip after having an in-depth conversation with Principal Gardner. Charlie discovers Kip is writing a play about adolescent issues and pitches the idea to Gardner who is, at first, unsure but agrees when Kip says that it would make him less inclined to attempt suicide again. Charlie decides to stop selling drugs to students but continues to provide free therapy.
Charlie arrives at Susan's house to pick her up for a date and he gives her a pharmacy bag. Mr. Gardner comes out and, thinking the bag contains drugs, attempts to grab Susan to make her go into the house. Charlie warns Mr. Gardner not to touch Susan, but he pushes Charlie instead. Charlie then punches Gardner as a reflex, and even though he tries to apologize, the principal does not forgive him. Susan and Charlie then drive off, and the bag turns out to contain nicotine gum to aid Susan in quitting smoking cigarettes.
That night, a large group of students are protesting against security cameras in the student lounge. The police arrive and arrest Charlie for assault, and the kids riot and trash the building in protest. As a result, Principal Gardner is fired. Charlie is released on bail. Before the play, which features Susan, Charlie goes to Mr. Gardner's house to invite him. Charlie finds Mr. Gardner drunk and waving a gun. They get into a heated argument, Charlie attempts to tackle Mr. Gardner and falls into the pool, hitting his head. Mr. Gardner, comes to his senses and dives into the pool to rescue him. Charlie says he thought Mr. Gardner was about to attempt suicide, and he replies that cannot kill himself as he has too many responsibilities. They talk over their problems about Charlie's father and Susan, and then go to the play.

documents.title: Fool's Gold
documents.tagline: This February True Love Takes a Dive.
documents.overview: Treasure hunter Ben 'Finn' Finnegan has sunk both his trusty boat and his marriage to Tess in his obsessive quest to find the legendary 'Queen's Dowry' treasure. When he finds a vital clue that may finally pinpoint the treasure's whereabouts, he drags Tess and her boss along on the hunt. But Finn is not the only one interested in the gold—his former mentor-turned-enemy will stop at nothing to beat him to it.
documents.plot:
Fool's Gold is a 2008 American action-adventure comedy film directed by Andy Tennant and starring Matthew McConaughey and Kate Hudson.

The movie begins with Ben "Finn" Finnegan (Matthew McConaughey), a treasure hunter, who has lost his way after the loss of his father. He is haunted by the memory of his father's death and struggles to find direction in life. Meanwhile, Tess Finnegan (Kate Hudson), Ben's ex-wife, is trying to move on from their failed marriage.

The story takes a turn when Tess discovers that her estranged husband has found a treasure map that supposedly leads to the legendary Golden Idol, also known as the "Fool's Gold." The idol is said to be hidden in the jungles of South America. Tess convinces Ben to join her on an adventure to find the idol and make up for their past mistakes.

As they embark on their journey, Finn and Tess are joined by a group of eccentric treasure hunters, including Moe (Donald Sutherland), a seasoned adventurer who becomes their guide. The group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, rival treasure hunters, and ancient booby traps.

Throughout the movie, Finn and Tess's relationship is put to the test as they confront their past mistakes and learn to work together again. Along the way, they discover that the Golden Idol is more than just a valuable treasure; it holds sentimental value for both of them.

As they near their destination, the group encounters a rival treasure hunter, Lucas (Ewen Bremner), who will stop at nothing to get his hands on the idol. In a thrilling finale, Finn and Tess must use all their skills and ingenuity to outwit Lucas and his team, while also overcoming their personal demons.

In the end, Finn and Tess successfully retrieve the Golden Idol, but not before realizing that the true treasure was their rekindled love for each other. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of reconciliation between the two leads, as they share a romantic kiss and look forward to a brighter future together.

Overall, Fool's Gold is an entertaining adventure film that combines action, comedy, and romance, with a dash of treasure hunting excitement. While it may not be a groundbreaking film, it provides plenty of thrills and laughs for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Taken
documents.tagline: They took his daughter.  He'll take their lives.
documents.overview: While vacationing with a friend in Paris, an American girl is kidnapped by a gang of human traffickers intent on selling her into forced prostitution. Working against the clock, her ex-spy father must pull out all the stops to save her. But with his best years possibly behind him, the job may be more than he can handle.
documents.plot:
Taken is a 2008 action-thriller film directed by Pierre Morel and starring Liam Neeson as Bryan Mills, a former CIA operative turned private security consultant. The movie follows Bryan's desperate search for his daughter Kim (Maggie Grace), who has been kidnapped while on a trip to Paris with her mother.

The story begins with Bryan's family life: he is married to Lenore (Holmes Osborne) and has two daughters, Kim and Sarah. During a family vacation in Paris, Kim is abducted by a human trafficking ring led by the ruthless and cunning Takao (Shin Koyamada). The kidnappers demand $1 million for her safe return.

Bryan's world is turned upside down as he receives a phone call from his daughter, who has been brainwashed to obey her captors. Desperate to rescue Kim, Bryan sets out on a perilous journey through the dark underworld of human trafficking in Paris and beyond.

As Bryan navigates the treacherous landscape, he encounters a range of unsavory characters, including corrupt police officers, ruthless gangsters, and cunning traffickers. Along the way, he teams up with a French detective named Beau (François Berléand), who helps him track down leads and gather intelligence on the kidnappers.

As Bryan delves deeper into the world of human trafficking, he discovers that Takao's operation is just one small part of a larger, more complex network. He also uncovers a shocking connection between his daughter's kidnapping and a mysterious figure from his own past.

The action unfolds at breakneck speed as Bryan faces off against hordes of thugs, dodges bullets, and battles his way through the streets of Paris. Along the way, he encounters a range of memorable characters, including a tough-as-nails nightclub owner (Léa Seydoux) who becomes an unlikely ally.

As Bryan closes in on Takao's operation, he discovers that his daughter has been subjected to brutal treatment and is struggling to maintain her sanity. In a heart-pumping climax, Bryan confronts Takao and his henchmen in a desperate bid to rescue Kim and bring the traffickers to justice.

In the end, Bryan successfully rescues his daughter, but not before facing off against Takao in a violent and intense showdown. The movie concludes with Bryan reunited with his family, but forever changed by his experience as a father and a protector.

Taken was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $214 million worldwide and cementing Liam Neeson's status as an action hero. The film's success spawned two sequels, Taken 2 (2012) and Taken 3 (2014), as well as a prequel, Taken: Origins (2020).

documents.title: The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen
documents.tagline: The power of seven become a league of one.
documents.overview: To prevent a world war from breaking out, famous characters from Victorian literature band together to do battle against a cunning villain.
documents.plot: To prevent a world war from breaking out, famous characters from Victorian literature band together to do battle against a cunning villain.
