documents.title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
documents.original_title: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy
documents.tagline: They bring you the news so you don't have to get it yourself.
documents.overview: It's the 1970s and San Diego anchorman Ron Burgundy is the top dog in local TV, but that's all about to change when ambitious reporter Veronica Corningstone arrives as a new employee at his station.
documents.plot: It's the 1970s and San Diego anchorman Ron Burgundy is the top dog in local TV, but that's all about to change when ambitious reporter Veronica Corningstone arrives as a new employee at his station.

documents.title: Baby Mama
documents.tagline: Would you put your eggs...in this basket?
documents.overview: A successful, single businesswoman who dreams of having a baby discovers she is infertile and hires a working class woman to be her unlikely surrogate.
documents.plot:
Baby Mama is a 2008 American buddy comedy written and directed by Michael McCullers, who made his directing debut with it. Tina Fey and Amy Poehler lead a cast that includes Greg Kinnear, Dax Shepard, Romany Malco, Maura Tierney, Holland Taylor, Steve Martin and Sigourney Weaver. Relativity Media produced it and Universal Pictures released it.

Kate Holbrook is a successful single executive in Philadelphia who has put her career first. At 37 she decides she wants a child, but doctors tell her she has a T-shaped uterus that makes pregnancy unlikely. Adoption falls through, so she turns to a surrogacy agency run by the steely Chaffee Bicknell. The agency pairs her with Angie Ostrowski, a woman from South Philadelphia. When Angie is reported pregnant, Kate prepares in her usual driven way, reading parenting books, baby-proofing her apartment and researching the best preschools. Her plans fall apart when Angie, thrown out by her common-law husband Carl, moves in with her. The two clash constantly, and Kate also starts dating Rob Ackerman, the owner of a local juice bar.

What Kate does not know is that the implantation failed and Angie is faking the pregnancy to collect the money. Angie feels increasingly guilty but keeps putting off the truth, until an ultrasound shows she really is pregnant, with Carl's child. Carl exposes the lie at Kate's baby shower. Kate argues that the baby might still be hers, but a court rules that it is Angie's, and Angie apologizes. Right after the hearing, Angie goes into labor. Kate rushes her to the hospital, faints during the delivery and wakes to learn that she herself is two months pregnant by Rob. Kate forgives Angie, who names her daughter Stef after Gwen Stefani, and the two become close friends. A year later, at Stef's first birthday, Kate and Rob are engaged and have a daughter, and Carl is an involved father. The film ends with Kate and Angie watching Tom and Jerry cartoons with their girls.

The film opened on April 25, 2008, at number one in the United States and Canada, taking $17.4 million from 2,543 theaters. It went on to gross about $64.2 million against a $30 million budget. Reviews were mixed to moderately positive. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a lightweight, predictable comedy carried by its performers. Variety's Todd McCarthy said its contents were easy to guess, while Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian called it enjoyable and amiable despite its romantic comedy clichés.

documents.title: Doom
documents.tagline: No one gets out alive.
documents.overview: A team of space marines known as the Rapid Response Tactical Squad, led by Sarge, is sent to a science facility on Mars after somebody reports a security breach. There, they learn that the alert came after a test subject, a mass murderer purposefully injected with alien DNA, broke free and began killing people. Dr. Grimm, who is related to team member Reaper, informs them all that the chromosome can mutate humans into monsters -- and is highly infectious.
documents.plot:
Doom is a 2005 science fiction action film directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak, produced by Babelsberg Film, and written by David S. Goyer.

The movie takes place on Mars, where a team of space marines are sent to investigate the disappearance of a research team at the Hell's Gate facility. The story begins with a dramatic opening sequence showing the destruction of the research team by demons from Hell, which is revealed to be an interdimensional portal known as the Hellgate.

The movie then shifts to the present day, where we meet our protagonist, Sarge (Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson), a tough and experienced space marine who has been sent to Mars with his team, including Lieutenant Preston (Carl Anthony Payne II) and Private Hudson (A.J. Buckley). The team is tasked with investigating the disappearance of the research team at Hell's Gate.

Upon arrival, the team discovers that the facility has been overrun by demons from Hell, which are using the Hellgate to invade Earth. The team soon realizes that they must close the Hellgate before it's too late.

As the team navigates through the facility, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including hordes of demons and treacherous terrain. Along the way, Sarge forms a bond with Private Hudson, who becomes his protégé.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that the Hellgate is being controlled by a rogue scientist, Dr. William Mapother (Ben Affleck), who has been using the facility to harness the power of the demons for his own gain.

As the team fights their way through the facility, they eventually reach the heart of the Hellgate, where they face off against Dr. Mapother and his minions. In a thrilling finale, Sarge and Hudson manage to close the Hellgate, saving humanity from the demonic invasion.

Throughout the movie, there are several action-packed sequences, including a memorable fight scene between Sarge and a group of demons in a zero-gravity environment. The special effects are impressive, bringing the demons and the Hellgate to life in a visually stunning way.

Overall, Doom is an entertaining sci-fi action film that delivers on its promise of intense action and suspense. While it may not be as complex or thought-provoking as some other movies in the genre, it's a fun ride that's sure to satisfy fans of science fiction and action films.

documents.title: 99 francs
documents.tagline: I'm the most influential bastard in 2000 years.
documents.overview: Paris, France, 2001. Octave Parango, a young advertiser working at the Ross & Witchcraft advertising agency, lives a suicidal existence, ruled by cynicism, irresponsibility and debauchery. The obstacles he will encounter in developing a campaign for a new yogurt brand will force him to face the meaning of his work and the way he manages his relationship with those who orbit around his egotistic lifestyle.
documents.plot: The film is a satire on the modern advertisement business. The plot mainly concerns the story of a commercial advertisement designer, Octave Parango, who has an easy-going, highly paid job, and an active free life mainly consisting of drugs and random one-time sexual encounters. However, he starts growing weary of his job, and after having his first ever long-time relationship with fellow worker Sophie fail miserably, he organises a revolt against the advertisement business and his own life.

documents.title: Il Divo
documents.overview: Italy, early '90s. Calm, clever and inscrutable, politician Giulio Andreotti has been synonymous with power for decades. He has survived everything: electoral battles, terrorist massacres, loss of friends, slanderous accusations; but now certain repentant mobsters implicate him in the crimes of Cosa Nostra.
documents.plot:
The film presents the story of Giulio Andreotti, a seven-time Prime Minister of Italy notorious for his alleged ties to the Mafia. The narration covers Andreotti's seventh election in 1992, his failed bid for the presidency of the Italian Republic, the Tangentopoli bribe scandal and his trial in 1995.
As the film opens, Giulio Andreotti gives an inner monologue observing how he has managed to survive his tumultuous political career while his various detractors have died. A montage shows the murders of various people connected to Andreotti, including journalist Mino Pecorelli, Carabinieri general Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa, bankers Michele Sindona and Roberto Calvi, and former Prime Minister Aldo Moro.

documents.overview: A man obsessed with conspiracy theories becomes a target after one of his theories turns out to be true. Unfortunately, in order to save himself, he has to figure out which theory it is.

documents.title: Legally Blonde
documents.tagline: Don't judge a book by its hair color!
documents.overview: Elle Woods, a fashionable sorority queen, is dumped by her boyfriend. She decides to follow him to law school, but while there, she figures out that there is more to herself than just looks.
documents.plot:
Legally Blonde is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Robert Luketic and written by Karen McCullah Lutz and Kirsten Smith. The movie stars Reese Witherspoon as Elle Woods, a fashion merchandising major who enrolls in Harvard Law School to win back her ex-boyfriend, Warner Huntington III (Matthew Davis).

The film begins with Elle, a popular sorority girl at California University, Los Angeles, who is dumped by Warner due to his disapproval of her shallow and materialistic lifestyle. Determined to prove herself and win him back, Elle decides to attend Harvard Law School, despite having no prior knowledge of law.

Upon arrival, Elle faces skepticism from her peers, particularly her roommate Paulette (Jennifer Coolidge), who is a hairdresser and a single mother. Despite the initial doubts, Elle proves herself to be a quick learner and earns the respect of her professors, including Professor Callahan (Bruce Thomas) and Professor Kingsfield (Camilla Belle).

As Elle navigates law school, she becomes involved in a high-profile murder case involving Brooke Wyndham (Ali Larter), a wealthy socialite accused of murdering her husband. Elle takes on the case pro bono, determined to prove that Brooke is innocent.

Throughout the film, Elle's character undergoes significant development as she confronts her own biases and stereotypes. She learns to look beyond superficial appearances and develops a deeper understanding of the law and its complexities.

As the trial approaches, Elle faces opposition from her classmates, particularly Vivian Kensington (Selma Blair), who is initially dismissive of Elle's abilities but eventually becomes an ally. The two women form a strong bond, with Vivian becoming a source of support and encouragement for Elle.

The film culminates in a dramatic courtroom showdown between Elle and the prosecution, led by the ruthless District Attorney, Arnold Stern (Victor Garber). In a stunning reversal, Elle presents a compelling argument that proves Brooke's innocence, and the jury delivers a verdict of not guilty.

In the end, Elle realizes that she has grown beyond her initial expectations and has discovered a new sense of purpose. She decides to stay at Harvard Law School and pursue a career in law, leaving Warner behind and embracing her newfound independence.

The film ends with Elle walking out of the courtroom, confident and self-assured, as the camera pans out to reveal the iconic Harvard Law School building. The final shot is of Elle's graduation cap, symbolizing her transformation from a shallow sorority girl to a confident and capable lawyer.

Overall, Legally Blonde is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and empowerment. Reese Witherspoon's performance as Elle Woods is particularly noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The film's blend of humor, wit, and drama makes it a beloved classic among audiences.

documents.original_title: The X Files: I Want to Believe

documents.overview: Six years after the events of The X-Files series finale, former FBI agent Doctor Dana Scully is now a staff physician at Our Lady of Sorrows, a Catholic hospital, and treating a boy named Christian who has Sandhoff disease, a terminal brain condition. FBI agent Drummy arrives to ask Scully’s help in locating Fox Mulder, the fugitive former head of the X-Files division, and says they will call off its manhunt for him if he will help investigate the disappearances of several women, including young FBI agent Monica Banan.  Mulder and Scully are called back to duty by the FBI when a former priest claims to be receiving psychic visions pertaining to a kidnapped agent.

documents.title: The Bank Job
documents.tagline: The true story of a heist gone wrong... in all the right ways.
documents.overview: Terry is a small-time car dealer trying to leave his shady past behind and start a family. Martine is a beautiful model from Terry's old neighbourhood who knows that Terry is no angel. When Martine proposes a foolproof plan to rob a bank, Terry recognises the danger but realises this may be the opportunity of a lifetime. As the resourceful band of thieves burrows its way into a safe-deposit vault at a Lloyds Bank, they quickly realise that, besides millions in riches, the boxes also contain secrets that implicate everyone from London's most notorious underworld gangsters to powerful government figures, and even the Royal Family. Although the heist makes headlines throughout Britain for several days, a government gag order eventually brings all reporting of the case to an immediate halt.
documents.plot:
In 1971, British Security Services (MI5) want a safety deposit box secured in a Lloyds Bank branch. Belonging to Black militant gangster Michael X, it contains compromising photos of Princess Margaret, insurance to keep the British authorities off Michael's back. Martine, an ex-model sleeping with MI5 agent Tim Everett, is caught smuggling drugs into the country; to avoid going to jail, she makes a deal with Tim to retrieve the photos so MI5 can finally arrest Michael.
MI5 has the idea to stage the retrieval as a robbery so Martine approaches her ex-boyfriend Terry Leather, who has criminal contacts. Terry is now a struggling car salesman but happily married with two kids. She tells him he will be richly rewarded if they pull off the robbery but does not tell him about the photos. Terry's team includes his close friends Eddie, Dave, and Kevin, as well as trusted criminal associates Bambas and Guy. While scouting the bank, Dave runs into gangster Lew Vogel, for whom he'd made pornographic films.
The gang rents a shop near the bank, tunnels below the vault, and breaks in. During the robbery prep, Martine, who is still in love with Terry, kisses him and they sleep together. They loot the safety deposit boxes, but Terry discovers Princess Margaret's photos and learns that Martine lied to them. The police are alerted to the robbery by ham radio operator Eric Addey, who overhears the gang's walkie-talkie communications, but the gang has fled. The robbery rattles important figures who kept incriminating items, including Vogel, who has a ledger of police payoffs and bribes inside, and Incriminating photographs of government officials who secretly frequented Sonia Bern's brothels. Vogel realizes Dave's presence outside the bank was not a coincidence, and has him kidnapped and tortured for information. Dave gives in, and Vogel has Gerald and Nick—two policemen on his payroll—kidnap Eddie. Terry discovers the explicit photographs of government officials in Sonia's brothels among their loot. Knowing Tim will let the gang take the fall once MI5 has Princess Margaret's photos, Terry uses the brothel photos to secure passports and new identities for the gang in exchange for Princess Margaret's photos.
Vogel's men murder Bambas and Guy. Vogel kills Dave and threatens to kill Eddie unless Terry surrenders the ledger. Terry agrees to meet with Vogel at Paddington Station to exchange the ledger for Eddie. He arranges for the meeting to happen at the same time he will be picking up the new passports and written immunity from prosecution from MI5, delivered by Lord Mountbatten. Terry also sends Kevin to honest straight cop Roy Given with a page from the ledger to ask for his help. Vogel tries to flee at the sight of MI5, but Terry attacks him—only for him and Eddie to be arrested. Tim has Terry, Eddie and Kevin released and Given uses the ledger they turned in to arrest Vogel, Gerald and Nick.

documents.title: Alfie
documents.tagline: Meet a man who never met a woman he didn't love.
documents.overview: In Manhattan, the British limousine driver Alfie is surrounded by beautiful women, having one night stands with all of them and without any sort of commitment. His best friends are his colleague Marlon and his girl-friend Lonette. Alfie has a brief affair with Lonette, and the consequences force Alfie to reflect on his lifestyle.
documents.plot:
Alfie is a 2004 romantic comedy-drama co-written, produced and directed by Charles Shyer, a reworking of the 1966 British film of the same name and its 1975 sequel. Jude Law plays the title role created by Michael Caine, with Marisa Tomei as Julie, Omar Epps as Marlon, Nia Long as Lonette, Jane Krakowski as Dorie, Sienna Miller as Nikki and Susan Sarandon as Liz.

Alfie Elkins is a Cockney limousine driver in Manhattan who drifts from one casual affair to the next, often addressing the audience directly. He keeps up an easygoing arrangement with Julie, a single mother, and a fling with Dorie, an unhappily married woman, dropping her when she wants more. Hoping to start a business with his friend and co-worker Marlon, he tries to help Marlon win back his ex-girlfriend Lonette, but ends up sleeping with her after a night of drinking. Marlon and Lonette reconcile and plan to marry.

Julie throws Alfie out after finding another woman's underwear in her bin, and by the time he decides to make amends she has gone back to her estranged husband. Lonette discovers she is pregnant by Alfie and, without telling Marlon, the two go to a clinic for an abortion; soon afterwards the couple move upstate without saying goodbye. Troubled by impotence, Alfie learns from a doctor that it is caused by stress, but a lump leads to an anxious wait for test results. In a hospital bathroom he meets Joe, a widower who advises him to find someone to love and live each day as if it were his last.

Cleared of cancer, Alfie resolves to aim higher. He falls into a passionate but stormy romance with Nikki, a beautiful, unstable young woman, then turns his attention to Liz, an older cosmetics mogul who wants only an affair, and breaks up with Nikki. He realises too late that he cares for Julie, who has moved on. Visiting Marlon and Lonette, he learns that she never had the abortion and that Marlon has stayed with her knowing the child is Alfie's. Liz, meanwhile, has taken a younger lover. Meeting Dorie again, Alfie apologises and admits he runs from intimacy, and he ends the film asking the audience what it is all about.

The film grossed $35 million worldwide against a $60 million budget and drew mixed reviews, holding 48% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but Mick Jagger and Dave Stewart won a Golden Globe for the song "Old Habits Die Hard".

documents.title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas
documents.tagline: He puts the mean in green.
documents.overview: Inside a snowflake exists the magical land of Whoville. In Whoville, live the Whos, an almost mutated sort of Munchkin-like people. All the Whos love Christmas, yet just outside of their beloved Whoville lives the Grinch. The Grinch is a nasty creature that hates Christmas, and plots to steal it away from the Whos, whom he equally abhors. Yet a small child, Cindy Lou Who, decides to try befriending the Grinch.
documents.plot:
How the Grinch Stole Christmas, also titled Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas, is a 2000 American Christmas comedy film directed by Ron Howard and written by Jeffrey Price and Peter S. Seaman, loosely based on Dr. Seuss's 1957 children's book. The second adaptation of the book after the 1966 animated television special, and the first Dr. Seuss book adapted as a live-action feature, it stars Jim Carrey as the Grinch, a misanthropic green creature who sets out to ruin the Christmas celebrations of Whoville, with Jeffrey Tambor, Christine Baranski and Taylor Momsen, and narration by Anthony Hopkins.

The Grinch lives in a cave on Mount Crumpit and despises Christmas and the cheerful Whos below. After meeting him at the post office, young Cindy Lou Who learns his story: raised by two elderly Who women, he had a crush on his classmate Martha May Whovier, but when the bully Augustus MayWho mocked his hairy face, he tried to shave, cut himself, and fled to the mountain after the class laughed at him. Hoping to set things right, Cindy nominates the Grinch as the town's Holiday Cheermeister, over the objections of MayWho, now mayor. The Grinch accepts after learning that Martha will attend, and he begins to enjoy the festivities, until MayWho humiliates him with a gift of an electric razor and proposes to Martha with a new car. The Grinch denounces the Whos' materialism, wrecks the celebration and returns to his cave.

Learning that the Whos will celebrate anyway, the Grinch disguises himself as Santa Claus, dresses his dog, Max, as a reindeer, and descends on Whoville to steal every present, decoration and scrap of food. On Christmas morning, MayWho blames Cindy, but her father, the postmaster Lou Lou Who, reminds the town that Christmas means more than presents, and the Whos gather to sing. Hearing them from the mountaintop, the Grinch realizes the true meaning of Christmas, and his heart grows three sizes. He saves Cindy and the sleigh from falling into a gorge, returns everything and apologizes. Martha gives back MayWho's ring and declares her love for the Grinch, who hosts the Christmas feast in his cave.

Released by Universal Pictures on November 17, 2000, the film grossed $350.6 million worldwide, the sixth-highest gross of the year. Reviews were mixed, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46; critics praised Carrey but preferred the animated special.

documents.title: Che: Part Two
documents.tagline: A revolutionary life.
documents.overview: After the Cuban Revolution, Che is at the height of his fame and power. Then he disappears, re-emerging incognito in Bolivia, where he organizes a small group of Cuban comrades and Bolivian recruits to start the great Latin American Revolution. Through this story, we come to understand how Che remains a symbol of idealism and heroism that lives in the hearts of people around the world.
documents.plot:
Che: Part Two (also released as Che: Part Two – Guerrilla) is a 2008 biographical war drama directed by Steven Soderbergh, the second half of his two-part portrait of Ernesto "Che" Guevara. Shot back to back with Che: Part One, it moves from the Cuban Revolution covered in the first film to Guevara's doomed guerrilla campaign in Bolivia in 1966–67, and is adapted from his Bolivian Diary. The screenplay is credited to Peter Buchman and Benjamin A. van der Veen, and Benicio del Toro again plays Guevara.

The film opens with Fidel Castro publicly reading, in October 1965, the farewell letter in which Che renounces his Cuban posts and citizenship after vanishing from public life. A year later Guevara, disguised as an older Uruguayan official named Ramón, travels with forged papers to La Paz and on into the mountains to join a small band of Cuban veterans and Bolivian recruits. Training and arms deliveries mark the early days, but the Bolivian Communist Party under Mario Monje refuses to back armed struggle, local peasants remain wary or hostile, food runs short and quarrels flare between Cubans and Bolivians. Deserters lead the army to the rebels' base camp, exposing the foreign identity of the group, while President René Barrientos accepts American help and U.S. advisers begin training Bolivian Rangers to hunt them down.

The journalist Régis Debray and the Argentine Ciro Bustos are arrested after leaving the camp, a rear guard that includes the agent Tania is wiped out in an ambush at a river crossing, and Guevara, increasingly crippled by asthma, leads a dwindling column through the forest. Wounded and captured in a firefight near La Higuera, he is held in the village school and executed on 9 October 1967.

Alongside del Toro, the cast includes Catalina Sandino Moreno, Franka Potente, Demián Bichir, Rodrigo Santoro and Joaquim de Almeida, with Matt Damon in a brief role as a priest. The film was shot mainly in Spain, with some scenes in La Paz, using the then-new RED digital camera and natural light. Produced by companies including Wild Bunch, Section Eight, Laura Bickford Productions, Morena Films and Telecinco Cinema, it premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival as part of a four-hour screening of the complete work, where del Toro won the award for Best Actor. Reviews were mixed to positive, and the film was not a commercial success.

documents.plot: Ernesto Guevara, known as 'Che', leads a group of Cuban exiles under Fidel Castro in a revolution to overthrow Fulgencio Batista, the dictator of Cuba.

They hardly ever have a choice and are forced to obey the rules of the Camorra. Only a lucky few can even think of leading a normal life.

documents.title: Amelia
documents.overview: A look at the life of legendary American pilot Amelia Earhart, who disappeared while flying over the Pacific Ocean in 1937 in an attempt to make a flight around the world.
documents.plot:
On June 1, 1937, aviator Amelia Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan, start their attempt to circumnavigate the globe. Moving in vignettes from her early years when Earhart was captivated by an aircraft flying overhead on the Kansas prairie where she grew up, her life over the preceding decade gradually unfolds via flashbacks. In 1928, Earhart is recruited by charismatic publishing tycoon and adoring business partner George Putnam to become the first woman to cross the Atlantic Ocean, albeit as a passenger. Taking command of the flight results in success and she is thrust into the limelight as the most famous woman pilot of her time. Putnam helps Earhart write a book chronicling the flight, much like his earlier triumph with Charles Lindbergh's We. Earhart and Putnam eventually marry, although she enacts a "cruel" pledge as her wedding contract.
Embarrassed that her fame was not earned, Earhart commences to set myriad aviation records, and in 1932, recreates her earlier transatlantic flight, becoming the first female pilot to fly solo across the Atlantic. Throughout the next five years, Earhart falls into an awkward passionate affair with Gene Vidal. In a display of romantic jealousy, Putnam quietly tells Amelia that he does not want Vidal in his house. Earhart is annoyed by the seemingly endless agenda of celebrity appearances and endorsements; Putnam reminds her it funds her flying.
Earhart returns to her husband as she prepares for her most momentous flight to date, to fly around the world, in a Lockheed Model 10 Electra, sponsored by Purdue University, with the help of navigator Fred Noonan. Vidal notes the biggest obstacle will be to locate tiny Howland Island. Earhart's first attempt ends in a runway crash in Hawaii, due to a collapsed landing gear, and her aircraft requires extensive repairs before the flight can be attempted again. Eventually, she takes the repaired Electra in a reverse direction, leaving the lengthy trans-Pacific crossing for the end.
On July 2, 1937, Earhart and Noonan set out to Howland. A rising crisis unfolds between the plane and the Coast Guard picket ship Itasca; the Coast Guard radio operators have a direction finder with a dead battery, and weak radio communications prevent Earhart and Itasca from making contact. Running low on fuel, Earhart and Noonan fly on and vanish. A massive search is unsuccessful, but solidifies Earhart as an aviation icon.

documents.title: Jeepers Creepers
documents.tagline: Jeepers Creepers
documents.overview: A brother and sister driving home through an isolated countryside from college encounter a flesh-eating creature in the midst of its ritualistic eating spree.
documents.plot:
Jeepers Creepers is a 2001 American horror film directed by Victor Salva and produced by United Artists. The movie follows the story of Darry Jenner (Justin Long) and his brother Travis (Gina Philips) as they embark on a road trip across the country to visit their father's grave.

The story begins with the introduction of the Creeper, a monstrous creature that is said to appear every 23 years to feast on human flesh. The Creeper is an ancient being with supernatural powers, and it is said to be able to control the minds of humans, forcing them to do its bidding.

As Darry and Travis drive through the desert, they come across a mysterious truck stop where they meet a local named John Smith (Jonathan Breck), who claims to have information about their father's grave. However, things take a dark turn when the Creeper appears, and John is revealed to be possessed by the creature.

The Creeper begins to terrorize Darry and Travis, forcing them to flee from its wrath. Along the way, they meet a local woman named Dr. Tendler (Patricia Belcher), who helps them understand the legend of the Creeper and how it can be defeated.

As the story unfolds, Darry and Travis discover that their father's grave is actually a trap set by an ancient cult to contain the Creeper. The brothers soon realize that they are in grave danger and must find a way to defeat the creature before it's too late.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Darry and Travis, who use a combination of ingenuity and bravery to outsmart the Creeper. In the end, they manage to trap the creature in a tomb, saving themselves and their father's grave from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds as the Creeper becomes increasingly menacing, forcing Darry and Travis to confront their deepest fears. The film's climax is both intense and satisfying, providing a sense of closure for the characters.

Overall, Jeepers Creepers is a tense and suspenseful horror film that explores themes of family, sacrifice, and the supernatural. With its blend of action, horror, and humor, it has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Green Street Hooligans
documents.tagline: Just think of someone you hate.
documents.overview: After being wrongfully expelled from Harvard University, American Matt Buckner flees to his sister's home in England. Once there, he is befriended by her charming and dangerous brother-in-law, Pete Dunham, and introduced to the underworld of British football hooliganism. Matt learns to stand his ground through a friendship that develops against the backdrop of this secret and often violent world. 'Green Street Hooligans' is a story of loyalty, trust and the sometimes brutal consequences of living close to the edge.

documents.title: What Just Happened
documents.tagline: Admit nothing.
documents.overview: During the course of an ordinary week in Hollywood, movie producer Ben must navigate his way through shark-infested waters as he struggles to complete his latest projects. A demanding studio boss demands extensive changes to a movie starring Sean Penn, while another chief won't greenlight a project unless star Bruce Willis shaves his beard. Meanwhile, Ben tries to reconcile with his wife and maintain a relationship with his young daughter.
documents.plot:
What Just Happened is a 2008 American satirical comedy-drama directed by Barry Levinson and starring Robert De Niro, based on producer Art Linson's 2002 book What Just Happened? Bitter Hollywood Tales from the Front Line, about his own experiences in the film business. An independent production of 2929 Productions, Art Linson Productions and Tribeca Productions, it screened at the Cannes Film Festival on May 25, 2008, before its release on October 17, 2008.

Ben, a veteran Hollywood producer, is beset by professional and personal problems. His new film, Fiercely, tests disastrously, largely because its ending shows the murder of the hero, played by Sean Penn, together with his dog. Studio executive Lou Tarnow suspects Ben shot the dog's death only as a bargaining chip and threatens to take over the edit and pull the film from Cannes unless that scene goes, while the volatile British director Jeremy Brunell refuses to change anything. At the same time, the studio may cancel Ben's next project because its star, Bruce Willis, will not shave the thick beard he has grown, and Ben's attempts to reason with him meet furious resistance. In his private life, Ben cannot cleanly separate from his second wife, Kelly, and discovers that she is having an affair with Scott Solomon, a married screenwriter he has worked with, whose own script soon attracts Brad Pitt.

Jeremy eventually agrees to let the dog live, and although Ben's appeal to Willis's agent only gets the agent fired, Willis finally shaves and production continues. At Cannes, however, Jeremy unveils a secret new cut in which the dog dies after all, with almost a minute of extra gunfire. The ending ruins any hope of a Palme d'Or, though some viewers, including Penn, cheer. Lou flies home on the studio jet, leaving Ben stranded, and when he finally makes it to a Vanity Fair shoot of Hollywood's top thirty producers, he is placed at the far edge of the photo.

The supporting cast includes Catherine Keener, Robin Wright, Stanley Tucci, John Turturro, Michael Wincott, Moon Bloodgood and Kristen Stewart. Filming began in March 2007, with exteriors in Los Angeles and interiors in Connecticut, where the production moved for tax incentives. Critics were divided, with 49% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51.

documents.title: I Love You Phillip Morris
documents.tagline: The Conman who wouldn't go straight.
documents.overview: Steve Russell is a small-town cop. Bored with his bland lifestyle, Russell turns to fraud as a means of shaking things up. Before long, Russell's criminal antics have landed him behind bars, where he encounters the charismatic Phillip Morris. Smitten, Russell devotes his entire life to being with Morris regardless of the consequences.
documents.plot: Steven Russell leads a seemingly average life – an organ player in the local church, happily married to Debbie, and a member of the local police force. That is until he has a severe car accident that leads him to the ultimate epiphany: he’s gay and he’s going to live life to the fullest – even if he has to break the law to do it. Taking on an extravagant lifestyle, Steven turns to cons and fraud to make ends meet and is eventually sent to the State Penitentiary where he meets the love of his life, a sensitive, soft-spoken man named Phillip Morris. His devotion to freeing Phillip from jail and building the perfect life together prompts him to attempt (and often succeed at) one impossible con after another.

documents.title: Steamboy
documents.tagline: He will save the future.
documents.overview: After receiving a package from his grandfather, Ray, a young inventor who lives in England during the mid-19th century, finds himself caught in the middle of a deadly conflict related to a revolutionary advance in steam power.
documents.plot: In 1860s Britain, a boy inventor finds himself caught in the middle of a deadly conflict over a revolutionary advance in steam power.

documents.title: Reservation Road
documents.tagline: To find the truth you have to find who's hiding it.
documents.overview: Two fathers' lives intersect when one of them is involved in a terrible and sudden hit-and-run car accident that leaves the other's son dead. In response, the two men react in unexpected ways as a reckoning looms in the near future.
documents.plot: Two fathers' lives intersect when one of them is involved in a terrible and sudden hit-and-run car accident that leaves the other's son dead. In response, the two men react in unexpected ways as a reckoning looms in the near future.

documents.title: Crimson Tide
documents.tagline: Danger runs deep.
documents.overview: After the Cold War, a breakaway Russian republic with nuclear warheads becomes a possible worldwide threat. U.S. submarine Capt. Frank Ramsey signs on a relatively green but highly recommended Lt. Cmdr. Ron Hunter to the USS Alabama, which may be the only ship able to stop a possible Armageddon. When Ramsay insists that the Alabama must act aggressively, Hunter, fearing they will start rather than stop a disaster, leads a potential mutiny to stop him.
documents.plot:
Crimson Tide is a 1995 American submarine thriller film directed by Tony Scott and written by David Twohy. The movie stars Gene Hackman, Denzel Washington, and Matt Craven.

The story begins with the USS Nebraska (SSBN-739), a United States Navy ballistic missile submarine, on a routine patrol in the North Atlantic Ocean. Captain Frank Ramsey (Gene Hackman) is the commanding officer of the ship, accompanied by his trusted executive officer, Lieutenant Commander Ron Hunter (Denzel Washington).

As the crew goes about their duties, tensions rise between Ramsey and Hunter due to their differing leadership styles. Ramsey is a seasoned veteran with years of experience, while Hunter is a younger, more aggressive officer who believes in taking bold action.

The situation escalates when the Nebraska detects a Soviet submarine, the K-143, which has been detected by the US Navy's early warning systems. The crew is put on high alert as they prepare to engage the enemy vessel.

As the standoff between the two submarines continues, it becomes clear that the K-143 is not just any ordinary Soviet sub - it's a Russian submarine carrying nuclear warheads. The situation reaches a boiling point when Ramsey and Hunter disagree on how to proceed, with Ramsey advocating for caution and Hunter pushing for a more aggressive approach.

The tension between the two leaders comes to a head as they engage in a heated argument, which ultimately leads to a dramatic confrontation. In the heat of the moment, Ramsey orders Hunter to take control of the ship, but Hunter refuses, leading to a power struggle that puts the entire crew at risk.

As the situation spirals out of control, it becomes clear that the K-143 is not just a threat to the US Navy - it's also a ticking time bomb. The Russian submarine has been carrying nuclear warheads for years, and its crew is unaware of the danger they pose to themselves and others.

In the end, Ramsey and Hunter are forced to work together to defuse the situation and prevent a catastrophic accident. In a tense and dramatic climax, they manage to disable the K-143's nuclear systems, averting a disaster that could have had far-reaching consequences.

Throughout the movie, the tension between Ramsey and Hunter is palpable, and their differing leadership styles create a sense of unease among the crew. The film's themes of power, authority, and the dangers of unchecked aggression are timely and thought-provoking, making Crimson Tide a gripping and intense thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, Crimson Tide is a masterclass in tension-building and character-driven drama, with outstanding performances from its leads. The film's themes and plot are both timely and timeless, making it a classic of the submarine thriller genre.

documents.title: Atlantis: Milo's Return
documents.tagline: The all-new adventures
documents.overview: Milo and Kida reunite with their friends to investigate strange occurances around the world that seem to have links to the secrets of Atlantis.
documents.plot:
Atlantis: Milo's Return is a direct-to-video animated film that serves as a sequel to the 1997 television series "Mighty Ducks." The movie follows the adventures of young hockey player and team captain, Ryan Duckworth, who has grown up since the events of the original series.

The story begins with Ryan (now a teenager) struggling to balance his love for hockey with his desire to attend college. He is forced to return to the Mighty Ducks' old rink, where he reunites with his former teammates, including Puck, Hannah, and Charlie. However, their reunion is short-lived as they soon discover that the evil villain, Vincent "Vinnie" Morneau, has returned to exact revenge on Ryan's family.

It turns out that Vinnie had been seeking revenge against Ryan's father, who had foiled his plans in the original series. Vinnie kidnaps Ryan and takes him to the underwater kingdom of Atlantis, where he intends to use Ryan as leverage to get back at Ryan's family.

In Atlantis, Ryan meets Milo, a young boy who is the son of King Poseidon and Princess Athena. Milo has been searching for his parents, who were thought to have been killed by Vinnie in a previous adventure. With the help of his friends, including Puck, Hannah, and Charlie, Ryan must navigate the dangers of Atlantis and work with Milo to stop Vinnie's evil plans.

As they journey through the underwater kingdom, Ryan and Milo encounter various obstacles, including treacherous sea creatures and treacherous paths. Along the way, Ryan learns more about his own destiny and the importance of teamwork and friendship.

In the end, Ryan and Milo successfully defeat Vinnie and shatter the curse that had been cast upon Ryan's family. With the curse lifted, Ryan is able to pursue his dreams of playing hockey in college, while also finding a new sense of purpose as a hero in the underwater kingdom of Atlantis.

Throughout the movie, there are many nods to the original series, including cameos from familiar characters and references to classic Mighty Ducks moments. The film's animation style is reminiscent of the original series, with vibrant colors and engaging character designs.

Overall, "Atlantis: Milo's Return" is a fun and action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-discovery. While it may not be as iconic as some of Disney's other animated films, it remains a beloved entry in the Mighty Ducks franchise.

documents.title: Twilight
documents.tagline: When you can live forever, what do you live for?
documents.overview: When Bella Swan moves to a small town in the Pacific Northwest, she falls in love with Edward Cullen, a mysterious classmate who reveals himself to be a 108-year-old vampire. Despite Edward's repeated cautions, Bella can't stay away from him, a fatal move that endangers her own life.
documents.plot:
Twilight is a 2008 American romantic fantasy film based on Stephenie Meyer's novel of the same name. The movie follows the story of Bella Swan (played by Kristen Stewart), a teenage girl who moves to Forks, Washington to live with her father.

Bella starts at a new high school, where she is drawn to a mysterious and handsome boy named Edward Cullen (played by Robert Pattinson). Despite his initial reluctance, Edward begins to spend time with Bella, and they develop a strong connection. However, Edward has a secret: he is a vampire.

As Bella and Edward's relationship deepens, they face threats from outside forces, including James, a rogue vampire who seeks to destroy Bella. Edward and his family of vampires, who are revealed to be "vegetarian" and drink animal blood instead of human blood, work together to protect Bella from James and other dangers.

Throughout the movie, Bella must navigate her feelings for Edward while also dealing with the challenges of high school and her relationships with her friends and family. The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Edward and James, which ultimately leads to James' defeat and Bella's safety.

One of the most striking aspects of Twilight is its portrayal of forbidden love. The movie explores the intense passion and all-consuming nature of Bella and Edward's relationship, as well as the risks and consequences that come with loving someone who is different from oneself. The film's depiction of vampire lore is also noteworthy, offering a unique take on the traditional mythology.

Overall, Twilight is a captivating and romantic tale that has become a cultural phenomenon among young audiences. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie's success can be attributed to its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and the chemistry between Stewart and Pattinson.

[No additional information available]

documents.title: The Tree of Life
documents.tagline: Nothing stands still.
documents.overview: The impressionistic story of a Texas family in the 1950s. The film follows the life journey of the eldest son, Jack, through the innocence of childhood to his disillusioned adult years as he tries to reconcile a complicated relationship with his father. Jack finds himself a lost soul in the modern world, seeking answers to the origins and meaning of life while questioning the existence of faith.

documents.title: Boogeyman
documents.tagline: You thought it was just a story.
documents.overview: Every culture has one – the horrible monster fueling young children's nightmares. But for Tim, the Boogeyman still lives in his memories as a creature that devoured his father 16 years earlier. Is the Boogeyman real? Or did Tim make him up to explain why his father abandoned his family?
documents.plot:
During his childhood, Tim Jensen witnesses his father being taken by the Boogeyman, an evil creature which lives in all closets worldwide. Since then, he has taken precautions to ensure that the Boogeyman cannot get to him, such as sleeping on a mattress on the floor, and removing all closets from his home, and keeping all his clothes in a dresser drawer.
After a Thanksgiving trip with his girlfriend Jessica to her parents' house, Tim has a premonition in which his mother tells him to return to the family home. Soon after, he receives a call from his uncle informing him that his mother has died. Upon returning to the psychiatric ward, where he grew up after his father died, he discovers that one of the patients, a young girl, is being terrorized by something hiding in the ceiling of her room.
Upon a suggestion by his psychiatrist that returning to his family home to spend the night in that house would be a good idea, Tim returns to his old Victorian style house in the open country, where he relives memories of his mother telling his father that the Boogeyman does not exist and therefore cannot possibly harm Tim. Tim is briefly attacked by the Boogeyman when he enters the downstairs closet.
Tim meets a young girl named Franny in his woodshed; she wants to know if it's true that the Boogeyman murdered Tim's father. Searching the woodshed, he discovers a file of Missing Person lists and documents left by Franny, and upon flicking through them, he discovers a disturbing collection of missing children who were all taken by the Boogeyman.
Tim panics and attempts to leave, but Jessica abruptly shows up and takes Tim out of the house for a night to a quiet motel, where she is murdered by the Boogeyman, dragging her into the bath.
Tim returns from getting ice and preparing drinks and enters the bathroom, where he finds that Jessica is missing. He realizes what has occurred, and stumbles blindly into a closet, and then walks out into his family home, just as Kate, his childhood friend, has returned to his home and, upon hearing noises from the closets, was about to open the door herself. Tim drags Kate back to the hotel, where they find the empty bath; this time with blood on the side. Kate begins thinking that Tim might've harmed Jessica, but Tim angrily denies it. Frustrated at Tim's refusal to tell her what is really wrong with him, Kate drives them back to her house where Tim spots something in the window. Kate claims that the person Tim saw was in fact her father. She then calls Tim's Uncle Mike to have him check on Tim. But he is captured and taken away by the Boogeyman.
Tim returns to his house and meets Franny once more, who leads him to a house full of proclamations describing the Boogeyman. There is a chair in the middle of the room facing a closet. Tim remembers this house as being the home of a doctor who everyone thought was insane.

documents.title: The Marine
documents.tagline: They took his wife. Now he's coming.
documents.overview: A group of diamond thieves on the run kidnap the wife of a recently discharged marine who goes on a chase through the South Carolinian wilderness to retrieve her.
documents.plot: A group of diamond thieves on the run kidnap the wife of a recently discharged marine who goes on a chase through the South Carolinian wilderness to retrieve her.

documents.title: A Lot Like Love
documents.tagline: There's nothing better than a great romance... to ruin a perfectly good friendship.
documents.overview: On a flight from Los Angeles to New York, Oliver and Emily make a connection, only to decide that they are poorly suited to be together. Over the next seven years, however, they are reunited time and time again, they go from being acquaintances to close friends to ... lovers?

documents.title: Dear Frankie
documents.overview: Nine-year-old Frankie and his single mum Lizzie have been on the move ever since Frankie can remember, most recently arriving in a seaside Scottish town. Wanting to protect her deaf son from the truth that they've run away from his father, Lizzie has invented a story that he is away at sea on the HMS Accra. Every few weeks, Lizzie writes Frankie a make-believe letter from his father, telling of his adventures in exotic lands. As Frankie tracks the ship's progress around the globe, he discovers that it is due to dock in his hometown. With the real HMS Accra arriving in only a fortnight, Lizzie must choose between telling Frankie the truth or finding the perfect stranger to play Frankie's father for just one day...
