documents.title: The Order
documents.tagline: Every soul has its price.
documents.overview: For centuries, a secret Order of priests has existed within the Church. A renegade priest, Father Alex Bernier, is sent to Rome to investigate the mysterious death of one of the Order's most revered members. Following a series of strangely similar killings, Bernier launches an investigation that forces him to confront unimaginable evil.
documents.plot:
The Order, also released as The Sin Eater, is a 2003 supernatural mystery thriller written and directed by Brian Helgeland. It reunites the director with Heath Ledger, Mark Addy and Shannyn Sossamon, whom he had directed in A Knight's Tale (2001), alongside Benno Fürmann and Peter Weller. The story follows a young priest investigating a suspicious death in Rome who uncovers a sin eater, a figure able to absolve sins outside the Church's authority.

Father Alex Bernier, a disillusioned member of the Carolingians, a fictional order devoted to exorcism and fighting demonic forces, learns that the order's head, Father Dominic, has died mysteriously in Rome. Cardinal Driscoll, an influential Vatican figure and candidate for the papacy, sends him to investigate. Before he leaves, he is visited by Mara Williams, an artist he once tried to exorcise, who had attacked him during the rite and been committed to an asylum; she senses he is in danger, and he lets her come along. Examining Dominic's body, Alex recognises marks left by a sin eater. With his fellow Carolingian Thomas Garrett, he secretly buries Dominic, who was excommunicated and denied consecrated ground. Driscoll gives Alex an ancient dagger and a fragment of parchment bearing an Aramaic incantation, which Alex takes to be a means of destroying the sin eater. Seeking answers, Alex and Thomas are led to the mysterious Black Pope of an underground sect, and a riddle from a dying man brings Alex to the sin eater himself, William Eden, at St. Peter's Basilica, while Thomas is hurt by demons. The weary, centuries-old Eden wants Alex to succeed him, but Alex refuses, intending to leave the priesthood for Mara. Eden then fatally wounds Mara, disguising it as a suicide attempt, and Alex eats her sins so she can reach heaven. Thomas discovers that Driscoll is the Black Pope and that the full text reveals the dagger rite transfers the sin eater's power. Too late to warn him, he arrives after Alex has stabbed Eden and inherited the role. Dominic, Eden and Driscoll had all used him. Alex exposes Driscoll, refuses to absolve him when the ruined cardinal attempts suicide, and resolves to grant salvation only to those he judges worthy.

Ledger plays Alex, with Sossamon as Mara, Fürmann as Eden, Addy as Thomas and Weller as Driscoll. 20th Century Fox released it on September 5, 2003. Critics panned it, giving it 10% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Rolling Stone's Peter Travers dismissing it as "The Exorcist warmed over".
production_companies: N1 European Film Produktions GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Dante's Peak
documents.tagline: The pressure is building...
documents.overview: Volcanologist Harry Dalton comes to the sleepy town of Dante's Peak to investigate the recent rumblings of the dormant volcano the burg is named for. Before long, his worst fears are realized when a massive eruption hits, and immediately, Harry, the mayor and the townspeople find themselves fighting for their lives amid a catastrophic nightmare.
documents.plot:
Dante's Peak is a 1997 American disaster film directed by Roger Donaldson and starring Pierce Brosnan, Linda Hamilton, and Jamie Renée Smith.

The movie begins with Dr. Harry Dalton (Pierce Brosnan), a volcanologist who has spent his life studying volcanic eruptions. He is married to Dr. Kate McCord (Linda Hamilton), a geologist, and they have a young daughter named Nicki (Jamie Renée Smith). The family lives in the small town of Dante's Peak, which is located near an active volcano.

As the story unfolds, Harry becomes increasingly obsessed with his work, neglecting his family life. Kate, on the other hand, tries to balance her career and family responsibilities. The couple's relationship begins to fray as they disagree on how to handle their daughter's education and Harry's increasing focus on his research.

Meanwhile, a series of earthquakes strikes the area, causing concern among the townspeople. Harry becomes convinced that the earthquakes are a warning sign for an impending volcanic eruption. He tries to convince Kate and the authorities to evacuate the town, but they are skeptical of his warnings.

As the situation escalates, Harry's predictions become more accurate, and he realizes that the volcano is on the verge of erupting. The family is forced to flee their home as lava flows towards them. In a desperate bid to save his daughter, Harry sets out to rescue Nicki from the town, while Kate stays behind to try and calm down the panicked townspeople.

As the eruption intensifies, Harry's vehicle becomes trapped in the ash-filled streets of Dante's Peak. He is forced to navigate through the treacherous terrain on foot, using his knowledge of volcanology to survive. Meanwhile, Kate tries to evacuate the remaining residents of the town, but many are too scared or too stubborn to leave.

In a heart-wrenching climax, Harry finally reaches Nicki, who has been trapped in her school. He fights off a group of panicked townspeople and makes his way back to his daughter, just as the volcano erupts in a massive explosion. The family is forced to flee on foot, with lava flows closing in behind them.

As they make their way down the mountain, Harry and Kate's relationship is put to the test. They must confront their differences and work together to survive. In the end, they manage to escape the volcano, but not without losing everything they had built in Dante's Peak.

The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal as the family begins to rebuild their lives. Harry has learned the importance of balancing his work and personal life, while Kate has come to appreciate her husband's dedication to his craft. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the face of disaster, love and determination can overcome even the most daunting challenges.

Overall, Dante's Peak is a thrilling disaster movie that explores themes of family, love, and sacrifice. With its stunning visual effects and heart-pumping action sequences, it has become a classic of the genre.

documents.title: Paycheck
documents.tagline: Remember the future.
documents.overview: Michael Jennings is a genius who's hired – and paid handsomely – by high-tech firms to work on highly sensitive projects, after which his short-term memory is erased so he's incapable of breaching security. But at the end of a three-year job, he's told he isn't getting a paycheck and instead receives a mysterious envelope. In it are clues he must piece together to find out why he wasn't paid – and why he's now in hot water.

documents.title: Elizabethtown
documents.tagline: It's a heck of a place to find yourself
documents.overview: Drew Baylor is fired after causing his shoe company to lose hundreds of millions of dollars. To make matters worse, he's also dumped by his girlfriend. On the verge of ending it all, Drew gets a new lease on life when he returns to his family's small Kentucky hometown after his father dies. Along the way, he meets a flight attendant with whom he falls in love.
documents.plot:
Drew Baylor is a shoe designer for Mercury, a global sportswear company. When his latest shoe, meant to be his great life accomplishment, is found to have a flaw, it costs the company $972 million, and Drew is shamed by his boss, Phil, before he is asked to speak to the press—his future unknown and likely finished at Mercury.
Disappointed in his failure, and the subsequent breakup with his fair-weather office girlfriend, Ellen, Drew stacks his expensive clothes and other valuables on the street for scavengers to take, then prepares to end his life. He stops at the last moment to answer a persistent phone caller, who turns out to be his sister, Heather, telling him that his father, Mitch, has died while visiting family in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. When his mother, Hollie, refuses to go because of a long-time dispute between her and the Kentucky Baylors, who are bitter about Hollie and Mitch moving to the West Coast, Drew volunteers to retrieve his father's remains and plans to go through with the suicide upon his return.
On the flight to Kentucky, Drew meets flight attendant Claire, who is managing the almost completely empty 747. To make her shift easier, she strikes up a conversation with Drew and invites him to move up to first-class seating. Depressed about his work failure, he tries to ignore the bubbly, quirky Claire who has nothing to do on the flight except talk to him incessantly about Kentucky and alludes to her boyfriend, "Ben", who is a workaholic. At the end of the trip, Claire gives him a paper with directions, helpful tips, and her phone number to help him get to his destination before they part. Drew dismisses Claire, who seems to be trying to get the last of his attentions as he seeks the airport exit.
Arriving at Elizabethtown, Drew is met by the family. He makes arrangements for cremation at his mother's request, despite the family's objections. While staying at a hotel, where a raucous bachelor party and wedding reception is being held, Drew calls his mother and sister, then his ex, Ellen, as he struggles with boredom and depression. Finally, he calls Claire, who is also alone because Ben is away working, and they talk for hours. She impulsively suggests they meet at sunrise, before she has to depart on a flight to Hawaii. They have a quiet, platonic moment, and then they part ways as she leaves for her trip.
Drew struggles between the family members and his mother's demands regarding burial arrangements. His mother is manically attempting self-improvement to compensate for the loss of her husband. Claire suddenly appears at the hotel, claiming Drew's needs for help outweigh her needs for a tropical vacation. They tour various parts of Kentucky and she helps him at the funeral home, picking out the urn and keeping Drew emotionally on track.
During a post-dinner discussion with the older family, Drew sees the stovetop flame and panics about the cremation. Rushing to the funeral home, he is too late to stop his father's cremation.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo
documents.tagline: Be afraid. Be kind of afraid.
documents.overview: The Mystery Inc. gang have gone their separate ways and have been apart for two years, until they each receive an invitation to Spooky Island. Not knowing that the others have also been invited, they show up and discover an amusement park that affects young visitors in very strange ways.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo is a 2002 American comedy-supernatural mystery film directed by Raja Gosnell and written by Daniel Waters. The movie is based on the popular Hanna-Barbera cartoon series of the same name.

The story begins with Fred Jones (Freddie Prinze Jr.), Daphne Blake (Sarah Michelle Gellar), Velma Dinkley (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy Rogers (Matthew Lillard), and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Neil Fanning) arriving at the Coolsville High School, where they plan to spend their summer vacation. However, upon arrival, they discover that the school is being haunted by a ghost.

The gang decides to solve the mystery of the haunting, which leads them to uncover a sinister plot involving a rival businessman, Emile Mondavarious (Tim Blake Nelson), who seeks to buy out the school's founder, Mr. Coolidge (John Mahoney). As they dig deeper, they discover that Mondavarious is using his wealth and influence to scare people away from the school, in order to drive down its value.

Throughout their investigation, the gang encounters various supernatural entities, including ghosts, monsters, and a mysterious curse. However, as they progress, it becomes clear that these events are being manipulated by Mondavarious's accomplices, who are using special effects and disguises to create the illusion of paranormal activity.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo become increasingly entangled in the plot, often providing comedic relief with their antics. Meanwhile, Velma uses her intelligence and research skills to uncover the truth behind the haunting, while Daphne and Fred work together to gather evidence and expose Mondavarious's scheme.

In the end, the gang discovers that Mondavarious is using a combination of special effects, disguises, and manipulation to create the illusion of paranormal activity. They also learn that he has been trying to buy out the school in order to build a new shopping mall on its site.

With the truth revealed, the gang exposes Mondavarious's scheme, and he is brought to justice. The movie ends with the gang being hailed as heroes for solving the mystery, and they all share a laugh together as Scooby-Doo enjoys his favorite food, Scooby Snacks.

Overall, Scooby-Doo (2002) is a fun and lighthearted take on the classic cartoon series, with plenty of humor, action, and adventure. The movie stays true to the spirit of the original series while also introducing new characters and plot twists to keep things fresh.

documents.title: Cheaper by the Dozen 2
documents.tagline: Same Big Family... Even Bigger Adventure.
documents.overview: Steve Martin and Bonnie Hunt return as heads of the Baker family who, while on vacation, find themselves in competition with a rival family of eight children, headed by Eugene Levy,
documents.plot:
Cheaper by the Dozen 2 is a 2005 American family comedy film directed by Adam Shankman and written by Sam Harper. The movie is a sequel to the 2003 film Cheaper by the Dozen, which was based on the 1997 novel of the same name by Frank B. Gilbreth Jr.

The story begins with Tom Baker (Steve Martin), a successful businessman who has just been promoted to CEO of his company. He is now married to Kate (Nikki Griffin) and they have 12 children together, ranging in age from 1 to 16 years old. The family is known for their chaotic and loving nature.

The movie starts with the family preparing for the annual Baker family reunion, which is being held at a lake house. However, things quickly take a turn when Tom's new job requires him to spend more time away from home, leaving Kate to manage the household and care for the children on her own.

As the story progresses, we see the challenges that Kate faces in managing the household and caring for the children. She struggles to balance work and family life, while also dealing with the constant chaos caused by the 12 kids. Meanwhile, Tom is struggling to adjust to his new role as CEO and is often away from home, leaving Kate to handle everything on her own.

As the reunion approaches, the family comes together to support each other and work through their individual struggles. Along the way, we see glimpses of the children's personalities and quirks, including the eldest son, Charlie (Tom Welling), who is trying to navigate his senior year of high school.

Throughout the movie, there are many comedic moments as the family navigates their challenges and learns to work together. The film also explores themes of love, family, and the importance of supporting one another through thick and thin.

In the end, Tom and Kate come to a realization that they need to find a better balance between work and family life. They make some changes to their routine and learn to communicate more effectively with each other. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with the entire Baker family coming together to support each other and celebrate their love for one another.

Overall, Cheaper by the Dozen 2 is a lighthearted and entertaining film that explores the challenges and joys of family life. With its talented cast and comedic moments, it's a great choice for families looking for a fun and uplifting movie experience.

documents.title: Asterix and the Vikings
documents.overview: Asterix and Obelix have been given a tough mission: Transform the chief's lazy nephew Justforkix into a warrior. When the Vikings abduct him and bring him back to their homeland, Asterix and Obelix must travel to Norway to rescue Justforkix.

documents.title: Ghost Ship
documents.tagline: Sea Evil
documents.overview: After discovering a passenger ship missing since 1962 floating adrift on the Bering Sea, salvagers claim the vessel as their own. Once they begin towing the ghost ship towards harbor, a series of bizarre occurrences happen and the group becomes trapped inside the ship, which they soon learn is inhabited by a demonic creature.
documents.plot:
Ghost Ship is a supernatural horror film released in 2002, directed by Steve Beck and produced by Village Roadshow Pictures.

The story begins with a salvage ship called the "Avalon" that has been missing for over 30 years. The crew of a modern-day salvage ship, led by Captain Peter Cullen (played by Julián Sands), discovers the long-lost Avalon while searching for treasure in the North Sea. As they board the ship, they find it to be remarkably well-preserved and intact, with no signs of decay or damage.

However, as soon as the crew sets foot on the ship, strange things begin to happen. They start experiencing bizarre occurrences, such as hearing eerie whispers, finding cryptic messages scrawled on walls, and encountering ghostly apparitions. It becomes clear that the Avalon is haunted by the spirits of its former crew members.

As the story unfolds, it becomes apparent that the ship was involved in a tragic accident 30 years ago, resulting in the loss of all hands on board. The crew soon discovers that they are not alone on the ship and that the ghosts of the dead sailors are trying to communicate with them.

The main character, Captain Cullen, is initially skeptical of the paranormal activity but eventually becomes convinced that something supernatural is at play. He teams up with a local historian, Dr. Vronsky (played by Jonas Armstrong), who helps him uncover the dark secrets behind the Avalon's disappearance.

As the crew delves deeper into the mystery, they realize that the ship was carrying a cargo of gold and other valuable treasures when it set sail on its ill-fated voyage. The ghosts, however, are not just seeking revenge but also trying to warn the living about the dangers of the sea.

The climax of the film takes place in the ship's engine room, where the crew discovers a hidden logbook belonging to the ship's captain. As they read through the entries, they learn that the captain had made a pact with a mysterious figure to ensure the safe passage of his crew, but at a terrible cost.

In the end, the crew manages to escape the ship, but not without realizing that some secrets are better left unspoken. The film ends with a sense of unease, as the survivors wonder if they have truly escaped the wrath of the Avalon's ghosts or if they will be haunted by their experiences forever.

Overall, Ghost Ship is a tense and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of tragedy, loss, and the supernatural. While it may not be as well-known as some other horror films, it has developed a cult following over the years for its creepy atmosphere and eerie plot twists.

documents.title: The Italian Job
documents.tagline: Get in. Get out. Get even.
documents.overview: Charlie Croker pulled off the crime of a lifetime. The one thing that he didn't plan on was being double-crossed. Along with a drop-dead gorgeous safecracker, Croker and his team take off to re-steal the loot and end up in a pulse-pounding, pedal-to-the-metal chase that careens up, down, above and below the streets of Los Angeles.
documents.plot:
Professional safecracker John Bridger's team has plans to steal $35 million worth of gold bars from a safe in Venice from Italian gangsters who had stolen it weeks earlier. Professional fixer Charlie Croker, computer expert Lyle or "Napster", wheelman Handsome Rob, explosives expert Left Ear, and inside man Steve comprise the team. Although the heist is successful, Steve double-crosses them as they drive towards Austria with the bullion; with another crew, he takes it for himself and kills John. Rob drives the van over the bridge into the water to protect the others, using air tanks from the heist to stay alive. Steve leaves them for dead.
A year later in Philadelphia, Charlie finds Steve, under a new identity, laundering the gold through Ukrainian jeweler Yevhen to finance his lavish lifestyle in Los Angeles. Charlie gathers the team, and also recruits John's daughter Stella, a skilled private safecracker, offering her the chance to avenge her father's death. They stake out Steve's mansion, and Stella, disguised as a cable technician, maps out its interior and determines the location of Steve's safe containing the bullion. Unaware of Stella's identity, Steve asks her out on a date. The plan is to blow the safe while Steve is away on his supposed date, using three heavily modified Mini Coopers to transport the gold out of the mansion. Supplier Skinny Pete gets the explosives and mechanic Wrench modifies the cars.
On Steve's last visit to Yevhen, Yevhen accidentally reveals that he knows about the Venice heist, and Steve shoots him dead to cover his tracks. Mashkov, the leader of a Ukrainian crime family and Yevhen's cousin, traces the gold back to Skinny Pete via Yevhen's ex-employee Vance.
On the night of the planned heist, the crew discovers that Steve's neighbors are having a party, forcing them to abort as the explosives would draw attention. Stella meets Steve anyway, but inadvertently gives away her identity by using her dad's catchphrase. The team arrives to protect her, and Steve taunts them as he says he still has the upper hand.
Aware that Charlie intends to steal it back, Steve decides to move the gold to Mexico City. His plan, which involves transporting the gold via armored car from his L.A. home to a private plane at LAX, is overheard by Napster using a phone tap. Charlie and his gang make a new plan to steal the gold en route to the airport by hijacking the city's traffic control system to force the armored car to a planned spot where they will execute the heist.
On the day, they are surprised when three armored trucks leave Steve's mansion, but Napster determines which one carries the bullion and manipulates the traffic accordingly. As Steve is monitoring the transport by helicopter, they maneuver the truck to the target spot and detonate explosives to drop the part of the road with the truck into the subway tunnel below. Opening the truck, they find the gold in a different safe from the one Stella saw earlier.

documents.title: She's the Man
documents.tagline: If you wanna chase your dream, sometimes you gotta break the rules.
documents.overview: Viola Hastings is in a real jam. Complications threaten her scheme to pose as her twin brother, Sebastian, and take his place at a new boarding school. She falls in love with her handsome roommate, Duke, who loves beautiful Olivia, who has fallen for Sebastian! As if that were not enough, Viola's twin returns from London ahead of schedule but has no idea that his sister has already replaced him on campus.
documents.plot:
She's the Man is a 2006 romantic comedy film directed by Andy Fickman and produced by DreamWorks Pictures. The movie is loosely based on Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

The story follows Viola Johnson (played by Amanda Bynes), a high school student who enrolls in an all-boys boarding school, Illyria Prep, after her twin sister Olivia (also played by Amanda Bynes) is cut from the school soccer team. Viola disguises herself as her brother Sebastian and assumes his identity to play on the boys' soccer team.

Initially, Viola struggles to navigate her new life at Illyria Prep, where she befriends Duke (played by Channing Tatum), a charming and popular student who becomes her confidant. As Viola tries to balance her secret identity with her growing feelings for Duke, she also catches the eye of Olivia's ex-boyfriend, Duncan (played by Vinnie Jones).

As the story unfolds, Viola finds herself entangled in a complicated web of relationships and misunderstandings. She falls for Duke, but he is unaware that she is actually his sister. Meanwhile, Olivia tries to win back her ex-boyfriend, causing tension between the two sisters.

Throughout the movie, Viola's disguise leads to various comedic situations, including her attempts to navigate male-dominated spaces and her struggles with her own identity. As she navigates her relationships and personal growth, Viola learns valuable lessons about love, friendship, and self-acceptance.

In the end, Viola's true identity is revealed, but not before she has formed strong bonds with Duke and the rest of the Illyria Prep community. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of acceptance and understanding between Viola and her sister Olivia, as well as a romantic gesture from Duke towards Viola.

Overall, She's the Man is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery in a humorous and relatable way.

documents.title: Flyboys
documents.tagline: Inspired by a true story
documents.overview: The adventures of the Lafayette Escadrille, young Americans who volunteered for the French military before the U.S. entered World War I, and became the country's first fighter pilots.
documents.plot:
In 1916, a group of Americans arrive in France to serve in the French Air Service, L'Aéronautique militaire, in World War I. They are placed under the command of Captain Georges Thenault, with veteran flying ace Reed Cassidy as their mentor.
Pilot Blaine Rawlings runs out of fuel on a practice flight and crashes. He meets a young woman named Lucienne and the two develop a relationship. During their first mission – escorting bombers to attack a German ammunition depot in Jametz – they are ambushed by German warplanes, and two of the rookies are killed. A third makes an emergency landing but is killed on the ground by "the Black Falcon" – a German pilot flying a black aircraft. The chivalrous German pilot Franz Wolferd shakes his head in disapproval.
In a later battle, Rawlings' machine gun jams while he is chasing Wolferd. Wolferd flies alongside and salutes before banking away. Higgins is killed in the battle, and Jensen suffers an emotional breakdown and is unable to fly again. The French military learns that Beagle fabricated personal information and accused him of being a spy. He admits to a crime he committed in the United States, and is allowed to stay on. The American pilots intercept Germans warplanes attacking a column of civilians. Rawlings kills Wolferd when he attacks another American pilot. Beagle is brought down in no man's land, and is trapped by the wreckage. Rawlings lands and attempts to free him with help from French soldiers but is forced to amputate Beagle's hand. Learning that German forces have entered Lucienne's village, Rawlings attempts to rescue her in a stolen plane. Lucienne is wounded during their escape, and Rawlings is awarded the Croix de Guerre for bravery by his grateful commander.
Porter is killed attacking a German Zeppelin and Cassidy, mortally wounded by the Black Falcon, flies into the zeppelin, destroying it. Rawlings reunites with Lucienne, is promotoed to Squadron Leader, and his plane is presented with an eagle, which had been Cassidy's insignia. Escorting another bombing run on the Jametz ammunition depot, Lowry's plane catches fire and he shoots himself. Rawlings fights through several enemy planes, shooting them down until only the Black Falcon remains. After a long dogfight, the wounded Rawlings comes alongside and shoots the Black Falcon dead with his pistol.
Jensen returns to Nebraska to a hero's welcome at the end of the war. Skinner enlists in the US Army but is kept from flying due to his race; he later joins the Airmail Service. Beagle marries an Italian woman and starts a flying circus. Rawlings tries to find Lucienne in Paris but returns to Texas alone, becomes a rancher, and never flies again.

documents.title: The Jacket
documents.tagline: Terror has a new name.
documents.overview: A military veteran goes on a journey into the future, where he can foresee his death and is left with questions that could save his life and those he loves.
documents.plot:
The Jacket is a 2005 American science fiction psychological thriller film directed by John Maybury and starring Adrien Brody, Keira Knightley, Kris Kristofferson and Jennifer Jason Leigh. Partly based on Jack London's 1915 novel The Star Rover, published in Britain as The Jacket, it was written by Massy Tadjedin from a story by Tom Bleecker and Marc Rocco, with music by Brian Eno and cinematography by Peter Deming.

Gulf War veteran Jack Starks survives a seemingly fatal bullet wound to the head and returns to Vermont in 1992 suffering from bouts of amnesia. On a roadside he helps a young girl, Jackie, and her alcoholic mother start their broken-down truck, giving Jackie his dog tags. Soon afterward he accepts a ride from a stranger, and the car is stopped by a policeman; Starks is later found by the road beside the officer's body. Unable to remember clearly, he is found not guilty by reason of insanity and committed to a mental institution, where the harsh Dr. Thomas Becker and the kinder Dr. Beth Lorenson oversee his care. Becker subjects him to an unauthorized treatment: he is drugged, bound in a straitjacket and shut inside a morgue drawer.

In this state Starks finds himself transported fifteen years into the future, where he meets an adult Jackie working at a diner. She takes him in for the night, but when he finds his own dog tags in her apartment, she tells him that Jack Starks died on New Year's Day 1993. On later journeys he gains her trust, and together they try to change his fate. Lorenson, meanwhile, risks her career to treat a friend's troubled son. Convinced at last by Starks's knowledge of the future, Lorenson takes him on January 1, 1993, to the home of Jackie and her mother, where he leaves a letter warning the mother that she will die after falling asleep with a lit cigarette, leaving Jackie orphaned. Back at the hospital, Starks slips on ice and hits his head, and bleeding badly, he persuades sympathetic staff to put him in the jacket once more. In 2007 he finds that his letter has transformed Jackie's life: she is now a cheerful nurse, and as she drives him to her hospital, her mother, alive and well, telephones.

The Jacket premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival and was released by Warner Independent Pictures on March 4, 2005, grossing $21.1 million on a $28.5 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, which called it creepy style over substance.

documents.title: Ringu 2
documents.overview: While investigating the horrifying death of her boyfriend, Mai Takano learns about a videotape haunted by the spirit of a disturbing girl named Sadako, which kills anyone who watches it exactly one week later. When her boyfriend’s son, Yoichi, starts to develop the same psychic abilities as Sadako, Takano must find a way to keep the boy and herself from becoming the next victims.

documents.title: Ringu 0
documents.original_title: リング０　バースデイ
documents.tagline: Discover the secret...
documents.overview: Taking place thirty years before the events of Ringu, Ringu 0 provides the shocking background story of how the girl on the video became a deadly, vengeful spirit.
documents.plot:
In the present, a girl confesses to her friend that she watched the cursed videotape. She also recounts having nightmares, including seeing Sadako's murder by Dr. Ikuma.
30 years prior, Miyaji, the fiancé of a fellow reporter who was killed during Shizuko's infamous ESP demonstration, interviews Shizuko's daughter Sadako's former elementary school teacher Sudo, about Sadako's nensha powers. Sudo recounts how Sadako was withdrawn as a child and predicted her classmates drowning in the ocean during a field trip. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Sadako joins an acting troupe as an understudy. Her natural charisma infuriates the lead actress, Aiko, whose relationship with the troupe director, Shigemori, sours due to the latter's newfound favor for Sadako. Aiko is later found dead, having been haunted by a figure in white, so Sadako takes her place. Sadako and troupe sound director Hiroshi Toyama are attracted to each other, much to the disappointment of costume designer Etsuko Tachihara, who harbours feelings for Toyama. While praised by Shigemori and Toyama, the other troupe members grow to distrust and fear Sadako, as they suspect that she is the one who caused Aiko's death and other supernatural occurrences, including an apparition of a girl in white with long hair similar to Sadako's.
Miyaji is told by Sudo that Shizuko descended into madness before her suicide, ever since moving to live with Dr. Heihachiro Ikuma, and that Sudo heard strange childlike noises in the attic. Etsuko, wanting to discover Sadako's origins, contacts Sadako's psychiatrist, but he refuses to answer and throws away Sadako's troupe's poster; the poster is taken by Miyaji's assistant, allowing him and Miyaji to locate Sadako in the troupe. When they start photographing her, she telekinetically breaks the camera; the two discover that all the photographs contain ghostly faces and a girl with long hair, confirming Miyaji's suspicion of "two" Sadakos. Shigemori, obsessed with Sadako, says he will kill her first if she tries to kill him, and proceeds to strangle her. Toyama interrupts, and Shigemori is killed through a blow that also wounds Toyama. Sadako heals him just by touching him; later, she helps a disabled man regain his ability to walk. After finishing their last play, the two confess their love and promise to leave the troupe and live together.
The play is a disaster as Sadako, influenced by recordings of her mother's demonstration played by Etsuko, sees visions of her mother during the demonstration and kills her psychiatrist. The troupe members, discovering Shigemori's body, corner her and beat her to death. Pursuing the "second" Sadako, they visit Ikuma at his home, who tells them that Sadako split into two beings resembling each of her parents; the malevolent one, who resembles her unknown father, is kept from growing by Ikuma in the attic. Before they can kill it, both Sadakos merge and escape with Toyama.

documents.title: Gone in Sixty Seconds
documents.tagline: Ice Cold, Hot Wired.
documents.overview: Upon learning that he has to come out of retirement to steal 50 cars in one night to save his brother Kip's life, former car thief Randall "Memphis" Raines enlists help from a few "boost happy" pals to accomplish a seemingly impossible feat. From countless car chases to relentless cops, the high-octane excitement builds as Randall swerves around more than a few roadblocks to keep Kip alive.
documents.plot:
Gone in Sixty Seconds is a 2000 American action heist film directed by Dominic Sena and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer Films. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, Angelina Jolie, and Robert Duvall.

The story begins with Randall "Memphis" Raines (Nicolas Cage), a former car thief who has retired from the business after a stint in prison. Memphis is haunted by his past and struggles to connect with his estranged daughter, Sara (Amber Valletta). He's also being pursued by a ruthless crime lord named Earl (Christopher Eccleston).

One day, Memphis receives an offer from a wealthy collector, Julian (Robert Duvall), who wants him to steal 50 high-performance cars within 60 days. The catch is that the cars are all highly valuable and extremely difficult to steal. Memphis agrees to take on the challenge, but only if he can do it with his old crew.

Memphis reunites with his former partner, Bobby (Angus Macfadyen), and together they assemble a team of skilled thieves, including Sara's boyfriend, Ben (Benjamin Bratt). The team includes a mechanic, a safe-cracker, and an expert in car customization. As the deadline approaches, tensions rise within the group, and Memphis must navigate his complicated relationships with his crew members.

As the heist unfolds, Memphis and his team face numerous obstacles, including rival thieves, corrupt police officers, and treacherous terrain. The stakes are raised when Memphis discovers that one of the cars is a rare 1967 Shelby Cobra, which holds sentimental value for him.

Throughout the film, Nicolas Cage delivers an energetic performance as the charismatic but troubled Memphis. His character's backstory is gradually revealed through flashbacks, showcasing his rise to fame as a car thief and his subsequent fall from grace.

The movie's climax features an intense car chase sequence, where Memphis and his team must outrun their pursuers while navigating the streets of Los Angeles. The film concludes with a dramatic showdown between Memphis and Earl, which ultimately leads to the redemption of Memphis' character.

Overall, Gone in Sixty Seconds is an action-packed thrill ride with a talented cast and impressive car stunts. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following over the years, thanks to its memorable characters, witty dialogue, and high-octane action sequences.

documents.title: Pulse
documents.tagline: You are now infected.
documents.overview: When their computer hacker friend accidentally channels a mysterious wireless signal, a group of co-eds rally to stop a terrifying evil from taking over the world.
documents.plot:
When Josh Ockmann enters a dark university library hoping to find a man named Douglas Ziegler, he is attacked by a humanoid spirit that sucks the life force out of him. Some days later, Josh's girlfriend, Mattie Webber, visits his apartment, seeing evidence that it has not been well kept. Josh tells Mattie to wait in the kitchen while he walks off. While waiting, she finds Josh's pet cat locked in a closet and dying from severe malnutrition. But when she rushes to tell him, she finds that he has committed suicide by hanging himself with an Internet cable.
Mattie and her friends begin to receive online messages from Josh asking for help but assume that Josh's computer is still on and that a virus is creating the messages. Mattie learns that Josh's computer has been sold to Dex McCarthy, who finds several strange videos on the computer. Mattie receives a package that Josh mailed two days before his death. Inside are rolls of red tape and a message telling her that the tape keeps "them" out, although he does not know why. Later, Dex visits Mattie and shows her video messages that Josh was sending to Ziegler. Josh had hacked Ziegler's computer system and then distributed a virus. This virus had unlocked a portal that connected the realm of the living to the realm of the dead. Josh believed he had coded a counter to the virus and wanted to meet Ziegler at the library. Josh's counter-program is found on a memory stick taped inside the PC case with red tape.
Dex and Mattie visit Ziegler and find his room plastered in red tape. They believe that the red tape keeps the spirits out. Ziegler tells them of a project he worked on where he found "frequencies no one knew existed". Opening these frequencies somehow allowed the spirits to travel to the world of the living. Ziegler also tells them that these spirits "take away your will to live" and where to find the main server infected with the virus.
Dex and Mattie find the server and upload Josh's fix, causing the system to crash and the spirits to vanish. Moments later, the system reboots and the spirits return, leaving Mattie and Dex with no option but to flee the city by car. Over the car radio, Mattie and Dex hear a report from the Army announcing the location of several "safe zones" with no Internet connections, cell phones or televisions. As Dex and Mattie are driving to a safe zone, a voice-over from Mattie is heard saying, "We can never go back. The cities are theirs. Our lives are different now. What was meant to connect us instead connected us to forces that we could have never imagined. The world we knew is gone but the will to live never dies. Not for us and not for them". The film closes by showing various clips of abandoned cities, which include a window of an apartment with Josh looking through it.

documents.title: Keeping Mum
documents.tagline: Some family secrets are best kept...buried.
documents.overview: A pastor preoccupied with writing the perfect sermon fails to realize that his wife is having an affair and his children are up to no good.
documents.plot:
Keeping Mum is a 2005 British black comedy directed by Niall Johnson, who co-wrote the screenplay. Rowan Atkinson stars as a distracted village vicar, with Kristin Scott Thomas as his frustrated wife, Maggie Smith as their new housekeeper and Patrick Swayze as an American golf instructor. Entertainment Film Distributors released it in the United Kingdom on December 2, 2005.

The film opens decades earlier, when a young pregnant woman named Rosie Jones boards a train with a large trunk that begins leaking blood. Inside are the bodies of her unfaithful husband and his lover. Found guilty of manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility, she is committed to an institution for the criminally insane.

Forty-three years later, in the sleepy village of Little Wallop, the Reverend Walter Goodfellow is so absorbed in writing the perfect sermon for an upcoming church convention that he fails to notice his family falling apart. His neglected wife, Gloria, has begun an affair with her lecherous golf instructor, Lance; their teenage daughter, Holly, goes through boyfriends at an alarming rate; and their young son, Petey, is tormented by bullies at school. Into this household comes Grace Hawkins, a sweet, elderly new housekeeper. Grace quietly sets about solving the family's problems in her own lethal way. She disposes of a neighbor's constantly barking dog, and its owner, sabotages the bullies' bicycles and dispatches Lance, hiding the bodies in the vicarage pond. She also gently helps Walter reconnect with his wife, suggesting he add humor to his sermons and pointing out the romance in the Song of Solomon.

As harmony seems to return, Walter leaves for his convention. Gloria and Holly then see a news report about the release of an elderly woman convicted of murder and realize that Grace is Rosie Jones, Gloria's long-lost mother. Gloria insists that you cannot simply kill people who cause you problems, a point on which, Grace admits, she and her doctors never agreed. The women resolve to keep the secret from Walter and Petey. After an interfering parishioner dies of shock during a misunderstanding, Grace slips away from the family. When two workmen inform Walter that the pond must be drained, Gloria smiles tightly and offers them tea, and a final shot reveals their bodies in the pond alongside the others.

Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes' consensus praised its strong cast but found the black comedy uneven, and Metacritic gave it 53 out of 100.

documents.title: Children of Men
documents.tagline: The future's a thing of the past.
documents.overview: In 2027, in a chaotic world in which humans can no longer procreate, a former activist agrees to help transport a miraculously pregnant woman to a sanctuary at sea, where her child's birth may help scientists save the future of humankind.
documents.plot:
In 2027, total human infertility has led to wars and global depression, pushing civilization to the brink of collapse as humanity faces extinction. The UK has transformed into a totalitarian police state in which asylum seekers are arrested and put in camps. Daily life is full of bombings, rationing, decay and propaganda. The populace mourns as they hear the news that the youngest person alive in the world is killed at age eighteen.
Theo Faron, a former activist turned cynical, depressed bureaucrat, is kidnapped by the Fishes, a militant refugee rights group led by Theo's estranged wife, Julian Taylor. The pair separated after their son's death in 2008. Julian offers Theo money to acquire transit papers from his cousin, the Minister of Arts, for a young refugee woman named Kee. Theo visits his cousin inside an elite mini-city within London where the powerful enjoy all the pleasures of the past. Theo obtains joint transit papers from his cousin, then tells Julian that he is willing to escort Kee himself in exchange for more money. Luke, a Fishes member, drives Theo, Kee, Julian, and Miriam (Kee's associate) towards Canterbury, but they are ambushed and Julian is killed. After the rest escape, Luke kills two police officers that stop them.
At a farm safe house, Kee reveals to Theo that she is pregnant, making her the only known pregnant woman in the world. Julian intended to take her to the Human Project, a secret scientific research group in the Azores dedicated to curing humanity's infertility. That night, Theo eavesdrops and learns that Luke and other Fishes orchestrated Julian's death, while also intending to kill Theo and use Kee's baby as their political tool. Theo orchestrates an escape for himself, Kee, and Miriam (revealed to be Kee's midwife) to the secluded hideaway of Jasper Palmer, a bohemian, old friend of Theo.
The group plans to reach the Human Project ship, the Tomorrow, that Julian had scheduled to arrive offshore at Bexhill, a notorious refugee detention centre. Jasper arranges for Syd, an immigration officer to whom Jasper sells cannabis, to smuggle them into Bexhill as refugees, from where they can take a rowboat and rendezvous with the ship. The next day, the Fishes arrive at Jasper's hidden entrance, forcing the group to flee. Jasper stays behind to stall them and is murdered by Luke. At an abandoned school, Syd meets Theo, Kee, and Miriam, and helps them board a bus to the camp where Kee's water breaks; Miriam feigns mental illness as a distraction and is dragged off the bus.
In Bexhill, their contact Marichka, a Romani woman, provides Theo and Kee a room, where Theo helps Kee give birth. The next day, Syd arrives to tell them that fighting has broken out between the military and refugees, and that the Fishes have infiltrated the camp. He reveals that Theo and Kee have a bounty on their heads and attempts to capture them. Marichka and Theo fight off Syd, and the group takes shelter with a kindly, elderly Russian couple.

documents.title: One Missed Call
documents.tagline: Death cannot be put on hold...
documents.overview: People mysteriously start receiving voicemail messages from their future selves, in the form of the sound of them reacting to their own violent deaths, along with the exact date and time of their future death, listed on the message log. The plot thickens as the surviving characters pursue the answers to this mystery which could save their lives.
documents.plot:
While out at a mixer with friends, Yoko Okazaki misses a call on her cell phone, playing a peculiar ringtone different from her usual one, and notices the caller ID says it came from her own number. She and her friend Yumi Nakamura listen to the message left on the phone, dated two days into the future, and hear Yoko's voice say that it's starting to rain, followed by a horrendous scream. Two days later, Yumi gets a call from Yoko and realizes that Yoko is saying the words they heard in the voice mail. Yoko screams as she is violently thrown off an overpass onto a speeding train. Her severed hand is then seen dialing a number. Although authorities assume suicide, her schoolmates recall similar deaths that were preceded by voicemails. Yoko's new boyfriend Kenji Kawai tells Yumi he got a voicemail from himself dated two days later, with a timestamp two minutes from now. As Yumi looks on, Kenji is inexplicably pulled down an elevator shaft. As he bleeds to death on the bottom, a red jawbreaker falls out of his mouth as his phone dials another number by itself.
A nervous Yumi invites her friend Natsumi Konishi to stay with her. Yumi turns both of their cell phones off, but Natsumi still receives a call from her own number and receives a photo instead of a voice mail, showing herself with a shadowy figure behind her. The media picks up on the story and offers Natsumi a chance to be exorcised on live TV. Despite Yumi's protests, Natsumi anxiously agrees.
Yumi meets Hiroshi Yamashita, a detective who has been investigating the curse that also claimed the life of his sister Ritsuko. Yamashita shares that the next victim is called one minute after the previous death, and victims are found with red jawbreakers in their mouths. Their investigation leads them to a hospital which has since changed its building and number. Yumi recognizes a sound she heard before Kenji's death as the spraying of an asthma inhaler. They trace the autopsy records to a girl named Mimiko Mizunuma who died from an asthma attack and whose mother Marie went missing. Ritsuko's journal shows that whenever Mimiko had an attack, her sister Nanako would suffer some injury at the same time. They suspect that Marie had Munchausen syndrome by proxy and harmed her own children for attention.
The night of Natsumi's exorcism goes horribly wrong. Yumi and Yamashita barge into the studio to see the exorcist be violently blown back by an invisible force and Natsumi die after her limbs are contorted at impossible angles, after which a jawbreaker drops out of her mouth, and a cursed voicemail arrives for Yumi. When Yamashita escorts her home and encourages her to stay with her family, she reveals to Yamashita that her mother abused her as a child.
At an orphanage, Yamashita meets Nanako, who will not speak but has a teddy bear that plays the same melody as the ringtone from the calls to the victims. Yumi goes to the abandoned hospital alone and encounters the spirit of Mimiko.

documents.title: Lady in the Water
documents.tagline: Time is running out for a happy ending.
documents.overview: Apartment building superintendent Cleveland Heep rescues what he thinks is a young woman from the pool he maintains. When he discovers that she is actually a character from a bedtime story who is trying to make the journey back to her home, he works with his tenants to protect his new friend from the creatures that are determined to keep her in our world.
documents.plot:
Lady in the Water is a 2006 American fantasy film directed by M. Night Shyamalan. The movie follows the story of Cleveland Heep, a quiet and unassuming apartment dweller who discovers a mysterious pool in his building's basement that seems to be inhabited by a mythical creature known as the "Lady in the Water." As Cleveland delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a complex web of secrets and lies that threaten to upend his mundane life.

At its core, Lady in the Water is a film about the human desire for connection and meaning. The movie explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the search for transcendence in a seemingly ordinary world. Cleveland's encounter with the Lady in the Water serves as a catalyst for him to re-examine his own life and relationships, forcing him to confront the emptiness and disconnection that can accompany modern urban living.

The film also touches on the idea of mythology and its role in shaping our understanding of ourselves and the world around us. The Lady in the Water is a symbol of something greater than oneself, representing a longing for magic, wonder, and connection with the unknown. Through Cleveland's journey, Shyamalan invites the audience to consider the ways in which we often seek to escape or transcend our mundane lives through fantasy, mythology, or other forms of escapism.

Ultimately, Lady in the Water is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges us to confront our own desires, fears, and longings. The movie's themes of connection, meaning, and the search for transcendence continue to resonate with audiences today, making it a rich and rewarding viewing experience.

documents.tagline: The end of an empire...the beginning of a legend.

documents.title: Swordfish
documents.tagline: Log On. Hack In. Go Anywhere. Get Everything.
documents.overview: Rogue agent Gabriel Shear is determined to get his mitts on $9 billion stashed in a secret Drug Enforcement Administration account. He wants the cash to fight terrorism, but lacks the computer skills necessary to hack into the government mainframe. Enter Stanley Jobson, a n'er-do-well encryption expert who can log into anything.
documents.plot:
Swordfish is a 2001 American action thriller film directed by Dominic Sena and starring John Travolta, Hugh Jackman, Halle Berry, and Don Cheadle. The movie follows the story of Gabriel Shear (Halle Berry), an FBI agent who goes undercover to infiltrate a group of hackers known as Swordfish.

The film begins with Gabriel Shear, a skilled hacker and expert in computer systems, being recruited by the FBI to help track down a group of hackers known as Swordfish. The team is led by Stanley Jobson (John Travolta), a charismatic and cunning hacker who has been using his skills for personal gain. Gabriel's mission is to infiltrate Swordfish and gather evidence against them.

As Gabriel gains the trust of the Swordfish team, she begins to uncover their true intentions. She discovers that they are planning to steal sensitive information from various corporations and governments around the world. The team's ultimate goal is to sell this information on the black market, making them a fortune in the process.

Meanwhile, Gabriel also meets Greg Beaumont (Hugh Jackman), a young hacker who becomes her ally within Swordfish. As Gabriel gains more knowledge about the team's plans, she realizes that they are not just ordinary hackers but are actually working for a mysterious figure known as "The Archon" (Don Cheadle).

As the story unfolds, Gabriel finds herself caught in a web of deceit and betrayal. She begins to question her own loyalties and motivations, wondering if she is truly fighting for justice or just playing into The Archon's hands.

In the climax of the movie, Gabriel discovers that The Archon is actually a powerful businessman who has been using Swordfish to further his own interests. With this knowledge, Gabriel must decide whether to continue working with Swordfish or turn against them and bring down The Archon.

The ending of the movie is intense and action-packed as Gabriel confronts The Archon and his henchmen in a thrilling showdown. In the end, Gabriel emerges victorious but not without scars. She has learned a valuable lesson about the dangers of playing with fire and the importance of staying true to her values.

Overall, Swordfish is an engaging and suspenseful thriller that explores the dark side of the internet and the world of hacking. The movie features strong performances from its cast, particularly Halle Berry as Gabriel Shear, who brings depth and nuance to a complex character.

documents.title: Spiral
documents.overview: A young pathologist seeks answers to the mysterious death of a friend and soon comes into contact with the same cursed videotape that caused the death of the friend's wife and son, which is haunted by the curse of Sadako, a relentless spirit.
documents.plot:
Spiral (Japanese: らせん, Hepburn: Rasen) is a 1998 Japanese supernatural horror film directed by George Iida and based on Koji Suzuki's 1995 novel of the same name. It was conceived as the sequel to Hideo Nakata's Ring (1998), and the two films were released in Japan simultaneously as a double feature, in the hope that the popularity of Suzuki's novel and an earlier television adaptation would boost box-office returns. Koichi Sato stars as the pathologist Mitsuo Andō, with Miki Nakatani, Hinako Saeki as Sadako Yamamura, Shingo Tsurumi and Shigemitsu Ogi. It was released in North America as Rasen and in several other territories as The Spiral.

Following the events of Ring, the body of Ryūji Takayama, the former husband of journalist Reiko Asakawa, is examined by his old friend and rival, the pathologist Mitsuo Andō, who is grieving the drowning death of his own young son. During the autopsy Andō finds a cryptic numerical message in Ryūji's body. Soon afterward, Reiko and her son Yōichi are found dead in a car crash, and Andō learns about a cursed videotape that is said to kill anyone who watches it exactly one week later.

With the help of Mai Takano, Ryūji's student and girlfriend, Andō investigates Ryūji's death and the story of Sadako Yamamura, the young woman with psychic powers whose spirit appears to haunt the tape. Scientific analysis suggests that the deaths are caused by a mysterious virus resembling smallpox, and Andō tries to understand why some victims die while others survive. Despondent and believing that his rival's ghost is guiding him, Andō eventually watches the video himself. Strange events multiply around him, and he discovers that the curse is spreading in new ways and that Sadako has a far more ambitious plan than mere revenge, one that offers Andō a temptation connected to his own grief and threatens to change the world.

Spiral was overshadowed by Ring, which became a major hit and spawned an international franchise, and it was poorly received by audiences who expected a conventional ghost story rather than a medical mystery. The continuity of the series was later revised with Ring 2 (1999), which ignored Spiral's events. Retrospective assessments have been more generous: Den of Geek called it neither as poor as its reputation suggests nor a lost gem, while Collider described it as a gonzo sequel that should not be forgotten.

documents.title: The Wicker Man
documents.tagline: Some sacrifices must be made
documents.overview: A sheriff investigating the disappearance of a young girl from a small island discovers there's a larger mystery to solve among the island's secretive, neo-pagan community.
documents.plot:
The Wicker Man is a 2006 folk horror film written and directed by Neil LaBute, a remake and reimagining of the 1973 British film of the same name that also draws very loosely on David Pinner's 1967 novel Ritual. Nicolas Cage stars as police officer Edward Malus. Made for $40 million, it was filmed in British Columbia, Canada, mostly on Bowen Island, in the summer of 2005. Warner Bros. Pictures released the film in the United States and Canada on September 1, 2006.

Edward hears from his former fiancée, Willow Woodward, that her daughter, Rowan, has gone missing, and travels to the island in Puget Sound, off the coast of Washington, home to a community of neo-pagans. They are led by Sister Summersisle, an elderly woman who embodies the goddess they worship and who explains that her ancestors fled persecution in England, only to face it again in the Salem witch trials before settling on the island. The community is mostly female and lives off its honey, whose production has recently declined. The islanders deflect Edward's questions about Rowan. He sees two men carrying a bag that seems to drip blood, digs up a fresh grave that holds only a burned doll and finds Rowan's sweater in the churchyard. At the school, Sister Rose tries to hide the register, in which Rowan's name has been crossed out, and when Edward demands to know how Rowan died, she says "She'll burn to death" before correcting herself to the past tense. Willow then admits that Rowan is Edward's daughter.

On the day of the fertility rite, Edward disguises himself in a bear suit to join the procession and finds Rowan tied to a tree, ready to be burned. He frees her and they flee into the woods, but Rowan leads him straight back to Sister Summersisle. Edward realizes the search was a trap from the start: Willow, Summersisle's daughter, had chosen him as a human sacrifice to restore the honey harvest. The islanders shut him inside a giant wicker man, and Rowan sets it alight. Six months later, Willow and Sister Honey approach two police officers in a Seattle bar and go home with them.

Ellen Burstyn plays Sister Summersisle, with Kate Beahan as Willow, Molly Parker as Sister Rose and Leelee Sobieski as Sister Honey. The film earned a rare F CinemaScore and 15% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and received five Golden Raspberry nominations, though Paul Sarossy's cinematography won a Canadian Society of Cinematographers award. It grossed $38.8 million.
production_companies: Equity Pictures Medienfonds GmbH & Co. KG III

documents.title: My Summer of Love
documents.tagline: The most dangerous thing to want is more.
documents.overview: In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tamsin. To seal their friendship, Mona introduces Tamsin to her born-again Christian brother and helps her spy on her adulterous father. Bound together by their secrets, the two girls see their friendship deepen and enter into dangerous waters.
documents.plot:
In the Yorkshire countryside, Mona is lying in a field when Tamsin passes by on her horse. Tamsin is from a wealthy family and says she has been suspended from boarding school. Mona comes from a working-class family, and her only living relative is her brother Phil. Both girls regard their lives as mundane and unsatisfying.
Mona finds Phil getting rid of all the alcohol in their late mother's former pub, situated below their living quarters. After going to prison for petty theft and violence, Phil has undergone a religious transformation and now uses the pub to host meetings of local Christians. Mona meets her lover, Ricky, for sex in his car, but he breaks up with her afterward. The next day, the girls begin to bond as they spend the day drinking, smoking, and talking about their problems. The next day, Tamsin takes Mona to the house where Tamsin claims her father's mistress lives. Mona smashes a window of Tamsin's father's car, and the girls flee.
Tamsin purchases an engine for Mona's scooter, and they ride to a small river for a swim. Under a waterfall, the girls share a kiss. At Tamsin's house, Mona tries on her dresses. Tamsin tearfully recounts the death of her sister Sadie from anorexia. In the garden, Tamsin plays the cello while Mona dances. Tamsin kisses Mona passionately, and they later have sex, but they are briefly interrupted when Phil comes to the house looking for Mona.
Phil wants Mona to come with him to a local cross-raising ceremony, and Tamsin accompanies her. During the ceremony, Tamsin seems to be attracted to Phil. At Tamsin's house, she and Mona enter her sister Sadie's bedroom, where they find a bag of magic mushrooms. They take the mushrooms and go to a dance hall, where their raucous behaviour disturbs the patrons. They return to the river and declare their eternal love to each other, swearing a suicide pact should they ever be separated.
Phil later comes to Tamsin's house seeking Mona again. Tamsin lets him inside and pretends open up to him for religious guidance, hinting she is sexually interested in him. When Phil tries to inappropriately have sex with her, she laughs and points out he is a fraud. He angrily chokes Tamsin, then releases her and forces Mona to return home with him, locking her in her bedroom. Later, during a meeting of the Christians, she loudly fakes suicide. Phil intervenes, but Mona further mocks his religious beliefs by pretending to be possessed by a devil. Reverting to his old anger, Phil beats Mona and forces the Christians to leave. Mona packs a suitcase and leaves to be with Tamsin.
When she arrives at Tamsin's house, Mona discovers that Tamsin is returning to boarding school. She also finds out that Tamsin lied about her parents, and that her sister Sadie is still alive. Dejected, Mona goes to the river. Tamsin joins her, and dismissively tells her that she shouldn't have been so gullible.

documents.title: Species III
documents.tagline: Beauty is only skin deep
documents.overview: After she delivers her child in an ambulance, alien Eve is killed by a half-breed. Fortunately, Dr. Abbot scoops up the baby alien and escapes. In time, the baby grows into a gorgeous blonde named Sara and begins her quest to find a worthy mate. But Sara is also savage and leaves a trail of deaths in her wake. This carnage makes chemistry student Dean question whether to help her race or not.
documents.plot: After she delivers her child in an ambulance, alien Eve is killed by a half-breed. Fortunately, Dr. Abbot scoops up the baby alien and escapes.
